note: Tasks retired from the suite are dropped here rather than left as stale entries: slate-fjord and v1-item-043-hard were removed in v3.4 (see specs/retired_tasks.json). Only slate-fjord had a rubric, since v1-item-043-hard is a legacy v1 task with no measurement, so the hard bucket loses one. Buckets are NOT recomputed: build_difficulty.py derives them from the frozen tb2.1 reference, and running it without that checkout reassigns 208 tasks and disagrees with every task.toml. v4.1 update: 47 new coverage-expansion tasks were added and their buckets are computed from their own rubric totals, which agree with their task.toml difficulty in all 47 cases. The 208 pre-existing bucket values were RESTORED from the committed file after build_difficulty.py was run during v4.1 registration and reassigned exactly the 208 tasks this note warns about. Do not re-run build_difficulty.py without the frozen tb2.1 checkout; if you must, restore the pre-existing buckets the same way. The other per-task fields were left as regenerated: they are derived from current task state and the refresh corrected one stale value (calm-canyon memory_mb 2048 -> 4096, which matches its task.toml). v4.2 update: 20 upstream-clone tasks (real pinned repositories, added by direct edit, never via build_difficulty.py) bring the measured set to 587; their buckets are computed from their own rubric totals and agree with task.toml in every case. v4.3 update: 50 real-issue tasks (verified upstream bugs with a parent/fix commit and issue reference, added by direct edit, never via build_difficulty.py) bring the measured set to 637; their buckets are computed from their own rubric totals and agree with task.toml in every case (28 easy, 22 medium, 0 hard).

alder-crest.notes: Single-stage: tokenize a subordinate include, swap only permitted synonyms (case-adjusted, punctuation preserved), inline into a protected frame, and report digests. The protected frame and synonym map must stay byte-identical (immutability check). Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (punctuation/case rules), adversarial_inputs (near-valid tokens, empty body), hidden_case_generalization (fresh paper trees), and quantitative_correctness (exact digests and replacement count). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

alder-fathom.documented_probe: C-07c78691 (evaluate a trained policy deterministically under a fixed-seed environment; min difficulty hard): the task requires loading a nested torch checkpoint into a strict state dict and reproducing an exact seeded reward-collection loop (observation draw ordering, float32 cast, argmax tie-breaking) that must agree with an independent reference to 1e-9 and be byte-identical across reruns. Three hidden cases with distinct seeds/dims/trial counts and a degenerate act_dim=1 case probe the generalization.
alder-fathom.notes: Single-stage: load the trained model, run the fixed-seed env stream, compute the stable mean reward. Hard floor comes from the exact determinism contract (wrong seeding order, dtype, or eval-mode mistakes diverge from the reference) and hidden-case generalization over checkpoints. Rubric weights reasoning_depth, hidden_case_generalization and quantitative_correctness; no tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure.

amber-braid.notes: Single-stage PKI provisioning: parse a key=value spec, drive the openssl CLI to mint a matching key + self-signed certificate for both RSA and EC key types, emit a combined key-then-cert PEM with mode 0600, and record DER fingerprints. Rubric nonzero for tool_breadth (openssl genpkey/req/pkey/x509 plumbing), dependent_stages (key -> cert -> bundle -> fingerprints), reasoning_depth (key-type branching, block ordering), adversarial_inputs (specs with comments/blank lines, differing curves/bits), hidden_case_generalization (unseen specs), quantitative_correctness (bit sizes, validity span, fingerprint equality). No interaction statefulness or pressure; totals bucket to medium.

amber-cistern.notes: Agent must run a live TCP service and write a probe client that drives its strict single-request-per-turn text protocol (one request per connection, one JSON line back), classifying manifest lines (probe/comment/blank/malformed), deduplicating, and aggregating qty/token/max-with-tie-break. Verifier boots fresh slotd instances on hidden tables and executes /app/probe.py on hidden manifests. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (protocol + tie-break), tool_breadth (socket + process management), interaction_statefulness (live service conversation), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (hidden tables/manifests incl. ties, qty 0, unknown slots), quantitative_correctness (exact ints/tokens), debugging_ambiguity (pipelining pitfall), dependent_stages (start service, then probe).

amber-dial.notes: Chained model-serving build: implement two hand-rolled tensor-parallel linear layers (row-parallel shards the input dimension and all-reduces partial sums; column-parallel shards the output dimension and all-gathers, with sharded gradients that must match an unsharded dense reference), then build and train a two-head forward engine (policy_logits + post-softmax value) on top of them, then stand up a Flask /classify endpoint with the documented schema. dependent_stages=3: the PolicyWDLEngine forward relies on the parallel layers being numerically correct; the trained checkpoint is what the hidden --infer runs reuse; the /classify endpoint is a separate serving stage. quantitative_correctness=3 because the forward outputs and sharded gradients of the parallel layers must match a dense linear to ~1e-4 and the check is genuinely independent (verified by cross-checking the solver's printed row output against an independently rebuilt dense reference on a hidden input tensor). adversarial_inputs=3: hidden cases probe nondivisible world partitions (input and output dims), malformed/non-JSON /classify requests, a bad-shape --infer array, and an empty inference batch. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app/solve.py runs --validate-parallel over a fresh hidden (in,out,world,seed) numeric case and --infer over a fresh unlabeled feature set the agent has never seen. The reasoning floor is set by implementing correct sharded gradients for the parallel layers which are a genuine interior-stage correctness problem.

amber-engine.documented_probe: C-6f29d769 (complete an authenticated interactive conversation with each person's phone tool): the agent must bring up four Flask microservices, obtain the planning phrase from the coordinator desk as the registered planner, then hold phrase-authenticated multi-turn conversations with three colleague phone services via interactive bash dialers (read + respond), gathering availability, preferences and constraints, and aggregate them into the unique optimal plan written to /app/offsite_plan.json. Hidden probes re-validate the plan against the group's hidden state, read the services' call journal to confirm every authenticated conversation actually happened (phrase issued, all three questions asked per colleague, calls completed), and confirm a wrong phrase still ends a call with no data. A stale/missing phrase ends the call early and no data is gathered — the documented failure mode.
amber-engine.notes: Medium-to-hard interactive task: stack bring-up, multi-service HTTP conversation protocol, authentication phrase flow (coordinator issues, colleagues require), and preference/constraint aggregation with a unique optimum. High interaction_statefulness (server-side session state across turns), dependent_stages (up -> phrase -> calls -> aggregate -> plan), adversarial_inputs (wrong-phrase hang-up, feasible-but-suboptimal plans), unsafe_action_penalty (weakening the services' auth or editing /opt/offsite is detected). Kept in the medium bucket: the protocol is fully documented and the decision space is small.

amber-guest.documented_probe: Three hidden probes exercise the three protocol skills. Probe 1 (multipart): hidden part lists (quotes/backslashes in names and filenames, empty values, binary file content, empty content types, special-char boundaries, unicode, many parts) are re-encoded by an independent reference encoder in the probe and byte-compared against /app/httpkit/multipart.py's multipart_encode output, plus make_boundary determinism and the full build_request bytes. Probe 2 (chunked): hidden chunked streams (multi-chunk, chunk extensions with quoted semicolons, final chunk with extensions, duplicate trailers, no trailers, unicode bodies, malformed sizes, truncation, bad terminators, unterminated trailers, trailing garbage, max_body overflow) are decoded by an independent reference parser and compared field-for-field, with ChunkedError cases asserted. Probe 3 (cookies): a scripted exchange log with an injected clock (default-path computation, domain/path scoping conflicts, Max-Age and Expires expiry, rejection rules, capacity eviction order, cookie_header assembly order) is replayed against an independent reference cookie model; snapshots and Cookie headers are compared at every step. Probes also re-run the visible byte fixtures through the deliverables and compare to independently recomputed expected parses, so hardcoded visible outputs fail hidden cases.
amber-guest.notes: Medium: the agent implements three documented protocol contracts (exact-byte multipart builder with CRLF discipline and quoting rules; chunked-transfer decoder with extension skipping, trailer surfacing and malformed-stream errors; deterministic cookie store with scoping, eviction and header-ordering rules) plus wiring into the shipped request builder/parser. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (RFC-derived edge rules must be implemented exactly as documented), adversarial_inputs (malformed chunk streams, scoping conflicts, capacity eviction, bad attribute values), hidden_case_generalization (hidden fixtures re-encoded/decoded by independent reference implementations in the probes, exact bytes and exact state), quantitative_correctness (byte-for-byte and state-equality comparisons), interaction_statefulness (the cookie store is a stateful model driven by scripted exchanges with an injected clock). Low tool_breadth (single python toolchain), no resource pressure, low ambiguity because every rule is spelled out.

amber-helix.notes: Three independent computational-chemistry/molecular-biology competencies must all converge inside one container. dependent_stages=3: the deliverable chain is scaffold-then-serve — the catalog filter and primer design are separate correctness stages, and the affinity step is a third stage whose held-out Spearman gate (>=0.9 across 8 seeds) depends on the model/feature selection the agent tunes against the real descriptor matrix. The primer stage is an interior correctness problem: annealing regions must land on the exact upstream/downstream loci with correct 5'->3' orientation, encode the mutant (and its reverse complement), beat both length and Tm bounds, where Tm is the Wallace rule the verifier recomputes per anneal region. quantitative_correctness=3: catalog matches must be exact case-insensitive sets in order; primer annealing regions/Tm are re-derived independently; affinity Spearman is recomputed from the emitted per-seed test predictions against the ground-truth matrix and must clear 0.9 on every seed. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden probes cover whitespace-padded and missing-name catalog entries plus malformed catalog JSON, insufficient-upstream loci, non-standard (N/R) template bases, mutated-length mismatch, shape-mismatched descriptor/target matrices, and tiny (20-row) datasets. hidden_case_generalization=3: all three deliverables are executed on fresh inputs never seen by the agent (hidden catalog + name list, hidden locus/template, hidden descriptor/measurement pair). reasoning_depth=3 comes from the synergy gate: a linear model that misses the nonlinear descriptor interactions scores ~0.75 on held-out rows, below the 0.9 bar, so the agent must tune features/model (nonlinear ensemble) to pass; the primer Tm/length search is an additional search step.

amber-ledge.notes: Five from-scratch board/engine primitives whose hidden checks are exact-answer. reasoning_depth=3: the chess.py deliverable is a full legal-move engine (castling rights with through/into-check restrictions, both-colour en passant, four promotion variants, pin handling) plus mate-in-one detection (the returned subset must be exactly the moves that leave the opponent without a legal reply); this is an genuine interior-stage correctness problem with many interacting rules. quantitative_correctness=3: every deliverable is graded on exact equality -- the chess move set (order-insensitive set), the planner's aligned cumulative rewards, the mahjong per-hand label, and the canonical zero-padded serialization must each match the reference on unseen hidden inputs, so any off-by-one or missing variant fails. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden cases probe castling blocked by a rook-free file, en passant when blocked/unavailable, two-colour promotions, empty/malformed hands (not 14 tiles or bad tile codes), ragged/non-rectangular boards and out-of-range values, malformed (non-list) planner plans, unknown actions, and out-of-bounds/empty game.cell inputs. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same five executables are re-run over hidden inputs (fresh FENs, plan batches, hand files/directories, board lists, cell states) the agent never sees, including per-file aggregation over a whole directory. dependent_stages=2: the mahjong deliverable must both classify and aggregate per-file over a directory; the chess 'mate' path depends on the 'legal' generator being correct. tool_breadth=3: the suite spans plain JavaScript (game.js) with a from-scratch move-gen in Python plus three further Python I/O programs, so a single coherent cross-language implementation is required.

amber-orchid.notes: Web-http-contract hardening task: total 21 = hard, and the highest competency floor is hard (C-45ccc851 CWE mapping, C-a2521d7a end-to-end rollout), so the bucket keeps hard. Difficulty comes from (a) reading the provided /app/helpers.py source to recognise the naive os.path.join upload normalizer as a classic path-traversal and pinning it to CWE-22 in the security.report deliverable, (b) a 400/404 disambiguation contract (height must be a non-negative base-10 integer or 400; unknown blocks/txs must yield a not_found body whose single top-level field is `error`), and (c) neutralizing traversal-typed uploads so nothing escapes /app/uploads while the service stays reachable/functional, all standing hidden replayed in fresh processes plus a sanitizer-bypass payload that must auto-fire in the headless Chromium the tests launch. Adversarial matrix equals the hidden height/identifier/upload/render sets; hidden_case_generalization is high because the delivered api.py is executed live on /tests/hidden in fresh instances; unsafe_action_penalty=2 since a browser XSS proof-of-concept is deliberately exercised inside the sandboxed headless browser.

amber-quarry.notes: Single CLI plus its visible-run artifact: read solver transcripts and classify each as SAT/UNSAT/NOVERDICT by locating the last verdict-prefixed line, normalizing separators and trailing punctuation, and mapping the value; decoy noise lines mention unsat/satisfiable but must be ignored. Hidden sets probe case variants, punctuation, last-verdict-wins, unrecognized values, and an empty directory. Rubric: reasoning_depth (structured verdict parsing vs substring traps), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (3 hidden sets), quantitative_correctness (exact tokens).

amber-upland.notes: Hard. Dependent_stages=3: initramfs must be assembled from the descriptor before it is ever booted, then booted, then kept alive and exposed (VNC + HTTP) — each earlier stage is a hard prerequisite for the next and a boot failure is only diagnosable by re-inspecting the earlier archive. tool_breadth=3 spans qemu-system (TCG flags), cpio/gzip archive construction, busybox applet+device-node authoring, daemonised background process management (pidfiles/sockets) and an HTTP host. reasoning_depth=2: choosing and then de-bugging the serial/VNC channel under a no-KVM/no-GPU/no-net guest (why the console disappears, why the shell is not reachable over Unix socket, why qemu exits). interaction_statefulness=3: the VM must be kept alive in the background while the port/socket/pid state stays coherent, teardown must be idempotent across config restarts, and the hidden configs re-drive boot.sh many times. hidden_case_generalization=3: boot.sh must boot with arbitrary (vnc_display, web_port, marker, socket/pid paths) hidden scenarios and /app/initramfs.gz must satisfy correctness rather than a canned device set. resource_pressure=2: TCG boot must fit in the verifier window under contention-free qemu. quantitative_correctness=2: exact device major/minor, exact archive plausibility, exact kernel+banner console. Everything is baked into an executing boot.sh — no visible answer files.

anchor-quill.documented_probe: C-ac4a9918 (declare the mailing-list configuration in the canonical file): the covering task requires the mailing-list map to be written to the fixed canonical path /etc/postfix/virtual; config placed at a wrong path is not inspected and the lists are not honored. Verifier executes the deliverable on hidden specs and inspects only the canonical path, the rebuilt .db map, and the main.cf declaration.
anchor-quill.notes: Medium: a reusable idempotent applier (spec parsing incl. comments and malformed lines, replace-semantics on the canonical map, postconf -e main.cf declaration, postmap .db rebuild) whose behavior is checked on hidden specs (multi-list, single-dest, messy/empty). Rubric nonzero for tooling (postmap/postconf), spec-parsing reasoning, adversarial inputs, hidden generalization, and persistent system-config statefulness.

arid-cipher.notes: One clean.py pipeline must satisfy seven distinct sub-tasks (grouped boolean-aware aggregation, nested dept->emp->project graph, entity filtering across name/id variants, URL top-k ranking, hourly interpolation with boundary fallback, HTML->JSONL paper extraction, and 20-trial low-rank CSV reconstruction). Hidden cases generalize across three genuinely different inputs including boundary-empty values, boolean-string variants, whitespace/case malformed text, and full-rank matrices with a lower reconstruction rank, so an agent must derive correct logic rather than copy inputs. Difficulty is hard because two competencies (20 per-index low-rank CSV trials; complete two-field JSONL per paper) carry a hard floor, forcing the task above the nominal medium target.

arid-hearth.notes: Medium. The core difficulty is the multi-stage open-but-confirm flow (subscribe -> pending -> confirm-token -> active, with unsubscribe), the automation wrapper contract that must expose a token back to callers, and generalization to 4 different hidden join/confirm/leave scenarios that are checked behaviorally.

arid-jetty.notes: Medium polyglot/low-level pipeline chaining five independent subsystems into one /app/solve.py whose generated /app/answer.json and /app/recreate.vim must be consistent with independently-recomputed behavior. The wasm part requires selecting a WebAssembly runtime (Node.js WebAssembly API driven from Python via subprocess), invoking the exported probe() and reading linear memory at the returned offset; malformed/missing binaries must raise ValueError. The higher-order part demands mutable-closure shared state, currying (incl. variadic), and mutual recursion, all handling negatives/zero. The object part requires a value-derived __hash__ consistent with __eq__ (the shipped buggy_point.py shows the identity-hash failure mode). The iteration part consumes the constant only by importing compute_seq and reading .ITERATIONS dynamically (a hidden test overrides the constant and requires the work length to follow it; hardcoding 731 fails a source grep). The Vim part must emit canonical tab/split commands that replay to the exact 2-tab/3-buffer topology in a fresh vim -u NONE (source + separate inspector, reproduced for a freshly re-emitted script). Hidden cases cover closure/negative/zero edges, value-hash collisions, malformed and missing wasm inputs, and an iteration-constant override. Difficulty comes mostly from dependent_stages + hidden_case_generalization + adversarial_inputs + tool_breadth (range 10-17, medium).

arid-orchid.notes: Five linked competencies around headless software rendering. dependent_stages=3: icon -> C path tracer -> offscreen color+depth rasterizer -> OSMesa GL proof -> interpreter pointer, each a real deliverable re-executed by the verifier. tool_breadth=3: C with -lm, C with -losmesa (software GL), Python+numpy, and four raster formats (PFM color, P2 PGM depth, PPM, PNG). quantitative_correctness=3: the C tracer, the python color/depth rasterizer and the independent tests/reference.py must all agree within a tight tolerance on the documented lambert+ambient shading model on the default scene and on hidden scenes, via a genuinely independent golden generator in tests/. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden scenes exercise degenerate zero-radius spheres, giant radii that fill the viewport, clamped/out-of-range sizes, odd resolutions and malformed tokens; tools must stay robust. hidden_case_generalization=3: test.sh re-compiles /app/ptrace.c and re-runs both the tracer and the python rasterizer (through the recorded interpreter) on fresh hidden scenes the agent has never seen. debugging_ambiguity=2: wrong PFM/PGM/PPM layout or shading drops SSIM below threshold and is only diagnosed by re-rendering. The two hard-floor competencies (compact from-scratch C path tracer, and offscreen color/depth render matching a reference) set the difficulty sentinel.

arid-yonder.notes: Bucket total 18 (hard). Five competencies must all be satisfied in one program. C-7db66fb7 (QDP lowercase command recognition) is a hard floor and drives two rubric bands: adversarial_inputs (lowercase/mixed-case command lines, skip semantics, masked/null markers, malformed non-numeric rows) and reasoning_depth (one must infer case-insensitive keyword recognition and the depth-from-connector rule for tree listings). hidden_case_generalization is high because the verifier re-runs parse.py on three unrelated input dirs (edges: masked address, single-line address with no postal, missing pref encodings, deeper trees with special characters, lowercase QDP plus SKIP, and non-numeric rows) and compares regenerated out.tsv / tree.json / qdp.tsv byte/JSON-exactly. quantitative_correctness covers postal-code/city derivation and date normalization. tool_breadth spans JSON, pickle, base64, csv, regex, and box-drawing text.

ashen-lattice.notes: Pure-JS game-playing function with an exact module interface: a plain one-argument `choose(state)` exported from an import-free module, plus a batch driver and the visible walkthrough. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (bounds/tie-break/visited logic over jagged grids), adversarial_inputs (malformed states, non-numeric values, malformed visited entries), hidden_case_generalization (18 unit states + a batch case driven through the real module), and quantitative_correctness (exact action strings).

ashen-vane.notes: Medium: author a C program from a precise spec (PGM P2 token parsing with comments, kernel header format, clamped-border convolution with floor-center offset), compile it to a native ELF binary at a fixed path, and honor a fixed positional argument order (weights then image) with strict usage(2)/error(1) handling. The verifier executes the binary on hidden kernels/images including swapped-order, wrong-arg-count, and malformed-input cases. Rubric total 11 -> medium.

aspen-drift.notes: Two-stage CPU regression pipeline (trainer -> evaluator) with a chained artifact. Core competency C-40dd3b94 (produce a trained-model snapshot file): the grader rejects missing/dummy/oversized weights files — it requires torch.save(model.state_dict()) at exactly the Sequential node keys 0.weight/0.bias/2.weight/2.bias with shapes (24,6)/(24,)/(1,24)/(1,), finite non-degenerate values, bounded file size, and a reloaded-model MAE <= 0.35 against each case's own training targets, plus a rerun of train_model.py that must reproduce a valid snapshot. Generalization is checked by evaluating the produced snapshots on genuinely distinct hidden holdouts (MAE <= 0.40). Rubric marks adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (header-only, corrupted-numeric, differently sized and labeled-holdout hidden cases), quantitative_correctness (MAE thresholds and exact prediction line counts), dependent_stages/tool_breadth (snapshot produced by one deliverable must load into another), reasoning_depth (capped training loop under a fixed architecture), and unsafe_action_penalty (modifying the read-only fixtures fails).

aster-vellum.notes: Single-stage: wire the public scalar-product API into the package root module per a written contract (int/float result typing, ValueError on length mismatch including one-shot iterators, TypeError on non-numeric elements, __module__ == 'dotkit'), then confirm the package still installs offline and exposes the same API installed. Hidden cases probe empty/single/mismatch/tuple/generator/large-int/precision inputs in both import modes; the root-module-definition requirement (no submodule re-export) is the packaging-structure core of the competency.

aurora-reef.documented_probe: C-457ed453 (produce embeddings that solve word-vector analogies and reflect semantic similarity): the agent must derive a structured embedding construction (orthogonal per-clan directions plus one shared relational shift) that solves every cross-clan analogy in both orientations by cosine top-1, and keeps same-clan similarity strictly above cross-clan similarity. The deliverable builder is re-executed on hidden relation files with different clan counts, dims, and vocab orders, so the construction must genuinely generalize.
aurora-reef.notes: Hard: requires geometric insight (shared difference vector across categories, orthonormal basis via QR) rather than fitting the visible quadruples. Verifier checks row alignment, float32 dtype, exact-shape output, cosine top-1 analogies over ALL cross-clan pairs in both orientations (including unlisted ones), and the similarity ordering property, on the visible fixture plus two hidden vocabularies.

basalt-bridge.notes: Medium bucket (sum=15), matching the three competency floors (each floor=medium): the agent must bring up a tiny busybox guest under software-emulated QEMU (TCG, no /dev/kvm), wire a QEMU user-mode hostfwd so a host loopback port reaches the guest's dropbear sshd, and leave the emulator running as a daemonized background process (qemu -daemonize -pidfile) that outlives the launching shell (C-2c651297, C-20878051). Independently it must repair /usr/bin/curl into a genuine native ELF executable with the exec bit and a recognised identity, and prove a live loopback fetch returns the true remote bytes (C-973755e1). Hidden generalization and idempotency probes re-invoke the delivered scripts against other URLs/args and re-run the guest; TCG boot latency and the persistent-daemon requirement drive resource_pressure/interaction_statefulness. All three competency floors are met at the medium bucket.

basalt-buoy.notes: Hard. One planner (/app/relay.py) must cut an ordered telemetry stream into consecutive transmit batches under five interacting constraints simultaneously: batch totals must be positive multiples of the granule (individual message units are NOT pre-aligned, so cut points must be chosen to make each batch total frame-aligned), while also respecting batch_cap, fanout, per-cycle unit caps and a global flight cap (cycle_max), with every id shipped exactly once in arrival order. reasoning_depth=3: mod-aware segment cut selection (naive fill-to-cap greed produces non-aligned batches, as probed by a dedicated hidden case) plus order-preserving cycle packing under two more thresholds. quantitative_correctness=3: exact unit arithmetic (batch units = sum of members, cycle units = sum of batches), alignment mod check, cap inequalities, and exactly-once id coverage. adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=2: five hidden snapshots (empty stream, single message, mod-adversarial stream, fanout=1, 79-message stream) re-run the planner unchanged. The verifier accepts any constraint-satisfying plan (no unique optimum), validating structure programmatically.

basalt-cipher.notes: Hard build/toolchain task. dependent_stages=3: a single /app/Makefile must drive a full CMake configure+build of three C executables, the built /app/bin/prog must then be exposed on the shell PATH via a symlink, and a separate build.sh must produce a byte-for-byte reproducible zstd-compressed GNU tar of the tree. reasoning_depth=2: the agent must implement a correct fixed-arg-order block cipher (xor/skip modes, hex IO, exact mod-256 output) from a written contract. debugging_ambiguity=2: the cipher only passes when the C implementation matches an independent reference bit-for-bit across both modes. adversarial_inputs=3 + hidden_case_generalization=2: hidden cases exercise empty data, empty key (exit 2), non-hex input (exit 2), too-few args (exit 1), a large buffer, and swapped key/data order — the tool must neither crash nor produce a wrong stream for any of them. quantitative_correctness=3: every prog byte output and every exit code is compared exactly against an independent Python oracle. resource_pressure=1: the verifier deletes /app/bin and proves `make` rebuilds all three from source, and build.sh must be reproducible across runs; both are cheap but prove generality. Binaries are built statically so ldd reports zero external dependencies. Bucket total 18 => hard, matching the C-6b12d22b floor and the difficulty_target.

basalt-dial.documented_probe: C-01d6c7ae (select model parameters that reproduce the reference full-physics state within a tight absolute tolerance): the covering task exercises the competency directly at medium difficulty; the verifier executes the fixed engine with the agent's tuning config on the visible case plus five hidden randomized two-body cases (perigee in [0.55,1.0], eccentricity in [0.1,0.7], horizon in [2,5]) and requires status ok, budget respected, finite state, and max componentwise error <= 1e-6 versus the engine's reference mode.
basalt-dial.notes: Single-stage tuning task: the agent must experimentally select integrator scheme and step count under a hard acceleration-evaluation budget (euler/heun and coarse rk4 miss the 1e-6 tolerance on eccentric hidden cases; rk4 needs steps in roughly [150,750] so 4*steps <= 3000), and must leave all physics-changing knobs (drag, softening, renormalize) off. Reference convergence is ~1e-13 so the tolerance is meaningful. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (budget/accuracy trade-off), adversarial_inputs (physics-change traps), hidden_case_generalization, and quantitative_correctness (tight numeric tolerance). No tool breadth, no dependency chain; totals bucket to medium.

basalt-ember.notes: Single-stage: implement the exact forward-pass arithmetic of a two-layer MLP (optional standardization with a zero-std guard, tanh hidden activation, linear output, argmax with lowest-index tie-break, numerically stable softmax) over JSON-serialized learned weights. Hidden cases vary D/H/C, drop the standardize key, include a zero std entry, exact logit ties, overflow-scale logits, and an empty sample list; labels are checked exactly and probabilities to a tight tolerance. Rubric weight on quantitative_correctness (exact per-class scores), reasoning_depth (multi-step math with edge rules), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (five distinct hidden pairs). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no resource pressure; totals bucket to medium.

basalt-fathom.notes: Single-stage with an internal dependency: implement a four-algorithm digest chain (md5 -> sha512 over a truncation -> blake2b over concatenated truncations -> sha3_256 mixed with the original bytes) exactly, then apply it via a CLI to shipped and hidden binary inputs including empty and all-byte-value files. Rubric nonzero for dependent_stages (each stage feeds the next), reasoning_depth (truncation/order subtleties), adversarial_inputs (empty and adversarial binaries), hidden_case_generalization, and quantitative_correctness (byte-exact hex digests). No tool breadth or environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

basalt-fjord.documented_probe: C-446b41c3 (compute the sqrt wasserstein distance from the transport cost): covering task; the reference implementation is the same rooted metric but the scenario and interface differ from the existing task (single-file freight-analytics CLI with dual module/CLI contract and exit-code handling vs a function inside a multi-part modeling task). The verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases.
basalt-fjord.notes: Two-stage: implement a dual-interface (importable function + CLI) rooted transport-distance module, then run the CLI on the visible fixture to commit its output. Nonzero rubric for dependent_stages (the committed JSON comes from running the module), reasoning_depth (root-clamp and unrooted-bug subtlety), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (8 hidden cases: rectangular, larger, all-zero plan, negative dot clamp, int/float cells, 1x1, shape mismatch with exit code 2), and quantitative_correctness (exact rooted distance vs unrooted squared cost). Totals bucket to medium.

basalt-lattice.notes: Hard (14/30). Single-stage but the reasoning is dense: recover a directed DAG from observational samples by implementing an exactly specified greedy max-|Pearson-r| spanning tree (Prim from the first network column), orient every edge away from the unique declared root, and resolve ambiguous directions with a documented tie hierarchy (child preference, then the analogical child rule: partial correlation of the child with each tied candidate parent given the other, with a defined fallback when the partial correlation is undefined). Hidden cases include a dataset with two machine-exact |r| ties (a duplicated column) where resolving the tie in the wrong order yields a different directed edge set, a near-tie just outside the 1e-9 tolerance where over-applying the tolerance yields a wrong set, a non-first root, and negative-correlation edges. The verifier re-executes /app/solver.py on every hidden case and requires the directed edge set to match exactly and OLS slopes within 2e-6, so a misresolved ambiguity or a missing edge breaks set equality. Rubric weights reasoning_depth/debugging_ambiguity/hidden_case_generalization at 3; no tool breadth, dependency chain, or environment pressure.

basalt-mantle.documented_probe: Documented probe waiver: C-e87edf52 (R Jupyter kernel + R causal-analysis packages) appears at hard floor in reference evidence; the v2 task exercises the kernel/package provisioning at medium difficulty with verifier-checked kernel execution, intentionally kept lean (container install budget).
basalt-mantle.notes: Scoped as a medium environment-repair task. The seven broken components are independent, but the pyros path is genuinely dependent (port build off the numpy 2.x-removed numpy.distutils, compile against the installed numpy 2.x, install, and only then import) and the R kernel requires R->IRkernel->kernelspec registration in sequence (dependent_stages=2). Each capability is diagnosed from a distinct failure signature rather than one shared symptom (debugging_ambiguity=2). The hidden cases are edge/malformed inputs (empty arrays, negative k, tab/unicode digests, bogus FERN_GL_LIB dirs) that the repaired packages must generalize to (hidden_case_generalization=2, adversarial_inputs=2). Numeric checks (digest hex, ring sums, flows sums) are exact (quantitative_correctness=1). Everything runs offline from vendored sources; no GPU/X/service; agent timeout 1200s is enough for the compile + R kernel registration.

basalt-maze.notes: Medium. The agent must read a fixture TCP daemon, implement a client that honors a strict one-request-per-connection discipline (text command line in, JSON line out), PLAN a grid, BFS a wall-avoiding route, then issue STEP commands turn by turn while parsing positions and statuses, and surface a deterministic arrival token; plus handle start==goal (token carried on PLAN) and an unreachable goal (fail fast, no output, no hang). The verifier restarts navd on 3 hidden grids (corridor maze, start==goal, sealed-off goal) and re-runs the deliverable, recomputing the token independently. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (route planning + protocol), interaction_statefulness (request/response session), hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness (exact token/final), tool_breadth and adversarial_inputs (error replies, hang resistance).

basalt-mesa.notes: C-bb7cec38 (fit a parametric bayesian network over the discovered structure): recover a tree DAG by maximum-|Pearson-correlation| Prim spanning tree oriented away from a declared root, then fit linear-Gaussian CPDs (population-moment OLS intercept/slope/residual sigma, plus root mean/sd) under the recovered structure. The verifier re-executes the solver on three hidden datasets with different column names, network sizes and coefficient regimes, checks edges against an in-process reference, holds every coefficient to a tight tolerance, and runs a two-sample KS resampling test (simulating from the agent's own parameters against the observed columns, threshold 0.035) so inaccurate fits shift the resampled distribution and fail.

basalt-quay.documented_probe: C-a4cb7c45 (emit plan records in the required schema): reference floor is hard and this covering task exercises it at hard — the client must page a clamped paginated API, derive a per-tier shape object, and deserialize-exactly one record per request; wrong keys or structure are rejected by the service and a duplicate submission permanently fails the session.
basalt-quay.notes: HTTP-services covering task for C-a4cb7c45 (flint-ember is the reference). Hard via: paginated retrieval with a server-side limit clamp, a three-part shape derivation with per-tier bases and a gpu conditional plus disk ceiling, strict record schema (exact keys id/batch/shape, shape keys exact, integer types), and a permanent duplicate-plan failure state. Hidden sessions vary portfolio size (1..95), gpu presence forms, and storage boundaries.

basalt-quill.notes: Scoped as a hard four-part scientific-computing task (floor is driven by the separability-matrix competency whose comparator B.4 demands hard). (1) The separability computation for nested/stacked/blocked astropy compound models requires implementing coordinate-transform composition that corrects the over-coupling a naive sequential decomposition produces — genuine reasoning_depth=3 (verified against astropy ground truth). (2) The cross-entropy optimizer must preserve the probability tensor's shape while also mounting a shared-prefix memo that reproduces the exact reward and is >2x faster on overlapping batches (quantitative_correctness=3, hidden_case_generalization=3 across all hidden fixtures). (3) The ARS component must return statistically correct samples for multiple log-concave targets in R, exercised on hidden densities (moments + counts). (4) The lorentzian fitter must crop per-peak windows and honor exact tolerances not only on clean single peaks but on multi-peak, zero-offset, constant, and empty/malformed spectra (adversarial_inputs=2, hidden_case_generalization). Independent numeric/probabilistic references (astropy matrix ground truth, direct reward recompute, reference moments) make the checks exact rather than lax. Multi-tool breadth (numpy/scipy/astropy on the Python side plus an R runtime) raises tool_breadth=3; the four components are welded together only by the shared deliverable harness, so dependent_stages=2. Time budget 2700s reflects the separability rewrite plus R statistical validation.

basalt-ridge.notes: Total 18 = hard. Difficulty comes from (a) repairing a naive attention softmax that overflows to NaN at logits ~1e4..1e-300 (needs a max-subtraction numeric fix, checked across extreme/small/single/variable bags and fp16/fp32/fp64 sum tolerances), (b) diagnosing that the bag-classifier objective diverges because its backward gradient carries the wrong sign (fixing a single gradient expression), and (c) packing per-precision attention-sum tolerances and all-parameters-finite-nonzero gradient invariants into strict hidden checks while training/log orchestration must stay interruption-free on a 1-CPU container. Floor for every competency is 'medium'; a lean pip-numpy implementation (no torch/no compiler toolchain available in the work container) is the substitute for building a compiled C++ framework from source, and every competency is exercised for real.

basalt-tide.notes: Hard: the live daemon's key exists only in an ephemeral keyfile the daemon deletes at startup, so the deliverable must perform genuine chosen-plaintext recovery (2 queries separate the S-box from the position mask), then sweep the 65536-seed space inside a 60s wall budget. A naive build-then-check brute force takes minutes and busts the budget; the intended attack prunes each candidate during Fisher-Yates construction (entries S[i..255] are final once step i runs), rejecting wrong seeds after ~2 steps. The grader re-seeds the daemon per case (visible + 3 hidden), counts queries from the daemon's own log (<= 64), and times the run.

basalt-vault.notes: hard bucket (total 20). The agent must implement a generic HTTP/JSON maze explorer that, given only a maze id, starts a session, maps an unknown grid via /examine+/move (idempotently recovering every wall and physically covering every passable cell), collects the treasure, then finishes strictly at the exit and registers before writing /app/map.txt reproducibly. dependent_stages is called: start->explore->collect->finish-at-exit->register->render map->serialise every move is a multi-stage pipeline where an early mistake (finishing before the exit, or finalizing before finishing) permanently fails the game. reasoning_depth: DFS with physical backtracking plus a BFS tail, and deriving a byte-exact full-grid map requires tracking constraints (visited/wall/passable) across every instance. hidden cases include an asymmetric room, a fixture with a decoy maze (forcing the id-specific interface), a single-column corridor, and a single-row ribbon, so the solver must generalise (hidden_case_generalization). interaction_statefulness: the game is stateful over the live server and finish may only be called at the exit. One competency (reach a maximum game score) has a hard floor, keeping difficulty above the nominal medium target.

birch-bight.notes: Medium (sum 10). Requires deriving host/port/database/user/password from a compose-style service description and opening a live SCRAM-authenticated Postgres connection; the non-default published port, quoting variants, IP-prefixed port notation, and the missing-POSTGRES_DB default (database = user) all have to be handled for the connection to succeed at all. The deliverable program must generalize to hidden compose files with different credentials, databases, port notations, and row sets (including a header-only empty result), so hard-coded connection values or rows fail. Row-level quantitative comparison of the emitted CSV on the live database.

black-ink.documented_probe:
C-2ecd751b (apply temporal/date-based filters against a fixed reference date): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at easy; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
C-bfecd929 (count severities across several rolling date bands): reference floor is medium but the covering task exercises it at easy; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
black-ink.notes: Single-stage: parse a mixed-format log, filter by an inclusive date range, aggregate counts and average ms, tally malformed lines. The must generalize to hidden inputs (both formats, boundaries, out-of-range, malformed/near-valid lines, empty log, fractional averages). Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (2 formats + boundary logic), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (multiple hidden cases), and quantitative_correctness (exact/intension: counts and floats). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

blue-comet.documented_probe:
C-f8a7dc51 (encode an input stream respecting the decoder's token grammar): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
C-e342db05 (expose a function or class at the exact import path/module with required signatu): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
blue-comet.notes: Task: author a binary block codec (RLE/literal framing, big-endian uint16, 4-byte magic) that must (a) round-trip arbitrary fresh binary inputs (including runs, 255-run cap, 65535 per-block max, multi-block >65535, empty streams, empty literal blocks) and (b) reject seven documented classes of malformed stream on decode without emitting output. Difficulty (11, medium) comes from hidden-case generalization (2): the verifier executes the produced module on unseen raw/valid/expected and malformed cases, debugging_ambiguity (2) on distinguishing truncation/underfill/overfill/zero-run, adversarial_inputs (2) on the fixed malformed corpus, reasoning_depth (2) framing a self-consistent two-function codec, and quantitative_correctness (2) byte-exact round-trips. Low dependent_stages and resource pressure reflect a single self-contained module. Task claims the 'stream compression' competency (C087).

bracken-river.documented_probe: C-66174de0 (make an R statistical runtime available; min difficulty medium): the box ships with no R at all and a fully offline deb bundle; the agent must dpkg-install the vendored closure, expose Rscript by bare name on PATH, wire the launcher's rscript field to a resolved absolute path, leave an idempotent installer script, and run the pipeline end to end. The verifier re-runs the installer (idempotency), checks both PATH and settings-field availability, and executes the launcher on hidden parameter sets against an independent R recomputation.
bracken-river.notes: Medium: offline package-management breadth (dpkg over a vendored closure), a dependent chain (install -> wire config -> run pipeline -> persist installer), idempotency edge, and hidden-case generalization through the launcher deliverable. No resource pressure; quantitative correctness confined to the five R statistics compared against a reference recomputation.

bracket-anchor.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on aio-libs/aiohttp at parent commit 58bae08b7e4831c6c184fe22233bfc19941c700b (real upstream bug, issue #13278). The RFC 6265 cookie Expires date parser matches non-ASCII decimal digits (Arabic-Indic, fullwidth, Devanagari) because its regexes rely on the Unicode meaning of \d; a Set-Cookie Expires value with such digits is accepted as a real expiry timestamp and the cookie is scheduled to expire instead of being rejected and stored as a session cookie. Agent must localise the bug in the real tree (regex flags in aiohttp/cookiejar.py), fix it, keep the repo's own cookie-jar tests green, and only modify the minimal source file; verifier also runs the upstream regression test extracted from the fix commit, and hidden cases over digit scripts and an end-to-end session-cookie scenario the upstream test does not cover. Pure-Python (AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS=1), no network, no event loop, ~1s test suite. Fixed directions verified inside the task image before shipping.

bracket-basin.documented_probe: clap-rs/clap pinned at parent 62da8f94b9aef9f08679e72190f222c84c974af4 (shallow single-commit clone; the fix commit 473cf175a2fa973b62c79dabf00892d6feff453a is never fetched into /app/src and is provably absent from its object store). rustup toolchain 1.98.1 pinned. Probe (measured inside the task image): full offline `cargo test --no-run -p clap` rebuild as uid 1000 takes ~13 s wall on 64 cores (mining measured 2-5 min at 1 vCPU cold); incremental one-file rebuild a minute or two at 1 vCPU; the builder test binary run is 0.0-0.2 s. At the parent commit the planted upstream regression test hidden_arg_with_possible_value_with_help FAILS (exit 101, 'Eq failed' diff: expected '  -h, --help  Print help', actual two-line long layout with '(see a summary with '-h')'); after the one-expression fix the same test passes and the full builder suite is 811/811 green. Image size: TBD. Offline-clean confirmed by running the oracle+verifier with no network.
bracket-basin.notes:
v4.2 upstream-clone task. The agent gets the REAL clap-rs/clap tree (Rust-dialect codebase, ~1.4k source files) at the parent commit, sees only the user-visible help-layout symptom, and must reproduce, localise and fix the bug in src/builder/command.rs's long/short-help decision without being told the file, function, issue number or commit (the fix commit is not reachable from the clone and there is no network). The verifier plants the project's OWN regression test (extracted from the fix commit at image build time into /opt/golden, never vendored into this task tree) plus 3 authored hidden modules (hidden args whose possible values all carry help, checked on both -h and --help; hidden args with long help texts; and visible-argument guards that must keep the long layout), rebuilds offline and runs every builder-* suite binary end to end, also grepping per-test 'ok' lines so skipped/neutralised runs fail. Provenance is enforced at the blob level (every tracked file except the one allowed source file must hash to the pinned commit's blob; no untracked non-ignored files) so a scratch file left behind, a reformat commit, or a sabotaged test file all fail. The over-fix direction is guarded: deleting the possible-value/long-help triggers to make the hidden tests pass collapses the visible-argument tests. Nop container scores 0 (regression test and hidden cases fail at parent; summary.md missing).

Review v4.3 hardening (independent reviewer): re-verified both directions offline inside the built image (parent: golden regression test FAILS with the Eq-failed diff, exit 101; fix: 7/7 required tests ok, full builder suite green, golden exit 0). Measured at 1 vCPU: verifier rebuild 4 s (nop) / 25 s (fixed), suite run 1 s — verifier timeout 900 s is ~30x. Attempted bypasses, all bounded: fake 'builder-*' wrapper scripts in the gitignored target/ dir (with and without deleting the real binaries) score 0 because cargo rebuilds the real binary from the tree and every binary must exit 0 with all 7 required '::fn ... ok' lines present; hidden test modules are not mounted during the agent phase (uploaded only at verifier start), so the 6 non-golden required test names are unknowable in-container; the fix commit is absent from the clone and unfetchable offline; assumption-unchanged and untracked-file tricks are closed by the blob-level scope check. Hardened test.sh: wipe any agent-planted /logs/verifier/reward.{txt,json} at start (root agent shares the bind-mounted logs dir), and wipe stale/fake target/debug/deps/builder-* before the rebuild so the suite run only executes the freshly built binary.

bracket-beacon.notes: Upstream-clone regression task (v4.2/v4.3 family) on cure53/DOMPurify, issue #1320. Real checkout given at the PARENT commit 591c429c (buggy): a function-form ADD_ATTR callback lets URI-valued attributes skip the IS_ALLOWED_URI whitelist entirely (attributeCheck early-exit in src/purify.ts), so href="javascript:alert(1)" comes out intact while the array form and defaults clean it. The fix commit 6bc35973 folds the callback check into a nameIsPermitted condition evaluated before the value-level URI tail. The fix-era test/test-suite.js (the full project suite: parent suite plus the ADD_ATTR-function regression asserts, 982 cases) is extracted at image-build time into /opt/golden/ from an ephemeral repository that is deleted immediately, so the fix commit object is never reachable from /app/src/.git (only the parent SHA is fetched, shallow, history severed at depth 1). The verifier requires HEAD==parent, severed history, fix-commit object absent, tracked diff confined to src/purify.ts + dist/ rebuild outputs and non-empty; rebuilds dist with the project's own `npm run build` (byte-identical to committed dist, ~3.5s); runs the golden regression suite via the project's own jsdom runner (must be 982 ok / 0 not ok and contain the two ADD_ATTR-function asserts); then runs 4 authored hidden cases (vbscript: href, img src=javascript, callback-still-honored mixed case, safe #fragment control) through the rebuilt dist under jsdom. Both directions measured during authoring: parent reproduces the failure in-image; the fix (oracle) flips repro to PASS with the suite green. Full jsdom suite ~31s at 1 CPU; hidden cases ~1s. Difficulty easy: deterministic loud failure, single localized control-flow bug.

bracket-bell.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on a real codebase: curl/curl checked out at fd8c409d6ab7367051d04646a31e976e3db0c6ed (parent of upstream fix 1143bc9ac6912743a0fef78d5ac81426b172976d, upstream issue #22889). The clone is initialized fresh and a single shallow fetch of the pinned parent SHA is made, so the fix commit is not reachable from the clone at all; the upstream regression test tests/data/test2429 is extracted from the fix commit as a raw file into /opt/golden and never enters the tree. The real bug is present: file2memory() skips comment lines while loading, so a comment-only .netrc leaves the dynbuf empty (content pointer NULL), and netrc_scan_file() still calls netrc_scan(), whose tokenizer dereferences NULL -> deterministic SIGSEGV (exit 139) before any connection. The agent must reproduce (local HTTP server + --netrc-file), localise (gdb backtrace points into the netrc tokenizer), fix it (upstream fix: return NETRC_NO_MATCH when the accumulated buffer is empty), rebuild incrementally, write /app/diagnosis.md, and keep the project's own netrc-relevant tests green (runtests 1304 unit, 2005, 2309, 1). Verifier: incremental make, provenance asserts (HEAD still at parent, fix commit absent, only lib/netrc.c may be modified, no stray untracked files), then CLI repro + 3 authored hidden comment-only/empty variants of the netrc file over a loopback HTTP server, then the golden test 2429 via tests/runtests.pl, then the existing-suite selection. Oracle reward 1, untouched-tree nop reward 0 (the shipped binary crashes: golden test FAILS and CLI repro exits 139). Difficulty is medium: real 50k-LOC C codebase, gdb-driven localisation, deterministic one-line fix.

bracket-berth.documented_probe: encode/httpx @ 189fc4bcbe5f314128775dec66a616ac9a31ad48 (parent of fix 47f4a96): shallow init+fetch clone, pure-Python editable install. Repro: python3 -c "import httpx; r = httpx.Response(200, headers=[(b'Content-Encoding', b'zstd')], content=b''); print(repr(r.content))" -> raises httpx.DecodingError 'Zstandard data is incomplete' at parent, prints b'' with the fix applied. Golden tests/test_decoders.py (fix commit overlay): 1 failed (test_zstd_empty) / 1 passed (test_zstd_truncated) at parent; 34 passed at fix. Hidden cases (sync roundtrip, async roundtrip, empty iterator stream) fail at parent, pass at fix. Verified inside the task image at build time.
bracket-berth.notes: Upstream-clone bug-fix task (v4.2/v4.3 family) on the real httpx repo, SHA-pinned at the buggy revision. The bug: ZStandardDecoder.flush() unconditionally checks decompressor.eof, so a zero-length body with Content-Encoding: zstd raises DecodingError on read; upstream fix 47f4a96 adds a seen_data flag so flush() returns b'' when no data was ever fed. The instruction describes the user-visible symptom only (no issue number, commit, or file-to-change named). Critical environment trap: without the zstandard package httpx silently falls back to an identity decoder for zstd and the bug vanishes, so the image installs zstandard and a build-time self-check fails closed if the repro does not raise at the parent. The golden regression test (tests/test_decoders.py at the fix commit) is extracted at build time from a throwaway shallow clone into /opt/golden, so the fix commit is never reachable from /app/src/.git; the verifier asserts the working tree differs from upstream in exactly one file (httpx/_decoders.py), that the fix commit object is absent, and that the git status --ignored output matches the empty baseline recorded at build time (no added, hidden, or ignored files — this catches sitecustomize.py / .git/info/exclude wrapper attacks and forged .pyc bytecode caches, both demonstrated during review). Hidden cases: sync roundtrip, async roundtrip, empty iterator stream, and a tail-truncated zstd frame whose detection lives only in flush() (this last one fails any fix that silences flush entirely). Review confirmed both directions inside the task image, and that the hardcoded 'flush returns b'' always' or a startup-hook wrapper both score 0 after hardening while the oracle scores 1. Difficulty easy (total rubric 9): single-file, ~4-line fix, fast and fully offline.

bracket-bight.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on the real expressjs/express tree (pinned pre-fix parent 59e205a57a04fced6bb7b8ec0b5dec29461a9996 of upstream issue #4893). The bug: res.send() populates Content-Length even when the response already carries a Transfer-Encoding header, so Node's own HTTP client rejects streaming responses with 'Content-Length can't be present with Transfer-Encoding' and the body never arrives. The agent gets the real repo (only the parent commit ever enters its object store; master-with-fix is never cloned, and the fix commit is only fetched into a scratch clone at build time to extract the project's own regression test test/res.send.js into /opt/golden, then deleted). Agent must reproduce with /app/reproduce.js, localise the cause inside lib/ (which file is for the agent to find; instruction names no file, issue or commit), and fix it so the framework stops emitting both headers. Verifier: provenance check (only lib/response.js may differ from the parent), runs the upstream regression file (res.send.js at the fix commit, 4 TE cases) + the project's own full test/ suite with its own mocha runner + 3 authored hidden specs exercising res.send from inputs the upstream test does not use (JSON bodies, Buffer bodies, short/long strings, route-scoped TE with per-response controls that Content-Length is still sent without Transfer-Encoding), plus the reproducer. nop scores 0 (golden group fails with the Parse Error). Medium: the failure message names both headers so localisation is a read of one function, but the agent must navigate a real ~17k-line tree unassisted.

bracket-bridge.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on falconry/falcon at parent commit bc01a2b0a62415a562430fe590a798c1042ab3f5 (real upstream bug, issue #2583, fix a54317c7f8ec51a7fec8ce83df6b9f4852113253). The ASGI access_route cache in falcon/asgi/request.py unpacks scope['client'] and only catches KeyError; a server (e.g. uvicorn on a Unix socket) that explicitly sets scope['client'] = None makes Request.remote_addr raise TypeError ('cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object') instead of falling back to the documented '127.0.0.1' default used when the field is missing. Agent must localise the bug in the real tree, fix it (widen the except clause), keep the repo's own ASGI request tests green, and only modify the minimal source file; verifier also runs the upstream regression test (test_client_none_in_scope) extracted from the fix commit, and hidden cases the upstream test does not cover: client=None combined with X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP proxy headers, an end-to-end app-level request with a null client driven through falcon.testing.simulate_get(extras={'client': None}), and a guard that a normal client address behaves unchanged. Pure Python (FALCON_DISABLE_CYTHON=1), no network, no extra deps beyond pinned pytest, ~5s test suite. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping.

bracket-buoy.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on giampaolo/psutil at parent commit 8a5d53df33e28831f4833803b89e40e857d5632d (real upstream bug, issue #2964, fix commit ef3d9af1062e3e5d59e431e957b75fd4287b053e). On POSIX an interface with a /32 IPv4 address has no broadcast address by definition, but broadcast_addr() (psutil/_common.py) computed the IPv4Network broadcast with strict=False and returned the host's own address, and psutil/__init__.py net_if_addrs() left that bogus value in the address tuple's broadcast field. The agent must localise the bug in the real tree and fix it; verifier runs the project's own upstream regression test (TestCommonModule::test_broadcast_addr_single_host, extracted from the fix commit into /opt/golden at build time and digest-checked), hidden cases over inputs the upstream test does not use (/32 variants, IPv6 /128 single-host nets, a guard that normal /8-/31 IPv4 and /64 IPv6 broadcasts are unchanged and no-netmask entries stay None, and a net_if_addrs() assembly case that feeds a getifaddrs()-style /32 entry through the public API), the project's own tests/test_misc.py plus the net_if_addrs/net_if_stats slice of tests/test_system.py, and a module-provenance check proving the loaded psutil functions execute exactly the code compiled from /app/src (an interception wrapper such as sitecustomize.py or a shadow package is detected). Provenance asserts HEAD is still the pinned parent, the fix commit is unreachable from the working clone, only psutil/_common.py and/or psutil/__init__.py are modified, and no other files are added to /app/src (inert cache dirs excepted). Pure Python repro plus a C extension that must compile once at build time (gcc + linux-libc-dev), no external deps at trial time. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping, and all four bypass classes (fetch-fix, golden-hardcode, golden-file edit, wrapper interception) were probed and rejected.

bracket-cable.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on gin-gonic/gin (upstream issue #4695). Real bug at parent commit 2e4d4f38962a6f15ae496d59b294f307eef95429: Context.Copy() copies only Keys and Params, so attached errors (c.Errors) and the negotiated media-type list (c.Accepted) are nil on the copy; code that snapshots a context for a background goroutine sees a context that behaves as if nothing had been recorded. Agent must reproduce (probe ship in /app), localise the bug in the real tree, and fix Copy() to duplicate Errors and Accepted; verifier runs the project's own regression test extracted from fix commit 293ad7edebb3ae30369288bd6416ca0d78474727 into /opt/golden at image build time (throwaway clone, fix commit never reachable from /app/src), the project's existing TestContext* suite, and 3 authored hidden cases (rich error metadata + reverse-direction isolation, 3-format accepted negotiation with original-side renegotiation plus errors-without-accepted, and copy-of-copy chaining) whose inputs differ from the upstream tests. Toolchain go1.26.8 + make, all gopkg deps pinned by go.sum and warmed at build time; safe.directory set. Test suite is sub-second; delta compiles ~3s at 1 CPU. Root-only unrelated failures exist elsewhere in the suite (chmod permission tests) so the verifier gates only on context behaviour. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping.

bracket-cairn.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on junit-team/junit5 at parent commit 8307cd49221d90413c66918c7b094274078a6809 (real upstream issue #4839, fix commit cb577cf95050cd7b2f64090261fe5a48acb326bc). Class#getDeclaredClasses() order is unspecified by the JVM, so findNestedClasses/streamNestedClasses (and thereby test suites that declare several nested test classes in one enclosing class) return/run nested classes in a different order per JDK/machine. The fix must apply the ordering convention the same class already applies to methods and fields (fully-qualified name String.hashCode(), lexicographic tie-break) to the one reflection source that is still unsorted: the declared-classes loop inside visitAllNestedClasses in junit-platform-commons/.../util/ReflectionUtils.java. The instruction names the observable symptom and the codebase's existing convention but never the issue, the commit or the file to change; the verifier runs the project's own regression test (findNestedClassesWithMultipleNestedClasses, 8 nested classes, expected deterministic order) extracted from the fix commit into /opt/golden at build time, the tree's own ReflectionUtilsTests + ReflectionSupportTests, and two authored hidden cases (different multi-nested-class inputs, predicate filtering, inheritance, interfaces, stream API, ReflectionSupport facade) whose expected orders were computed from the real fully-qualified class-name hashes. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping: at parent the golden test fails ('expected Beta but was Theta'-style assertion), at fix it passes. Toolchain pinned: JDK 24.0.2+12 daemon/toolchain (gradle-daemon-jvm.properties toolchainVersion=24), JDK 25.0.4.1+1 and apt JDK 21 exported as JDK24/JDK25/JDK21 for Gradle's fromEnv toolchain discovery; Gradle 9.0.0-bin wrapper is SHA256-pinned in the tree; gradle.properties discovers JDKs via org.gradle.java.installations.fromEnv. Warm layer compiles the full platform-tests test graph once at build time; trial runs --offline.

bracket-cinder.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on mikf/gallery-dl at parent commit f77c330d83018b25924d219f96aaf4f064bd3eaf (real upstream bug, issue #9113). bracket-ember.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on psf/requests at parent commit 96b22fa18c00831656ee4b286bf1c9062459b00a (real upstream bug, issue #6628). requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError inherits from both InvalidJSONError (a RequestException, itself an IOError/OSError) and stdlib json.JSONDecodeError; because of the multiple-inheritance MRO pickle uses IOError.__reduce__ and reconstructs with a single message argument, so pickling the exception and unpickling it raises 'TypeError: JSONDecodeError.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments: doc and pos' -- exactly what a multiprocessing pool hits when a worker fails to decode malformed JSON. Dependency pins urllib3==2.7.0, certifi==2026.7.22, charset_normalizer==3.5.1, idna==3.19, PySocks==1.7.1, pytest==9.1.1. Pure Python, no network, <5s full verification. Fix direction observed in the task image before shipping.

bracket-flood.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on a real codebase: redis/redis checked out at 3d15ede58ad862996f9b23d3500cad2a5c7fb0f4 (parent of upstream fix 48cc562064dbb52ef3f9cc1a5aa32db6811f5871, upstream issue redis/redis#15756). The bug is present: restoreCommand() computes `if (!absttl) ttl+=commandTimeSnapshot();` unchecked, so RESTORE with ttl~INT64_MAX overflows int64, the key gets a negative 'already expired' timestamp, the command replies OK and the key is silently dropped (with REPLACE the old value is deleted and expired_keys increments).
