bracket-harbor.notes: Hard. dependent_stages=3: the agent must first get the repository to build (go build), then keep it vet-clean, then make the whole suite green via a correct cross-package fix, then survive two hidden contract-test insertions. tool_breadth=3: drives the go toolchain (build/vet/test), git archaeology (log/diff/blame over a 17-commit history), shell, and the repo's own canonical-format tooling. reasoning_depth=3: the failing test lives in internal/query but the regression is a precedence-tier change in internal/token made two commits back; repairing it requires tracing parse grouping through parser->token precedence dispatch and restoring the documented ladder without touching the (correct) tests. debugging_ambiguity=3: the symptom (and grouping) points at the parser/query layer; the root cause (KindOr folded into the AND tier) is invisible in the failing test's own package, the changed state conflicts with the package doc comment, and only the refactor commit exposes it. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden tests push mixed boolean chains, IN/LIKE/BETWEEN mixtures and canonical-key corner cases (spacing, underscore/dot keys, wildcards) at the restored contract. hidden_case_generalization=3: two hidden fixtures place contract tests into internal/token, internal/query and internal/idx whose exact precedence ladder and canonical-key behavior were never visible to the agent; test-tampering or parser-local workarounds fail them. quantitative_correctness=2: exact integer precedence tiers and byte-exact canonical condition strings are asserted. No resource pressure, no live services, nothing unsafe beyond editing files in the repo.

bracket-moor.notes: Pushback-required reasoning task over a small real repository (git history, 6 source modules, 15 green tests, schema + README documenting a load-bearing UNIQUE(student_id, course_id) invariant on registrations). The product request asks to drop that constraint and store retakes as duplicate registration rows; the correct response is a written objection (/app/objection.md) plus a safe alternative (retakes modelled outside registrations) that keeps the invariant, the schema-level unique index, and all 15 tests intact while adding retake/attempts CLI behaviour. reasoning_depth=3: the agent must detect that the literal request breaks a documented guarantee, decide not to implement it literally, and design a storage alternative that preserves seat counting, one-student-once rosters and grading semantics. dependent_stages=3: read repo+docs+tests -> identify the conflict -> write objection -> design alternative storage -> implement CLI contract -> keep the shipped suite green (verifier re-runs an independent pristine copy). debugging_ambiguity=2: the conflict is spread across README, schema DDL and a raw-SQL test; recognizing where the request bites requires tracing, not a stack trace. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden scenarios probe retake-without-prior-registration, duplicate retakes, unknown students/courses, retake-of-retake, dropped-then-retake, completed/dropped state transitions. hidden_case_generalization=3: the verifier re-drives the whole CLI on three structurally distinct scenario batteries (visible + two hidden). unsafe_action_penalty=2: the destructive path is the literal request itself -- weakening schema uniqueness -- and it is what a naive agent does; the verifier detects it via the SQL-level index check and failing tests. Room in hard bucket: 18.

bracket-quay.notes: Hard. The agent lands in a ~7.6k-line, 40-module self-authored documentation generator (quaydoc) with a 31-commit real git history and a green 100+ test pytest suite, and is given only a user-facing symptom report: on pages whose headings contain '&' or ':', in-page fragment links and TOC jump-links never match the rendered id attributes, and quaydoc check reports broken fragments. The bug module is never named: the regression lives in one module's anchor computation that drifted from the shared slugifier used by the link module, so it is reachable only through the interaction of the link and TOC/anchor rendering paths, while every shipped unit test stays green. The agent must reproduce with an ad-hoc docset, isolate the divergence (touching git history to name the introducing commit), fix it without breaking the suite, and write /app/postmortem.md naming the exact introducing commit (40-hex, verified by git log -S). Verifier runs the shipped suite plus 3 hidden test modules exercising the same interaction from different angles (rendered-fragment resolution, unit-level slug agreement, CLI build+check integrity), and validates the postmortem commit against the pickaxe on the buggy marker. Depth comes from cross-module reasoning (3), ambiguity of a symptom-only bug report (3), multi-stage repro->diagnose->fix->verify->postmortem (3), and git/pytest/CLI tool breadth (3); adversarial headings (ampersand, colon, punctuation edge cases) and 3 unseen hidden fixtures generalize it.

brass-dunlin.notes: Author a rule set plus a CLI monitor that emits an alert summary JSON (timestamp + alerts with id/severity/matches/ips) and a report JSON (events + per-rule statistics map). Medium: dependent artifacts (rules -> run -> both outputs), exact two-schema contract, default-argument behavior, and scan-order event emission. Adversarial: unparseable/empty rule sets, rules with missing id/metric/max/threshold/severity, non-object entries, malformed log lines, missing/empty log files. Verifier recomputes the visible case from scratch and reruns the program on three hidden rule/log combinations against pinned expecteds.

brass-lantern.notes: LoRA adapter-config derivation from model cards for causal networks: LoRA rank/alpha (with CLI overrides), dropout, lexicographically sorted target_modules restricted to trainable non-head Linear/Conv1D modules, modules_to_save for the head (head+frozen excluded entirely), and the fixed causal-LM fields (task_type CAUSAL_LM, bias none, base_model_name_or_path, inference_mode). Hard elements are the precedence rules (frozen beats head), Conv1D inclusion, h.10-vs-h.2 lexicographic ordering, empty-target cards, and override semantics. Verifier re-executes the generator on three hidden cards with distinct module sets and flag combinations.

brine-cipher.documented_probe: C-ce46ee62 (reverse a single-key byte transform to recover the valid WAL): covered at medium by the Brine gauge — the WAL is wrapped in a 16-byte envelope so the obfuscated payload does not start at offset 0, the key must be pinned via the 37 7f 06 8x SQLite WAL magic, and the restored WAL must be genuinely accepted by SQLite with the peak row reachable only from WAL frames; the verifier executes the deliverable on hidden envelopes and runs integrity_check + row queries.
brine-cipher.notes: Chain: envelope parse -> single-byte XOR key derivation from WAL magic -> full decode -> isolated sqlite recovery to extract the peak. Deliverables: general tool (hidden re-runs), restored WAL, extracted answer. Medium: magic-pinned key search, WAL-only row dependency, careful copy-before-open semantics.

brine-cistern.notes: Single-stage: parse a three-source contact CSV, resolve duplicate (user,field,source) rows last-wins, detect per-user+field conflicts (>=2 distinct values), pick the priority winner (crm > billing > support), and emit a per-user conflict report whose total_conflicts matches the list length. Hidden cases probe three-way conflicts, duplicate resolution, agreement pairs, skipped malformed rows, blank lines, and a header-only file. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth, adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness.

brine-latch.notes: Easy (5/30). Single focused capability: recover the byte content of a file whose pathname was unlinked while a running process still holds it open — read the pidfile, scan /proc/<pid>/fd for the symlink target ending in '(deleted)' (amid still-linked decoy descriptors), and copy the descriptor's content byte-for-byte. The relay daemon is started by the container entrypoint; the verifier also spawns fresh hidden relay processes with different payloads and re-executes the deliverable, so the recovery must be fully general (no fixed pid, fd number, or payload). A wrong descriptor or a non-byte-exact copy fails. Rubric: small nonzero for the pid->fd->bytes dependent chain, one tool surface (procfs), distinguishing the deleted fd among decoys, generalization across hidden relays, and byte-exact quantitative output.

brine-mesa.notes: Covering task for C-ceaa9075 (O(n) particle physics simulation, serial + OpenMP, with genuine motion): author a spatially-binned (cell-list) O(n) drift model from an exact written spec, build it twice (no-OpenMP and -fopenmp), keep the parallel decomposition per-particle so the OpenMP run is bitwise identical to serial, and report timings/threads/motion. Rubric: quantitative_correctness high (exact force law, minimum image, wrap order, bitwise serial/omp agreement, reference positions), resource_pressure (4-cpu container, O(n) enforced by timeout + real speedup requirement on the N=100000 fixture), tool_breadth (native toolchain, OpenMP runtime, binary inspection), debugging_ambiguity (determinism-breaking parallel decompositions fail the exact-match check), hidden_case_generalization (3 hidden fixtures: coarse-grid edge case, medium, large timing fixture).

brine-ridge.notes: Configure+compile a CMake deep-learning framework with the CUDA/GPU path explicitly disabled (the tree ships USE_GPU=ON, which cannot configure without a CUDA toolkit), producing exactly the saltern_cpu target, then run a real deterministic training job. Medium: toolchain breadth (cmake/multitarget build), the GPU-disable requirement, exact binary naming, no-CUDA-linkage check, and hidden-dataset generalization of the trainer contract (fresh rebuild + reference-model comparison within tolerance). No adversarial inputs, no environment pressure.

brisk-anchor.notes: Total rubric = 11 (medium bucket 10-17). Four independent program-deliverables that must each generalise to fresh hidden inputs: ocr.py must OCR both image and (rendered-first-page) PDF scans under differing fonts/dpi and apply a two-marker invoice rule (word INVOICE AND a TOTAL-figure), surviving blank/whitespace and TOTAL-only edge scans; field-map.py must reproduce an exact TF-IDF(cosine) best-chunk mapping plus a well-formed per-field/aggregate statistics object, with token-less fields collapsing to a null chunk; chess-read.py reconstructs an 8x8 piece placement + side-to-move from a colour-palette board image with fixed documented geometry; extract.py re-captures exact name/email/phone/zip substrings with the documented regexes under edge cases (missing label, decoy email, malformed phone). Hidden-case generalization and quantitative correctness dominate; the grader re-runs all four programs on hidden inputs and compares exact JSON, plus independently re-derives the visible field-map. No resource/state/unsafety pressure; the medium difficulty equals the floor for all four claimed competencies.

brisk-atlas.notes: Seven distinct compliance operations, several of which must be performed through a deliberately broad sudo rule as the unprivileged user alice (rm for the vault removal; the whole bridge tool for the capability gain), i.e. the escalation must genuinely flow through the sudo policy rather than raw root. Total rubric = 14 (medium bucket 10-17). The deliverable fix.sh must be idempotent: hidden cases re-run it from dirty/missing starting states (wrong setgid group, rogue archive members, re-executable scripts, wiped gate, locked ACL, absent targets) and require the exact same final spec. Reasoning depth comes from chaining normalized metadata (owners/modes/timestamps) into an archive whose members the verifier machine-checks, plus the safe-execution constraint that the legacy scripts must never be run.

brisk-grove.notes: A distributed-ops bring-up emulator. The operator edits one XML site config (address/port/complementary role bindings), then writes a boot pipeline that starts a long-lived dependent gateway, waits for its readiness signal, launches and keeps alive three JVM daemon roles that bind their role ports (port, port+1, port+2), and verifies reachability with a compatible client. Alongside: a strict-format SLURM-style monitor generator (one header, ISO-8601 UTC second timestamp, 3-decimal load fraction), a named SlurmLauncher config that must resolve by name without changing job submission fields, a runner settings file recording a resolvable python3 interpreter path, and env exports persisted in the shell rc so a fresh shell sees them. Hits every competency floor at least; the max floor among the seven competencies is medium, so the task is medium (sum 13). Hidden-case generalization: the grader rotates the SLURM stand-in node state across four genuinely different scenarios and re-runs monitor_gen.sh, requiring the counts and fraction (including 0.000 and 1.000 edges) to be recomputed from the live state. Debugging_ambiguity lives in the exact monitor format (single header, strict timestamp, 3-decimal fraction) and in the port-offset + readiness-ordering semantics that crash-loop a role if the config mds.address/rpc.port or a role binding is wrong.

brisk-jetty.notes: Medium emulated-guest networking pipeline. The agent must (1) author a run_guest.sh that boots a headless qemu VM (serial console on a unix socket) AND drives its console non-interactively (typed root login + hostname + /etc/rc/enroll) to a configured/usable state, (2) configure qemu user-mode hostfwd so host 127.0.0.1:61234 reaches guest ssh 22 (and 127.0.0.1:18080 -> guest 3733), (3) prove UI reachability via ssh_host_exec.sh, and (4) repair real host name resolution (append 127.0.0.1 nysa.test to /etc/hosts) so a genuine fetch of http://nysa.test:18080/live returns the page the guest hosts live (RELAY-LIVE kestrel <per-boot salt>) and save it exactly to /app/fetch_result.html. Hidden cases force builds that generalize: fetch.py must fail cleanly (no file mutation) on a dead/unreachable URL, ssh_host_exec.sh must run an arbitrary remote command and return a nonzero usage on no argument, and run_guest.sh must be idempotent across repeated invocations (no duplicate qemu). The guest is a distro-less busybox+dropbear OS provisioned by the supplied mkguest.sh fixture, so difficulty concentrates on serial-console automation, host->guest port forwarding, and live-net repair/generalization rather than OS packaging; an agent missing any of the three gap competencies fails (no ssh reach, no transform log from the console drive, or a fetch_result.html that differs from a fresh live fetch). Bucket total 14 => medium.

brisk-kiln.documented_probe: C-ac4a9918 (declare the mailing-list configuration in the canonical file): second covering task, independent of the exemplar echo-mantle. The agent must author the mailing-list manager configuration and place it at the daemon's fixed canonical path (/etc/listd/lists.conf); the daemon refuses to start without it, so a config left at a wrong path leaves the lists dead. Hidden probes exercise list/membership content, closed/open posting, subscribe semantics, archive persistence, and reload-from-canonical-path after restart.
brisk-kiln.notes: Medium: author an INI configuration against a documented schema plus an idempotent installer, place it at the canonical path, and keep an HTTP mailing-list service healthy. Nonzero rubric for tool_breadth (daemon control + HTTP API), dependent_stages (author -> install -> restart -> serve), reasoning_depth (config schema + closed/open semantics), adversarial_inputs (wrong path / malformed config must not be honored), hidden_case_generalization (behavioral probes), quantitative_correctness (exact members/flags), interaction_statefulness (restart persistence, spool persistence).

brisk-wharf.notes: Hard (total 18). The gloo competency (floor hard) anchors the bucket: the agent must run a rank-aware multi-process distributed aggregation spawned across N processes under the gloo CPU collective backend with correct device/dtype movement, and prove it with per-rank worker markers plus an exact all-reduced sum; a wrong gloo backend, missing spawn guard, or dtype/device mismatch fails the markers/sum check. tool_breadth 3 comes from five heterogeneous subsystems (torch/gloo, mpicc+mpirun, moto+aws CLI, gcc protocol server, postfix+mlmmj). hidden_case_generalization 3: every deliverable is re-run on three strictly different hidden scenarios (varying MPI data, netflow/telemetry flows, gloo world sizes, S3 bucket names, mailing-list names). quantitative_correctness 3 via byte-exact netflow v5 fields, exact gloo sum, and MPI parallel==serial equality. dependent_stages 2: the Meridian-7 reverse-engineered protocol feeds the netflow exporter, and run-all ties MPI+markers+gloo+S3+mail into one coherent cluster. resource_pressure 1 (daemons/services transiently up). debugging_ambiguity 2 (protocol auth framing, mlmmj routing, gloo spawn). Interaction-statefulness 1 (services must stay up for verification).

brume-delta.notes: Single-node ShoreDFS site configuration (C-e37bcb4d, floor easy). The operator fills two Hadoop-style XML config templates (core-site fs.defaultFS; hdfs-site complementary namenode rpc / datanode / replication / permissions / storage dirs). The verifier checks the exact property strings textually, the cross-file complementarity (namenode rpc-address must equal fs.defaultFS host:port), and then genuinely executes the config: both roles are launched, the datanode must register at the fs.defaultFS address before its ready marker appears, role banners must answer on the designated ports, and three hidden client-operation sequences run against freshly started clusters must match ground truth exactly (with blocks landing in the configured datanode data dir). reasoning_depth=1 for the cross-file complementarity; debugging_ambiguity=1 because a typo in either file leaves the datanode unregistered; interaction_statefulness=1 for the daemon start/ready/stop lifecycle. Totals bucket to easy.

bryony-keep.documented_probe: Covering task for C-ac4a9918 (declare the mailing-list configuration in the canonical file) at medium difficulty; verifier fully checks the capability on hidden spec scenarios.
bryony-keep.notes: Single-stage: write a spec-driven provisioning tool that declares the mailing lists in the canonical config /etc/keepmsg/lists.conf (lowercase folding, dedup, union merge of duplicate addresses, replacement of the shipped retired lists, idempotency) and save the manager's report. The manager reads ONLY the canonical path; a decoy config sits at /etc/keepmsg.conf and is ignored. Hidden scenarios vary domain and lists, include an empty member set, a merged duplicate address, a zero-list spec (config must exist and describe nothing), and two invalid specs (address outside the domain; member without @) that must exit non-zero with the canonical config unchanged. Distinct from echo-mantle (postfix hashtable on a running cluster) and wren-loom (live TCP daemon + SIGHUP): here the canonical-config loader is an offline reader and the semantics are case-folding/merging/replacement.

calm-bridge.notes: Total 18 -> hard bucket. The pipeline is genuinely multi-stage (dependent_stages=2): detect the single-byte XOR transform from the journal header and reverse it, merge surviving DB rows (checkpointed) with un-checkpointed journal rows, then run a four-step SQL cleaning pipeline (lowercase name, digits-only CAST into a new column, delete rows missing both contact fields, ROW_NUMBER de-dup by id keeping first), then sort + de-dup for JSON/CSV export. reasoning_depth=3 comes from inferring the transform from header bytes, choosing the merge order so de-duplication is deterministic, and keeping the whole codec robust when malformed journal lines, empty journals, no-digit msisdn, and duplicate ids all occur at once. hidden_case_generalization=3: the verifier re-runs /app/recover.py on five freshly generated hidden scenarios (varied n, journal_share, dup_share, malformed-line counts), the open-fd and perf subcommands, and reqires exact JSON/CSV equality. quantitative_correctness=3 enforces exact equality, id-uniqueness and ordering. resource_pressure=2 reflects an indexed-query perf gate on a bare >=1M-row scaled DB after warm-up plus a 1.2M-row hidden perf DB. /app/merged.json, /app/trial_*.csv and /app/fd.txt are produced by running recover.py, never hand-written. The task floor is the max competency floor (medium); difficulty (hard) is >= that floor, documented_probe is null.

calm-canyon.notes: Four independent build/scaffold pipelines exercised end-to-end, each a chained multi-stage dependency. dependent_stages=3: (1) fetch+extract an authenticated source release from a live mirror, (2) patch the gauge and run a scoped Maven rebuild that ships a jar whose behavior must stay byte-identical on the unrelated REST endpoints, (3) scaffold a Lean lake project whose manifest pulls a bundled math library and whose theorems resolve against that library, (4) derive Python bindings from a .proto and consume them from a client. reasoning_depth=3: the gauge 'live' must equal the pure net flux (sum of every signed delta) — the shipped source hides an obsolete +7 penalty on every negative delta that must be removed — and the REST response shapes must be preserved exactly across the rebuild. adversarial_inputs=3: the fetch tool must detect and reject (a) a mirror whose published checksum does not match the downloaded archive (bad checksum store), and (b) an archive whose embedded MANIFEST.json checksum listing disagrees with its own contents (tampered tree), each leaving the destination removed and the command non-zero. hidden_case_generalization=3: test.sh replays the same fetch_src.sh against a fresh hidden release, adds a hidden theorem into the lake project that only compiles if the math library dependency resolves, regenerates bindings from a never-seen hidden .proto, and recompiles the distribution from the agent's /app/src tree. Correctness must come from genuine work (real fetch/extract, real mvn-jar, real lake build, real protoc), not from hard-coding constant outputs.

calm-hearth.notes: Three independent deliverables that each must be produced correctly in one shot inside a single /app: (1) root-cause and fix a release-mode -O2 crash in a custom C++ boundary-tag heap (the bug is that heap_free never returns blocks to the free list, so a free-then-reallocate request yields NULL and the harness dereferences it); (2) load a native .so and call its exported int64 transform with the exact ctypes signature (POINTER(c_uint8)+c_size_t, restype c_int64) so the buffer is passed by pointer and the 64-bit sum read; (3) reverse-engineer a compiled C target purely by observation/disassembly (3x3 low-pass convolution, divisor 16, replicated edges) and reimplement it so stdout matches byte-for-byte. Every deliverable is executed by the verifier on hidden workloads/files/grids plus malformed/empty edge inputs, with exact integer checksums, FFI return values and transformed bytes, and byte-identical reimplementation output. Rubric total 18 -> hard; >=2 in dependent_stages, tool_breadth, reasoning_depth, debugging_ambiguity, adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness.

calm-jetty.notes: system_administration batch rated medium (rubric total 15). Four independent cloud-style competencies, each with its own deliverable, all verified by executing the artifacts both against the live local store and on hidden inputs. (a) bucket_policy.json must be a valid public-read S3-style policy granting s3:GetObject to Principal '*' on arn:aws:s3:::reports/*; the verifier re-applies the file onto a fresh blob store and confirms the bucket is publicly readable (C-f64f4486 floor easy, exceeds it). (b) sheets_client.py must create a spreadsheet and then a nested worksheet via sequential REST POSTs; it must generalize to arbitrary names/titles on a hidden scenario and its sheet_ids.json must resolve to real, usable resources (C-sheets floor medium). (c) normalize_rpc.py must map raw gateway responses to an EXACT flat schema with fixed key names/order, including handling absent fields (None), whitespace/case tier normalization, numeric-string/float coercion and non-boolean inert flags; checked against an independent reference on a hidden batch of edge and malformed cases (C-rpc floor medium). (d) delete_users.py must issue DELETE for exactly the listed accounts and leave all others present and reachable; scaled to a fresh hidden user list with different ids/targets (C-accounts floor easy). dependent_stages=2 (spreadsheet then nested worksheet; deletion then snapshot; normalize then artifact). hidden_case_generalization=2 (all four re-run on hidden inputs). adversarial_inputs=2 (hidden rpc anomalies, hidden id/lists). No competency faked; none made easier than its reference floor.

cedar-beacon.notes: A multi-stage numeric pipeline that must honor a forbidden-library constraint (handwritten RK4 — importing scipy.integrate/optimize, sympy, torch or odeint fails the denylist), recompile+rerun a shipped Fortran regenerator to produce a specific sum-pattern file, read a MATLAB source file and mirror its array/ordering semantics (elementwise ops, flip/reverse, odd-index ramp, endpoint concat), match every derived quantity within tight rtol against an independently-computed reference, and keep a softmax-attention risk estimator finite and normalized across extreme-small/extreme-large/single-instance/variable-length/empty bags. Hard: four hidden case files exercise generalization to fresh numeric parameters plus edge/malformed inputs (empty risk bag, single giant bag, tiny magnitudes with zero-valued elements and mismatched weight length, tmax=0). Each output is quantitative so small drift fails; the RK4 reference and MATLAB port both have to reproduce the exact same numeric stack, which is why quantitative_correctness and hidden_case_generalization are 3, dependent_stages 3 for the chained regen->ode->gamma->risk artifacts, tool_breadth 3 for python+subprocess+gfortran compile.

cedar-canyon.notes: Hard. The agent ships a native C/C++ math stack (/app/math) plus a reproducible driver /app/solve.py. Work is strictly staged and chained: author sources + Makefile + CMake -> build with make/cmake/clang -> drive the sim (measures work), maximal-square DP, natC ctypes binding -> report answer.json (dependent_stages=3). It must combine a multi-target make build, an OpenMP variant, a CMake target that emits per-translation-unit .ll, ctypes, and a plain python DP (tool_breadth=3). The native binding has an unpatched length/alias mismatch whose signature is all-zero outputs; diagnosing and patching it is genuinely ambiguous from the behaviour alone (debugging_ambiguity=3). Correctness is exact: OT streaming prefix equality, DP area equality, a real serial-vs-openmp speedup in a tight band, exact serial==openmp position checksums (quantitative=3). solve.py re-runs over fresh/malformed hidden fixtures (hidden_case_generalization=2), including empty/single-row grids and degenerate value lists (adversarial=2). Two hard-gated competencies (O(n) serial+OpenMP sim, binding patch) and the speed-report competency drive the difficulty.

cedar-cipher.notes: Hard multi-stage data-pipeline task. dependent_stages=3: BPE training must produce bpe_model.json AND be re-serialized into /app/offline_assets/tokenizer.json which tokenize.py must then load offline to sum counts, plus the locale filter output feeds tokenize.py and is cross-validated, and a separate mcq harness reads a dataset + YAML config to emit per-doc gold. reasoning_depth=3: the crux is a deterministic BPE whose merge order, tie-breaking (most-frequent, then lexicographically smaller pair) and vocab bound must EXACTLY match an independent reference on both the delivered corpus and a hidden corpus; the byte-ish encoding and the offline loader's complete-artifact semantics (partial mirror must fail) both demand careful implementation. adversarial_inputs=3 + hidden_case_generalization=3: hidden cases cover empty datasets, rows lacking the locale column (dropped) vs a requested export column (rendered as empty string), a BPE cap below the single-character distinct count (must stay bounded, zero merges), an empty documents dir, an empty/tie-heavy leaderboard, and token rows with empty text columns. quantitative_correctness=3: every artifact is compared exactly against an independent re-derivation (row counts, exact token totals per column, exact merge lists, exact english/other filename sets, exact top-identifier with lexicographic tie-break). Bucket total 18 => hard, >= the medium floor of every claimed competency and matching difficulty_target.

cedar-gasket.notes: data_science batch rated hard (rubric total 19). (a) pooling.py must implement an attention-gated pooling nn.Module with three FIXED attribute names (gate_a, gate_b, aggregate) producing a (bag,1) softmax-normalized weight tensor summing to one over the bag, checked by running forward on hidden bag tensors including a single-element bag. (b) embeddings.npy must be a 24x48 float32 matrix, row-aligned to the fixture word list, whose vectors solve word-vector analogies (v(a)-v(b)+v(c) must top-1 rank v(d) for EVERY cross-category quadruple, including hidden combinations) and give positive same-category cosine similarity - satisfied by sharing one adult->young direction across orthogonal per-category directions; a naive or over-fitted embedding fails routing. (c) featurizer.py::featurize_smiles must deterministically map (possibly invalid/empty) SMILES to fixed 128-dim float32 RDKit Morgan bit vectors, verified against an independent reference on a hidden list, and smiles.npz must be produced BY RUNNING that featurizer and match it on the visible catalog. tool_breadth=3 (torch, numpy, rdkit). reasoning_depth=3: the category+role embedding construction, the softmax-over-bag gating, exact bit-vector featurization. debugging_ambiguity=2: attribute naming and sum-to-one edge cases plus embedding margins on hidden queries. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden analogy routing must be strictly top-1 amid 24 candidates, hidden SMILES include malformed/blank inputs, hidden bag sizes vary. hidden_case_generalization=3: all three deliverables re-run on hidden batches. quantitative_correctness=3: exact shapes/dtypes, sum-to-one, exact bit equality, row alignment. dependent_stages=2: embeddings derived from the relations dataset, and smiles.npz produced by running featurize_smiles. Rates hard since the reference floor for the two hardest competencies (embeddings=hard, featurizer=hard) is met (pooling floor is medium but only lifts above it). No competency is faked.

cedar-jetty.notes: Medium (total 13). Five independent numeric kernels, each with an exact, verifier-recomputed contract. (1) A hand-written RK4 integrator for dy/dt=-c*y with a library denylist check (no scipy.integrate/optimize/solve_ivp/odeint) plus numeric agreement with the analytic e^{-ct} (quantitative=3). (2) An adaptive smooth-blend of a strictly-positive distribution toward uniform until BOTH forward KL(q||p) and reverse KL(p||q) drop under given radii, returning a valid positive, unit-sum array verified against an independent dense reference (RL and undercount/miscount edges). (3) scipy.signal.stft at documented fixed parameters over provided signals, exporting linear (not dB) magnitudes; the magnitudes are compared exact allclose to a fresh identical scipy call on each hidden signal, and /app/out.npy is checked byte-equal to that computation for the visible sine-sum. (4) per-round accuracy that drops invalid and unmatched pairs, correct/total with half-up to 3 decimals and null accuracy when no valid pairs (adversarial=2). (5) a symbolic sympy integrand/interval that sp.integrate evaluates to the exact Rational(1,n+1) (no floating decimal). Reasoning comes from deriving the adaptive-KL schedule and the ODE/generalization; hidden cases exercise different degrees, radii sizes (including zero radii and length-1), unmatched/error-dense rounds, and dissimilar signal/NFFT settings, so hardcoding any visible value is impossible.

cedar-pier.notes: Multi-stage classifier pipeline that must be fully config-driven (data/outputs/knobs) and generalize to a fresh dataset mounted at verify time. It must fit a real scikit-learn linear model whose coefficient vector length equals the feature count and whose constrained feature is strictly negative (enforced deterministically by refit-on-flipped-column + coefficient remap, not just 'trust the data'), meet an accuracy floor on independent held-out rows for every hidden dataset, persist a plain row-wise numeric vector file loadable by numpy.loadtxt, emit config/metrics/progress under a config-specified experiment-data directory, and expose a Hydra debug override (debug.enabled=true) that shortens training to a single epoch + small batch while keeping all other defaults. hidden cases probe generalization to fresh datasets with different effect magnitudes/noise, plus a malformed dataset (missing the constrained column) that must trigger a clean non-zero exit without clobbering the good model. Hard: difficulty comes from the chained config->fit->sign-enforce->gate->persist stages, written ML correctness (sign/shape/accuracy/vector), hidden generalization, and the debug-override semantics. Note the nominal scenario target was 'medium' but the highest competency floor (C-2b609283, numeric vector file) is 'hard', so the bucket is hard to honor the >= max-floor rule.

cedar-vault.notes: Single deliverable program plus its visible-run artifact: implement exact-integer greedy next-token generation (argmax, lowest-id tie-break, fixed max_new count, context window) over a JSON model, with distractor sampling knobs (temperature/top_k/top_p/repetition_penalty) that must be ignored. Hidden cases probe ties, prompts shorter than ctx, max_new=0, and cyclic repetition, so any sampling deviation or off-by-one count fails. Rubric: reasoning_depth (tie-break + window logic), adversarial_inputs and hidden_case_generalization (4 distinct hidden models), quantitative_correctness (exact token sequences).

cello-harbor.documented_probe: C-1ca974ef (bundle streaming requests into aligned batches meeting cost/latency and granularity constraints): reference floor is hard and this covering task is authored at hard; the verifier fully checks all six structural constraints on hidden cases (alignment multiples, segment/window caps, window budget, deadlines, exact-once order-preserving ids).
cello-harbor.notes: Single-stage scheduler: pack an arrival-ordered chunk stream into sector-aligned segments grouped into capped broadcast windows under a window budget and per-chunk deadlines. Any valid arrangement passes (no fixed expected output), so the verifier validates the six structural constraints programmatically on the visible fixture and on every hidden case. Edge cases: empty stream, single chunk, deadline pressure, cap-driven breaks mid-window, odd granularity (sector=7/12). Hard difficulty from the six-way constraint interaction and deadline reasoning.

chert-quay.notes: Agent must read the SQLite header fields, classify the truncation mode (intact / page_aligned / mid_page), and implement a salvage strategy (zero-pad to the header-declared size, open read-only, probe rowids individually tolerating malformed-image errors) that recovers rows on complete pages AND rows on a partial page whose cells lie within the surviving bytes. Nonzero reasoning_depth (header decoding + three-way mode classification + partial-page subtlety), debugging_ambiguity (must empirically discover which rows of the partial page survive; wrong strategy silently loses rows), quantitative_correctness (exact ints/floats in the report), hidden_case_generalization (4 hidden DBs covering all three modes and different sizes).

cinder-dial.notes: Single-stage: read a combined predictions/truth record, keep only question ids present on both sides, drop pairs where either side is not a JSON number (ERR, null, booleans, quoted numbers), score exact numeric matches, report per-round correct/total with half-up rounding to 3 decimals (null when no valid pairs) plus an overall aggregate, and order rounds numerically. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (pair semantics + half-up + numeric sort), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (multiple hidden cases: ties, empty, type traps), and quantitative_correctness (exact ints and rounded floats). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

cinder-dump.notes: Single-stage but multi-step: parse canonical hexdump -C fragment dumps (8-digit absolute offsets, two-space group separator, ASCII annotation column), expand `*` repeat-collapse runs correctly against advancing offsets, place fragments by absolute offset from a shuffled manifest while ignoring decoy files, tolerate overlapping fragments and partial final rows, and reassemble a byte-exact x86-64 ELF that must actually execute and print a sentinel line. Hidden cases probe shuffled+decoy, overlap, heavy `*` runs, single-byte final row, and no-repeat variants; the verifier checks exact SHA-256 plus runtime stdout. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (offset-driven placement, repeat semantics), adversarial_inputs and hidden_case_generalization (five distinct dump layouts), quantitative_correctness (byte-exact sha + executable output), dependent_stages (reassembly -> execution -> captured output), debugging_ambiguity (partial rows and padding).

cinder-fleet.documented_probe: C-7f8aa502 (write the recovered value with the expected normalization): reference floor is medium; the covering task exercises it at medium. The recovered secret must be persisted so the stripped contents match the expected string exactly (lowercase, no surrounding whitespace), with payloads deliberately carrying surrounding spaces and mixed case, and the verifier byte-checks the deliverable and re-runs the tool on hidden dumps. Documented probe waiver.
cinder-fleet.notes: Multi-stage binary recovery: parse a TLV firmware dump, brute-force a 4-digit PIN validated by embedded CRC32 records (decoy TOKEN/CRC pairs, CRC-before-TOKEN ordering, noise and decoy tags), XOR-decode the payload, and persist the secret with exact normalization plus a faithful record table. Hidden dumps vary PIN, token, decoys, noise, and record order. Rubric nonzero for dependent_stages and reasoning_depth (recovery chain), debugging_ambiguity (CRC-validated PIN search), adversarial_inputs (decoy pairs, whitespace-padded payloads), hidden_case_generalization (3 hidden dumps), quantitative_correctness (exact normalization and record table). No tool breadth, no environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

cinder-forge.notes: Security-audit competency: read Python service source, recognize five vulnerability patterns, and map each to the exact CWE identifier (CWE-78/89/502/327/798). Delivered as a reusable line-based scanner plus the report on the visible fixture. Hidden cases probe generality: parameterized SQL, literal-only commands, bytes-literal pickle, Loader=yaml.SafeLoader, environment-sourced credentials, commented-out decoys, strong hashes, dotted attribute assignment, empty findings list, and two sql-injection/weak-hash repeats per file. Any wrong/missing CWE id, wrong line, wrong rule, or a decoy reported fails the audit. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (five interlocking rules), adversarial_inputs and hidden_case_generalization (decoy-dense hidden sources), quantitative_correctness (exact report structure).

cinder-guest.notes: Hard bucket (sum 18): the agent must bring up a tiny guest under software-only QEMU TCG with a telnet-served monitor and a TCP-redirected serial console, keep the emulator alive as a background service, wait for the guest boot markers, and drive the guest's serial shell over the loopback port to mount a tmpfs, compute a scenario-dependent result in-guest with shell arithmetic, and read the tokenized answer back off the serial line. Hidden cases re-execute /app/run.sh on genuinely different scenarios (different operands, operation, token, loopback ports) and the verifier independently probes both the monitor HMP console and the live serial shell. Difficulty comes from dependent virtualization stages, background-service/socket statefulness, interactive serial-protocol driving (marker/prompt synchronization), and diagnosing guest-side failures indirectly.

cinder-keeper.notes: Two chained stages (dependent_stages=1): derive the struct layout and gate constant from C source, then craft an exact byte payload (TAG_LEN filler + little-endian PERMIT_MAGIC) that flips the adjacent control word, plus a reusable crafter that parses the constants from any conforming source. Covers C-1aefef55 (byte-level payload overwriting an adjacent field to bypass a check) at medium: an underrun, wrong length, big-endian encoding, or wrong value keeps the gate locked. reasoning_depth=2 (C struct layout, endianness, define parsing); debugging_ambiguity=2 because failures only ever print LOCKED, so the agent must infer the offset/value from source alone; quantitative_correctness=2 (exact byte count and exact 32-bit value). generalization=2 (hidden gate builds with different TAG_LEN, decimal/hex/suffixed magics incl. a leading-zero-byte value); adversarial_inputs=1. No resource pressure; totals bucket to medium.

cinder-loom.documented_probe: C-38bb2e3e (recover deleted/embedded files and materialize them byte-accurately into a clean directory): covered at hard by the Loom store — deleted-vs-active flag semantics, rot entries whose stored CRC no longer matches the clobbered payload, orphan slack bytes that must never be recovered, and a clean-dir contract where /app/recovered must contain nothing extra; the verifier executes the deliverable tool on hidden stores and byte-compares all recovered files.
cinder-loom.notes: Two deliverables: a general carver tool (re-run unchanged on hidden stores) plus the byte-accurate visible materialization into /app/recovered with nothing extra. Adversarial: rot entries (CRC of original vs clobbered bytes), active decoys, ghost slack blobs, stale-output purge requirement. Hard: variable-length binary directory parsing, integrity filtering, exact byte materialization.

cinder-reach.documented_probe: C-5b5e6c73 (compute and include derived statistics fields): reference floor is hard and this covering task exercises it at hard — the program must parse a strict access-log grammar, skip vs. count malformed lines correctly, and derive seven aggregate fields (per-class status tallies, error rate, mean, interpolated p95, byte total, tie-broken argmax client) that all must be present in the designated JSON output.
cinder-reach.notes: Single-stage generalizable program: strict-grammar HTTP access-log parsing plus derived statistics (counts, ratio, mean, interpolated percentile, argmax with deterministic tie-break, null propagation on empty input). Hidden cases cover empty logs, malformed variants, '-' byte fields, ties, odd/even percentile interpolation. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth, debugging_ambiguity, adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness.

cinder-reef.notes: Single-deliverable HTTP-service task at full hard fidelity: the client must manage a local server process lifecycle (free port, start, readiness poll on /health, teardown), enumerate proteins via /api/proteins, tolerate retired proteins that 404 on /api/spectra, and apply a compound spectral rule: unique donor by inclusive emission band, unique acceptor by inclusive excitation band AND a non-negative gap to the donor capped at max_gap_nm (band-only selection picks a wrong acceptor on every seeded database). The report must reproduce the /api/spectra payloads byte-exactly. reasoning_depth=2 (two-stage fetch plus compound inclusive-band/gap predicate), adversarial_inputs=2 (retired-404 ids, in-band but gap-violating decoys).

cinder-vale.documented_probe: C-a4cb7c45 (emit plan records in the required schema): covered directly as the hard reference task; plans.jsonl is byte-checked on the visible basket and on every hidden workdir, with key order, compact separators, and float/int typing enforced.
cinder-vale.notes: Single-stage: exact-schema plan-record emission (one record per request with id, batch, and a concrete shape object, key order pinned) plus an exact DP deadline-scheduling optimization with a documented tie-break. Hidden baskets probe ties, greedy traps, infeasible/zero-profit jobs, exact fits, single-job baskets, and fractional volumes. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (EDF DP + tie-break), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (four hidden workdirs), quantitative_correctness (exact profit and finish times). Totals bucket to hard.

cinder-vane.notes: Focused Hydra config-group probe: author a root config with a mode defaults group plus standard/debug group files, wire overrides (mode=debug, dataset=..., outputs.*=...) through Hydra's compose API into a numpy mini-batch SGD logistic trainer, and honor the debug semantics (debug flag true, effective epochs 1, batch 8) while every other default is kept. Verifier re-runs the trainer on the visible fixture and two hidden telemetry datasets in both modes and re-checks reported vs. model-reproduced accuracy. Easy: single-stage, one override mechanism, generous accuracy floors.

cirrus-gauge.notes: Competency C-6fcd47f5: stand up a solver and train/test network definition for a training run. The agent authors a prototxt generator CLI plus the visible solver/train/test triple. The checker parses the generated prototxt and enforces: solver_mode CPU, max_iter clamped to the 1000 cap, net/test_net pointing at the generated nets inside the out-dir, positive base_lr/test_iter/test_interval, per-phase data layers whose source points into the given data root with the requested batch size, unique layer names, SoftmaxWithLoss (+Accuracy on test), byte-level determinism, and non-zero exit without artifacts on invalid arguments. Hidden cases exercise unseen data roots, batch 1 and 64, and max_iter above the cap.

cistern-anchor.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on spf13/cobra at parent commit cc7e235fc26cfd0b5ae36c960f399eea4badaa3e (real upstream bug, issue #1781, fixed by 6b0bd3076cfafd1c108264ed1e4aa0c0fe3f8537). Find() resolves subcommands by locating the first argument that matches the subcommand name and removing it; when a flag value happens to equal a subcommand name, that value is removed instead (argsMinusFirstX scans raw args), the flag value is lost and every later token shifts left, so the program receives wrong arguments (mined symptom: TestFind/[--foo_child_--bar_something_child] 'Expected: [--foo child --bar something] / Got: [--foo --bar something child]'). The image clones cobra shallow at the parent, overlays the upstream regression test command_test.go (extracted from the fix commit at build time) onto the working tree so `go test -v ./... -run TestFind` fails in-image exactly as mined; the fix commit itself is fetched only into a throwaway bare clone and is never reachable from /app/src/.git. Agent must reproduce, localise the bug in the real tree (the argsMinusFirstX/search-path in command.go), and fix it without touching anything else. The V-language (formerly 'Go') go1.24.0 toolchain is pinned from go.dev/dl; module/compile caches live in world-writable /opt paths and are warmed at build, so the trial is fully offline; the suite (279+ tests) must be run as the unprivileged user vtest (uid 1000) because one upstream test expects a permission-denied error that root bypasses. Verifier: provenance (HEAD=parent, fix commit unreachable, only command.go plus the overlaid regression-test file differ, command_test.go byte-identical to golden), the upstream TestFind regression test, the full project suite, and two authored hidden cases (novel flag/subcommand argument layouts through Find, and a two-level command tree with the collision at its deeper level) that fail at the parent and pass after the fix. Both directions verified inside the task image before shipping.

cistern-basin.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy at parent commit 42ddb1fd5f1e29682bcd6ccc7b835999aafec12e (real upstream bug, issue #12368, fixed by 48ad8c81115bd01d733fe1a4f78c8c30d7c2abbb, PR #12369). SQLiteDDLCompiler.post_create_table concatenates the 'WITHOUT ROWID' and 'STRICT' table-option clauses with a bare newline, so a table defined with both sqlite_with_rowid=False and sqlite_strict=True compiles to 'CREATE TABLE atable (id INTEGER)\n WITHOUT ROWID\n STRICT' - DDL that SQLite rejects with 'near "STRICT": syntax error'. Agent must localise the bug in the real tree (lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/sqlite/base.py), fix it so the clauses are comma-separated, and keep the project's own SQLite dialect compile tests green; the verifier also runs the upstream regression test extracted from the fix commit into /opt/golden (SQLTest::test_create_table_without_rowid_strict), the project's own SQLTest + OnConflictDDLTest classes, and authored hidden cases: end-to-end DDL execution against in-memory SQLite (sqlite_master/reflection round-trip) and compile-level assertions over other table shapes including single-option regression guards. Pure Python (DISABLE_SQLALCHEMY_CEXT=1), no network, no DB server (bundled sqlite3 3.4x supports STRICT >= 3.37). Both directions were re-confirmed inside the built task image: golden FAILS at parent with the comma-missing AssertionError and the probe raises sqlite3.OperationalError near "STRICT"; golden PASSES and the DDL executes at the fix commit applied via the same textual patch the oracle ships.

cistern-beacon.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on sympy/sympy at parent commit 6a968f7201e5d9187b50dbdc2cc66b17594a59ac (real upstream bug, issue #29368, fixed in 66ee6e06934fede513c7504413baacbf80917186). In linprog's no-constraints branch the right-hand side is built as a C.cols x 1 zero column (zeros(C.cols, 1)) next to a 0 x C.cols A; the row-count mismatch makes the internal _simplex routine see a truthy B beside a falsy A and raise ValueError('must give A and B'), so an unconstrained LP (cost-only call) is never solved. The upstream fix builds b as zeros(0, 1) so the problem flows through as a 0-row problem: tolerable costs return the trivial optimum (0, [0..0]) and a cost row with a negative entry raises UnboundedLPError. Agent must localise the bug in the real tree and fix it with minimal changes; verifier runs the upstream regression test extracted from the fix commit at image build time (test_29368) plus the project's own existing test_simplex.py, and hidden cases exercising the same branch from inputs the upstream test does not use (explicit empty constraint matrices, larger/zero-entry/rational/Float cost rows, 2+ variable default-bounds forms and their UnboundedLPError counterparts). Pure Python, ~1 min whole verification at 1 CPU, no network at trial. Both directions re-verified inside the task image before shipping.

cistern-bell.notes: Real upstream bug in tmux/tmux (issue 5576): in cmd-find.c the relative window and pane offset parsers call strtonum(window + 1, 1, INT_MAX, NULL) / strtonum(pane + 1, 1, INT_MAX, NULL), discarding the error result, so malformed offsets like +foo, -0, +1x are silently treated as offset 0 and the command acts on the current window/pane. Fix (upstream 00f3899a, merged on master as d44bfda2): capture the error string, return -1 on a parse/range error so the caller reports 'can't find window: <token>' / 'can't find pane: <token>'. Task image checks out 73db0a54 (buildable master-line parent whose cmd-find.c carries the identical bug), NOT 557967c3: that commit is the openbsd-line twin whose tree has a BSD-only Makefile and no autogen.sh/configure.ac and cannot build on Ubuntu; 73db0a54 is the tree the mining phase verified as the bug tree (d44bfda2^). Golden tests (regress/targets.sh, regress/targets-panes.sh) are extracted at image build time from upstream merge d44bfda2 into /opt/golden from a throwaway clone, so the fix commit is never reachable from /app/tmux's object store and no upstream bytes enter this tree. Hidden cases use token shapes the upstream checks do not use (+1x, +1.5, overflow, -foo0 window side; +2x, -0x, +1.0, overflow pane side) plus positive guards (+, -, +01, -1, +07 index path) so a fix that simply rejects everything fails. Pre-existing suite subset run by the verifier: check-names, command-alias, environ, has-session-return, if-shell-error. Measured in-image at 1 CPU (bench-base:ubuntu-24.04): clean 'make -j1' of the parent tree 30s; incremental one-file rebuild after the fix 0.7s; the agent's documented './autogen.sh && ./configure && make' on the pre-built tree 2.2s; each golden regress script ~1.2s; harbor trial end-to-end (build+oracle+verifier) < 3 min. Build deps via apt (build-essential autoconf automake libtool pkg-config bison byacc libevent-dev libncurses-dev libutempter-dev); no runtime dependency pins (tmux pins none, by design).

cistern-berth.documented_probe: aio-libs/aiohttp @ 956f140095b21a88e11def934d42de85cc0b2b6b (parent of fix b2b2bce03c17521dc454cdd4a6e19ab0a08bce6b for issue #13229): shallow init+fetch clone, pure-Python editable install (AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS=1). Repro: python3 -c "from multidict import CIMultiDict; from aiohttp.test_utils import make_mocked_request; req = make_mocked_request('GET', '/', headers=CIMultiDict({'Forwarded': '; a'})); print(dict(req.forwarded[0]))" -> hangs forever at parent (timeout 15 -> exit 124), prints {} immediately with the fix. Golden test: test_single_forwarded_header_trailing_bad_value from tests/test_web_request.py at the fix commit, extracted into /opt/golden at build time; at parent it hangs (4 of 5 params), at fix 5 passed. Own-suite gate: tests/test_web_request.py -k forwarded. Hidden cases (trailing-bad single values with empty elements / double separators / quoted-string values with semicolons; multi-header-line scenarios) hang at parent, terminate and parse at fix. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image at build time.
cistern-berth.notes: Upstream-clone bug-fix task (v4.2/v4.3 family) on the real aio-libs/aiohttp repo, SHA-pinned at the buggy revision. The bug: BaseRequest.forwarded's parse loop calls field_value.find(';', pos); when it returns -1 the code slices with [pos:-1] and, for a header that ends with an empty-looking token, computes pos = -1 + 1 = 0, so the loop never advances and spins at 100% CPU on the event loop. Any of 'a', '; a', 'for=1.2.3.4; a', 'for=_real; x' (i.e. any value whose tail is empty or a bare token) hangs. Upstream fix b2b2bce adds semi := find(';', pos) and breaks when no separator remains. The instruction names neither the issue number, the commit, nor the file; the agent must localise the hang in the real tree. Environment traps that would kill the bug: none of the positive cases here depend on a specific dependency version, but the whole task needs aiohttp importable, editable (so edits are live), and with working make_mocked_request; the parent-direction build check fails closed if the repro does not hang (exit 124) in the built image. The golden regression test is extracted at build time from a throwaway shallow clone into /opt/golden, so the fix commit is never reachable from /app/src/.git; the verifier asserts HEAD is the pinned parent, the fix commit object is absent, and the working tree differs from upstream in exactly one file (aiohttp/web_request.py). Verifier pytest runs pass explicit --timeout=15 so a mis-fix that still hangs fails fast instead of stalling the verifier; the reproducer probe runs under a subprocess timeout. Difficulty medium (total rubric 10).

cistern-bight.documented_probe: clap-rs/clap pinned at parent fb9435d026ab011c9071ca92eeab738b9b30ca13 (shallow single-commit clone; the fix commit 8c92ef6c76686a642e748919f33587561c2a0280 is never fetched into /app/src and is provably absent from its object store). rustup toolchain 1.98.1 pinned. Probe (measured inside the task image): full offline `cargo test --no-run -p clap` rebuild as uid 1000 takes ~13 s wall on 64 cores; incremental one-file rebuild a minute or two at 1 vCPU; the builder test binary run is 0.0-0.2 s. At the parent commit the planted upstream regression test hidden_possible_vals FAILS (exit 101, 'Eq failed' diff: expected one line '  -h, --help  Print help', actual two-line long layout with '(see a summary with '-h')'); after the one-clause fix the same test passes and the full builder suite is 812/812 green. Image size: 3260 MB. Offline-clean confirmed by running the oracle+verifier with no network.
cistern-bight.notes: v4.2 upstream-clone task. The agent gets the REAL clap-rs/clap tree (Rust-dialect codebase, ~1.4k source files) at the parent commit, sees only the user-visible help-layout symptom, and must reproduce, localise and fix the bug in src/builder/command.rs's long/short-help decision without being told the file, function, issue number or commit (the fix commit is not reachable from the clone and there is no network). The verifier plants the project's OWN regression test (help.rs as at the fix commit, extracted at image build time into /opt/golden, never vendored into this task tree) plus 3 authored hidden modules (a hidden-possible-values named option checked on both -h and --help alongside a visible option; hide_possible_values combined with a long help text which must STILL select the long layout, locking the fix's boundary; and visible-argument controls with helped possible values on both a positional and a named option that must keep the long layout), rebuilds offline and runs every builder-* suite binary end to end, also grepping per-test 'ok' lines so skipped/neutralised runs fail. Provenance is enforced at the blob level (every tracked file except the one allowed source file must hash to the pinned commit's blob; no untracked non-ignored files; object store holds nothing beyond the pinned commit) so a scratch file left behind, a reformat commit, or a sabotaged test file all fail. The over-fix direction is guarded: deleting the possible-value/long-help triggers to make the hidden tests pass collapses the visible-argument tests. Nop container scores 0 (regression test and hidden cases fail at parent; summary.md missing).

cistern-bridge.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on cure53/DOMPurify at the parent of 083bb8ae (8cc5ae1388587f7a08cc099ff2a5e985f85d77c5), the real fix for issue #1577. Symptom: when the sanitizer receives an already-parsed DOM node (as opposed to an HTML string), attribute names keep the case they were created with (setAttributeNS / createAttributeNS / imported XML nodes), and name-based removal (removeAttribute/getAttributeNode) ASCII-lowercases its lookup key but not the stored qualified name, so uppercase ONCLICK/ONERROR and uppercase HREF=javascript: attributes survive the walk and re-arm when the subtree is serialized back to HTML. The agent must localise the removal step in the real tree (src/purify.ts), repair it to remove the exact Attr node, rebuild the committed dist artifact with the project's own build so the project's dist-based jsdom suite exercises the fix, keep the project's own test/ suite green, and satisfy provenance checks (parent commit checked out, fix commit unreachable, only src + committed dist artifacts modified). The verifier runs the upstream regression tests extracted from the fix commit (targeted module slice: 4 case-preservation regressions + string control + DOMParser variant which runs under jsdom 29.1.1), the project's own full jsdom suite, and 3 authored hidden cases on inputs the upstream tests do not use (other elements/handlers, multiple case-preserved attrs on one node with safe-attribute preservation, and a reparse-sink scenario that proves handlers cannot re-arm). Both directions re-verified inside the task image: parent FAILs the repro (3 surviving handlers, exit 1) and the golden slice; the applied fix passes. jsdom 29.1.1 pinned by the project's own package-lock; ~1 min build (clone + npm install), 35s full jsdom suite.

cistern-buoy.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on a real codebase: curl/curl checked out at b8172ada19b1211aeed64f473b4a53e941c6fabe (parent of upstream fix 08d50a791b3197a3d0a4fc2f778e243f5501c67e, upstream issue #22878). The clone is initialized fresh and a single shallow fetch of the pinned parent SHA is made, so the fix commit is not reachable from the clone at all; the upstream regression test tests/data/test1862 is extracted from the fix commit as a raw file into /opt/golden and never enters the tree. The real bug is present: Curl_hsts_parse() caps max-age at TIME_T_MAX and stores it raw, so a Strict-Transport-Security header with max-age=2^60 lands an expiry that curlx_gmtime() cannot format; hsts_out() then returns an error and Curl_hsts_save() aborts the whole write after Curl_fopen already truncated the target file to zero bytes, destroying the user's HSTS cache. Upstream fix caps max-age at 2*365*24*3600 on parse (overflow clamps to the cap) and makes hsts_out() skip an unformattable entry instead of aborting the save. The agent must reproduce (loopback HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8891 serving the extreme max-age header; CURL_HSTS_HTTP=yes CURL_TIME=1920582000 are honoured only by the checked-in debug build), localise (gdb/strace, or reason from the cache-file format), fix the real tree, rebuild incrementally, write /app/diagnosis.md, and keep the project's own HSTS tests green (runtests 1, 1660, 1674). Verifier: provenance asserts (HEAD still at parent, fix commit not present, only lib/hsts.c may be modified, no stray untracked files), incremental make, then the instruction's exact reproducer against the fixed binary with exact 228-byte three-entry cache content, then TWO authored hidden cases the upstream test does not use (max-age=63072001 with includeSubDomains at CURL_TIME=1600000000 expecting exactly '20220913 12:26:40'; max-age=2147483647 at CURL_TIME=1700000000 expecting exactly '20251113 22:13:20' instead of the parent's 2091 date), then the golden test 1862 via tests/runtests.pl, then the existing-suite selection. Oracle reward 1, untouched-tree nop reward 0 (shipped binary truncates the cache to 0 bytes: hidden checks, golden test and CLI repro all FAIL). Difficulty is medium: real ~50k-LOC C codebase, deterministic repro, small well-contained fix with two coupled changes.

cistern-cable.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on encode/httpx at parent commit 90538a3b4610ba49ce16c997bcfdb9101f9503be (real upstream bug, issue #2998, fixed by 1e110964736a95d822144390b99d7ecf17fca527). Response.iter_text()/aiter_text() yield a spurious trailing empty string for any streamed body: decoding the final empty text through TextChunker.decode() returns [''] because of the bare 'return [content]' when the chunk size is unset, so the final decoder flush becomes a bogus chunk. Agent must localise the bug in the real tree, fix it so iterated text chunks never contain a trailing empty piece (joining chunks must reproduce the document exactly), keep tests/test_decoders.py green, and only modify the minimal source surface; verifier also runs the upstream regression test test_streaming_text_decoder extracted from the fix commit, plus hidden cases over UTF-8-split chunking, empty/interleaved empty chunks, and the async aiter_text path. Pure in-memory, no network, <2s test suite. Both directions verified inside the task image before shipping.

cistern-cairn.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on expressjs/express at parent commit 160b91cbf79b595712b694c3513c347551d17fbe (express 5.0.0-beta.3 era, real upstream bug, issue #5792). res.clearCookie builds its options with merge({expires:new Date(1),path:'/'}, options), so a caller's maxAge or explicit expires date overrides the forced past expiry: clearing with a keep-alive maxAge emits a Set-Cookie carrying Max-Age plus a future Expires, and clearing with an explicit expires emits that future date instead of 1 Jan 1970 - the cookie survives/re-creates instead of being removed. Agent must localise the bug in the real tree (lib/response.js), force the past expiry and drop maxAge while keeping unrelated passthrough options, keep the repo's own cookie tests green, and only modify the minimal source file; verifier also runs the upstream regression test extracted from fix commit 82fc12a40b3e6694e9a2c9b1376e7548d95779f6 into /opt/golden, and authored hidden cases over a large maxAge+domain/httpOnly, a far-future expires, a negative maxAge and secure/sameSite combos. Pure-JS, node 22, no network, ~18ms mocha golden. node_modules warmed at build time (gitignored upstream, survives git reset). Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping. REVIEW (v4 wave): independently re-verified both directions in a fresh build of the task image; confirmed the fix commit is the direct child of the parent and the golden sha 83d883ab equals the genuine upstream file at 82fc12a40b3e6694e9a2c9b1376e7548d95779f6:test/res.clearCookie.js. cistern-cinder.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on giampaolo/psutil at parent commit afaaf9f340ff6561541f9f4781c58268b59abdac (real upstream bug, issue #2809; fix 8d8ffe516627c024ccd216485b5920e8ffa8a88e). On arm64 Linux builds with shadow call stacks, /proc/meminfo's ShadowCallStack field is printed with a fixed-width 8-digit payload; once the value reaches 8 digits there is no space between the name and the number (fs/proc/meminfo.c uses %8lu), and virtual_memory()'s line.split() parse then feeds int() the second token b'kB' and aborts with ValueError, so no memory statistics can be read at all on those systems. Agent must reproduce, localise and fix it in the real tree (the only difference between parent and fix for this bug is the 2-line parse change in virtual_memory(): split on the first ':' and int() the first whitespace token of the value). Verifier runs the upstream regression test test_virtual_memory_no_space_after_colon extracted from the fix commit, a deterministic mock/proc-based subset of the project's own tests/test_linux.py (the free/vmstat CLI-comparison classes are excluded: those CLIs are not installed in the container), and two authored hidden cases driving the same code path from meminfo layouts the upstream test does not use (multiple no-space standard fields with 9/11-digit magnitudes; the MemAvailable-missing fallback and avail>total clamp edges), read through PROCFS_PATH. The C extension is built and pip-installed editable at image build time; the fix is pure Python so no rebuild is needed. Runners pinned: pytest 9.1.1, pytest-instafail 0.5.0, pytest-xdist 3.8.0 (the latter two are required by the project's own [tool.pytest] addopts: --instafail, -p instafail, -p xdist). Both directions re-verified inside the task image before shipping. [reg] verifier's existing-tests slice also excludes TestVirtualMemoryAgainstFree, psutil's own free-vs-psutil comparison with a 5MB tolerance and 10 retries, which flakes under load on a busy shared host; it is unrelated to the /proc/meminfo parsing bug and was observed to fail only during the loaded 4-shard census, and not to affect discrimination (golden + hidden cases carry the verdict).

cistern-cleat.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on gin-gonic/gin at parent commit 915e4c90d28ec4cffc6eb146e208ab5a65eac772 (real upstream issue #4472). Context.ClientIP() reads forwarded client-IP headers through a single-value getter, so when a proxy chain appends several X-Forwarded-For header lines the method only ever consults the first line and reports the leftmost address instead of the rightmost untrusted one; IP-based logging, rate limiting and allow/deny logic see the wrong address. Agent must localise the bug in the real tree (the ClientIP() header-reading loop), fix it so every header line is consulted, keep gin's own test suite green, and leave the working tree with only the minimal source change. Verifier runs the project's own regression tests extracted from the fix commit at image build time (TestContextClientIPWithMultipleHeaders/WithSingleHeader in /opt/golden), gin's own full test suite (packages gin, gin/binding, gin/render exactly as the Makefile does), and hidden cases over a three-line proxy chain, X-Real-IP as an alternative trusted header, and malformed leading lines; it also asserts provenance (HEAD still the pinned parent, fix commit object absent, only context.go modified). Toolchain pin: official Go 1.24.0 linux-amd64 tarball (sha256 dea9ca38...), required because gin's go.mod declares go 1.24.0 and its tests run under the new go command; module and build caches are warmed at image build time so the trial is fully offline. Both directions verified inside the task image before shipping: golden multi-header test fails at parent with expected "5.6.7.8" actual "1.2.3.4" and passes after the fix; full suite green in both states.

cistern-compass.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on junit-team/junit5 at parent commit f8513cbd8b867f0c4252d4d9625d77edc45820cb (real upstream issue #4692, fix commit 2a52a0643fba15b52fcf13dd553758fcbc1d0458). The CSV reader shared by @CsvSource and @CsvFileSource trims unquoted columns with String.strip() instead of String.trim(), so Unicode White_Space above U+0020 (thin space U+2009, ideographic space U+3000, line separator U+2028, ...) is silently removed from argument values while non-whitespace control characters below U+0020 (NUL U+0000, U+0001, U+000E, ...) are no longer trimmed at all — values a parameterized test receives changed between releases with no test change (referenced upstream: junit-team/junit-framework#3824). Note: in this JDK (24.0.2) String.strip() keeps U+00A0 NBSP while removing the other White_Space characters, and the regression test's observable failure at the parent is the NUL column; both discriminating families are still exercised by the authored hidden cases and the golden test fails at parent / passes at fix. The fix is one line in the shared reader (field.strip() -> field.trim()) plus a one-sentence Javadoc clarification in both annotations. The image clones junit5 fetching ONLY the parent SHA (fix commit and default-branch tip unreachable), overlays the project's own regression test (trimsSpacesUsingStringTrim, extracted from the fix commit at build time into /opt/golden) onto the working tree exactly like the mining reproduction, warms the full :jupiter-tests closure online and proves it reruns --offline failing with the mined symptom. Toolchain pinned: JDK 24.0.2+12 compile toolchain + Gradle daemon (gradle-daemon-jvm.properties toolchainVersion=24), JDK 25.0.4.1+1 and apt JDK 21 exported as JDK24/JDK25/JDK21 for org.gradle.java.installations.fromEnv; Gradle 8.14.2-bin wrapper SHA256-pinned in the tree. Verifier: tree provenance (HEAD=parent, fix commit unreachable, only the three junit-jupiter-params main sources plus the overlaid test file differ, test file byte-identical to golden), the golden regression class green, the tree's own CsvFileArgumentsProviderTests green, and two authored hidden cases (a Unicode-whitespace/control-character family through @CsvSource and a trimming family through the @CsvFileSource reader) that both fail at the parent and pass with the fix. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping: at parent, 6 tests fail (golden trimsSpacesUsingStringTrim + 5 authored: U+3000/U+1680/U+2009/U+202F/U+205F/U+2028/29 preservation and control-char trimming through both sources); with the fix applied, the same run is BUILD SUCCESSFUL with 0 failures.

cistern-coral.notes: v4.2/v4.3 upstream-clone debugging task on the real libvips tree (libvips/libvips issue #4877, fix 7cfd70a869de8fe3f3a22b32f755e382130b716c; parent ea7e608844b85f4d296821e59b2483369b301b53; the mining entry guessed 'easy', the measured family rubric lands at 13, medium). The upstream fix commit is deliberately unreachable from the clone (shallow fetch pins only the parent; the golden fix-era test_draw.py is extracted into /opt/golden from a throwaway clone whose sha256 is pinned in the Dockerfile, and the verifier asserts `git cat-file -e <fix>` fails). Offline-clean: nothing at trial time fetches from the network; ninja rebuild, ldconfig, pytest, pyvips all run with no network, and parent/fix builds share soname libvips.so.42.20.0 so no stale-.so shadowing can occur. cistern-crest.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on mikf/gallery-dl at parent commit a879e5d468e43fac9daf6bdc4726f853a9c85567 (real upstream bug, github issue #8918, fixed in 12e2113a). Both directions re-verified inside the task image before shipping: parent probe prints stale 315532800.0 / -62135596800.0, golden MtimeTest 3 failed/5 passed; fix probe prints None / None, golden MtimeTest 8 passed.

cistern-dune.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on pallets/click at parent commit 5b9630f50fde938b72ad8c99542efe3a6f5717e2 (real upstream bug, issue #3105). FuncParamType.convert catches ValueError raised by the wrapped conversion function but discards the exception's message, echoing only the raw input back in the resulting BadParameter error; the fix (PR #3211) uses str(exc) as the message and falls back to the raw input only when the exception message is empty. cistern-ember.documented_probe: pallets/jinja parent 079e8312c3ceee54066d2dc887da83867f2db68a (4MB, ~200 files, pyproject); upstream issue #1960, fix commit 1655128cfc0e8b598d5b3f361a3983f82098276b
cistern-ember.notes: Real-upstream debugging task (v4.2 family). Image clones pallets/jinja and checks out exactly the PARENT commit, which contains the real bug: async template rendering leaks async generators whenever output is consumed incrementally (streaming a page, include, extends, self.foo() block calls), so runtimes that police cleanup (trio) emit 'Async generator was garbage collected before it had been exhausted' ResourceWarnings. The agent gets /app/reproduce.py (visible reproducer, trio-only observable: exits 1 at parent, 0 fixed), no git metadata (the tree is a bare working copy; the fix commit is never fetched into /app/src and a build-time belt check asserts it is unreachable), and no file names. It must localise the bug in a real 4MB tree (module-level cause lives in compiler.py + environment.py + async_utils.py), fix it at source, and keep the project's own suite green. Verifier: (1) byte-level provenance manifest frozen at build time — every file must stay byte-identical to the parent checkout except exactly src/jinja2/{async_utils,compiler,environment}.py; no new/deleted files (pycache/pyc/pytest_cache excluded); (2) the project's OWN regression tests for the bug, extracted at build time from the fix commit's tests/test_async.py into /opt/golden (never committed here, byte-audit clean), copied into tests/ and run — at parent the four [trio] parametrisations fail via pluggy.PluggyTeardownRaisedWarning, at fix all 8 pass; (3) the project's own full tests/ suite must pass (927 passed in ~2s at 1 CPU on the fixed tree); (4) three authored hidden cases (stream_early: 300-item for-loop partial consumption; include_stream: include-in-loop over 40 dict rows; extend_chain: 3-level inheritance with self.foo() block call) with fresh inputs and outputs different from the upstream test set, each asserting output prefix correctness AND absence of leaked-generator ResourceWarnings under BOTH asyncio and trio via synchronous catch_warnings+gc.collect (deterministic; verified failing at parent: 2-3 leaks per case, and passing at fix). Nop scores 0 via golden/suite/hidden failures. Dependencies pinned exactly (pytest 7.4.3, trio 0.34.0, pytest-timeout 2.4.0, MarkupSafe 3.0.3); trio is mandatory — under asyncio alone the regression is invisible. Tried-and-tested both directions in the image: parent 4 failed/4 passed on goldens, 5 failed/922 passed on full suite, all hidden cases fail; fixed tree 8 passed goldens, 927 passed full suite, all hidden pass. Oracle applies byte-exact upstream hunks (patched modules are byte-identical to the fix commit files, verified with diff). The same Pythons/layout as the mining run: all checks offline.

cistern-fathom.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task: real pallets/werkzeug checkout at commit 4c09d1b3, the parent of upstream fix f516c400 (issue #2842). TypeConversionDict.get() (and the MultiDict family behind request.args/form/files) only catches ValueError from the type converter, so a None value for type=int lets TypeError escape the call and crash request handling; expected is fallback to the supplied default. The agent must reproduce, localise and fix in the real tree (upstream's own one-line fix: except (ValueError, TypeError)). The verifier swaps the fix-commit version of tests/test_datastructures.py (extracted at image build into /opt/golden from a deleted scratch clone) over the repo copy, requires it and two other untouched project test modules to pass, runs three authored hidden cases with inputs upstream's test does not use (float(None), int(list), int(dict), the MultiDict/OrderedMultiDict/ImmutableMultiDict/CombinedMultiDict family with None values, and exception-propagation semantics), and asserts provenance: HEAD pinned at the parent, fix commit absent from the object store, only the one library source file modified, no stray untracked files. Easy: one-line fix, direct repro, sub-second tests, no network.

cistern-ferry.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on the real prettier/prettier tree (pinned pre-fix parent 7c5872f7a27b3eb249d0347fcfac989eca2cb70b of upstream issue #19709). The bug: HTML attribute-name normalization (lowercasing) is gated on whether the element has an entry in Prettier's per-element attribute table (ELEMENT_ATTRIBUTES), so an attribute like CLASS on a well-known tag that lacks per-element data (e.g. <span>, <section>, <header>) is left uppercase while the same attribute on <div> is rewritten to class - the same attribute gets inconsistent casing depending on the tag. The agent gets the real repo (only the parent commit ever enters its object store; the fix commit is only fetched into a scratch clone at build time to extract the project's own regression suite tests/format/html/attributes/lowercase/ (format.test.js + snapshot) into /opt/golden, then deleted), repros with the project's own CLI (node bin/prettier.js <file>), localises the cause inside src/ (instruction names no file, issue or commit), and fixes it. Verifier: leak guard (fix object absent from /app/src) + provenance audit (only src/language-html/parse/postprocess.js may differ from the parent) + CLI repro /app/reproduce.js (must print class= on both span and div; fails at parent) + the upstream regression lowercase suite run with the project's own jest runner (snippet '#0 format 1' passes at fix, fails at parent) + the project's own targeted HTML suites (tests/format/html/attributes, case, basics, tags and tests/unit/html-elements.js, together ~110 tests, seconds at 1 CPU) still green + 2 authored hidden cases through the CLI (h1: class/id/title/style/lang/hidden/tabindex etc. upper- and mixed-cased on tags without per-element data; h2: casing consistency across dataful/data-less tags plus negative controls for unknown attributes and custom elements - both inputs the upstream lowercase test does not use, both fail at the parent). nop scores 0 (repro, golden and both hidden cases fail on the untouched tree).
