The agent must author and compile a compact C ray tracer (ray-sphere intersection, lambert+phong materials, one reflection bounce, shadow rays) that re-derives a target color render and a depth/color raster from scene data rather than reading a reference; the verifier recompiles ptrace.c and re-renders it, then compares against goldens with strict SSIM/density tolerances plus a compressed source-size ceiling, so an overfitting agent that embeds the golden bytes fails the budget and wrong shading/geometry fails the SSIM bar (hard). Debugging ambiguity is high because there is no numeric output to copy: the agent must get the ray/camera/lighting math, the PFM/PGM/PPM binary formats (row order, endian, headers) and full determinism exactly right to match reference thresholds. Complementary easy floor (PNG icon, byte-identical regeneration, parsing canvas size and fallbacks, rendering edge/malformed hidden scenes at correct size) is exercised too; the fixed-scene exact-golden checks are the hard gate.

dunlin-key.notes: Deterministic member ordering and identity: build a packing tool whose index and ZIP bundle derive member order from plain UTF-8 byte sorting (never locale collation) and carry zero host-identity fields (no owner/group/uid, no mtimes, fixed 1980 ZipInfo timestamps, external_attr 0, STORED, fresh ZipInfo per member). Medium floor from the multi-surface determinism contract (byte-identity across runs and across mtime-shifted/re-ordered tree copies, structural ZIP metadata checks) plus subtle sort cases (case, unicode, prefix ties). Hidden cases probe byte-order-only distinguishable name sets, a deep/binary/duplicate-content tree, and a synthesized empty tree; the verifier executes /app/pack_index.py unchanged on all of them.

dunlin-shoal.notes: Single-stage but multi-step: parse a compose-style stack file for db/user/password/published port, connect over TCP with md5 auth (wrong credentials genuinely fail), export a sorted table snapshot to JSON, and fail cleanly (non-zero, no output) on an unreachable port. Hidden scenarios reuse the deliverable against differently-configured live clusters (different db/user/password/port), so hard-coding the visible credentials fails. Small nonzero rubric for the dependency chain, psql tooling, parse/connect logic, adversarial unreachable-port input, hidden generalization and exact JSON correctness; no environment pressure or statefulness; totals bucket to medium.

dusk-anchor.notes: Single focused job: read a recovered-behavior spec (3-stage byte transform with an output-fed key register and an XOR trailer) and reimplement it as a fully standalone, statically linked C program. Hard because the cascade's key advances on the emitted byte (not the input), the trailer convention for empty input is non-obvious, and the isolation contract (clean-room rebuild from only app.c+Makefile, stdlib-only includes, no /app references, arbitrary-length and NUL-bearing input) has many ways to fail. The verifier independently derives expected outputs from the spec on hidden inputs (empty, NUL-mix, 64 KiB) and re-checks the proof digest.

dusk-forge.documented_probe: C-03964901 (keep the serialized model within a tight size budget): this task is the covering exercise at hard difficulty; the verifier byte-audits the entire /app/model directory against the 102400-byte ceiling and runs the loader on hidden calibration sets, so optimizer state, checkpoints, or float64 duplicates blow the gate.
dusk-forge.notes: Model-quality-vs-byte-budget tension: a 24-160-80-1 ReLU net trains to RMSE ~0.3 with plain numpy Adam, and its float32 weights (~67 KB) fit the 100 KB gate only if the artifact stores exactly the inference path — any optimizer moments, checkpoints, or float64 copies exceed it. The RMSE gate (0.45) sits between the best linear model (~0.52-0.60) and a genuine nonlinear fit, so the model must really be trained. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (architecture/training under a hard constraint), resource_pressure (the byte budget is the core difficulty), hidden_case_generalization (two hidden calibration sets, one with a 5% channel rescale), quantitative_correctness (RMSE threshold).

dusk-lattice.notes: Reverse-engineer a stripped native codec with no source: recover a three-part transformation (90-degree clockwise geometry, 8-bit bit-reversal tone table, channel-order swap) plus the exact output serialization, purely by observation and/or disassembly. Hard: partial models (geometry-only or table-only) all fail the byte-identical check; the agent must design discriminating probes (1x1 sweeps, orientation probes, distinct-channel probes) and nail canonical formatting. Verifier executes the deliverable on 6 hidden frames plus the visible fixture, byte-compares stdout, hides the native binary during grading, and enforces the no-modify rule on the fixture.

dusk-wicket.documented_probe: Linter rule engineering over a shipped mini lint engine (tokenizer + tiny AST + CLI skeleton with line-scoped suppression). The agent authors three rule plugins (forbid-call incl. attribute forms and an inside-function scope rule; shadow-var on a documented block model with for-target/param/def bindings; mut-default for mutable literal defaults), extends suppression with region (stack-nested, unclosed-to-EOF) and next-statement forms, and adds an incremental findings cache keyed by (rules signature, file content hash) with a --stats flag. The verifier runs /app/lintkit/lint.py on hidden minipy sources and independently recomputes the expected findings (its own tokenizer, parser, three rules and suppression semantics) comparing exact sorted JSON per file; cache correctness is checked by running the CLI twice against a fresh /app/lintcache (run 2 must be all hits with identical output) and by mutating a copied hidden file so the content-hash key must miss and produce updated findings.
dusk-wicket.notes: Medium: the task is staged (rules -> suppression -> cache) but every stage is small and self-contained; reasoning depth comes from the documented scope/block model and suppression precedence, adversarial inputs from nested/overlapping regions, unclosed regions reaching EOF, next-directives aimed at compound headers, for-target and param shadowing and defaults nested inside functions. Hidden sources generalize beyond the visible examples, and the probe recomputes everything independently so hard-coded or shortcut answers fail. Exactness is quantitative (line/col/message JSON equality) and the cache adds one interaction-statefulness dimension; no resource pressure and no unsafe-action penalty.

dust-tape.notes: Single tool with many adversarial byte-level edge cases: four PDP-11 a.out magic variants with 8-word header decoding (incl. truncated headers with null fields), ELF endianness/class/machine table, truncated ELF, MZ stub, text/junk/empty heuristic. Two hidden artifact sets (distinct PDP-11 binaries, big-endian MIPS ELF, unknown machine, x86_64 host case) plus a cross-checked archive inventory. Bucketed hard due to the header-layout reasoning and truncation semantics, though it is a focused single-competency task.

echo-dial.notes: One attack.py pipeline must, for any relay directory: recognise the exact 'encoded_<base64url unpadded>' naming convention (and not be fooled by look-alike decoys), recover original filenames (restoring base64url padding), decrypt each node body (standard base64 then byte-wise XOR with the repeated password key, validating UTF-8), emit name/plaintext artifacts in sorted order, and extract the single normalized secret word from the VAULT-VERDICT line. The debugging/ambiguity and adversary scores come from the unpadded-base64url restoration, the XOR/key-repetition decoding, mandatory skip of malformed and non-UTF-8 nodes, and the exact case/hyphen/digit normalization of the secret token. Hidden generalization comes from three genuinely different relay trees (fresh set, adversarial decoy set incl. a convention-matching but non-UTF-8 node, and an edge set with hyphen/dot/long unpadded names) that the deliverable must pass via the same CLI interface. Dropped the hard-floor reverse-engineered radix/range decoder competency (C-e41d6ebb) to keep the task coherent at the medium target.

echo-latch.notes: Easy: reclaim the content of an unlinked-but-open file descriptor via /proc/<pid>/fd. The only subtlety is selecting the right descriptor: the keeper also holds decoy fds whose paths still exist, so the tool must match the '(deleted)' readlink suffix and skip unreadable/non-numeric entries. The verifier executes the deliverable tool against the live visible keeper and against freshly spawned hidden keepers with different payload bytes/sizes (1.5 KiB and 12 KiB), pidfile locations, and decoys, byte-comparing outputs; a wrong-fd read or a name-based (not fd-based) recovery fails. Rubric is small across the board, bucketing to easy.

echo-mantle.notes: hard bucket (total 20). One provisioning script binds several competencies: launch & keep three JVM daemon replicas alive and serve a healthy cluster report over a TCP HTTP RPC port writing /app/status.json; repair DNS/name-resolution and hostname via persistent files; declare a mailing-list config in the canonical /etc/postfix/relay_lists and switch list mail to local delivery (transport_maps + rebuilt aliases); parse/aggregate a provided pcap into sorted 5-tuple network flows; capture the terminal ending text byte-for-byte into /app/answer.txt; persist mailreader's default login shell as /bin/bash. Verifier executes /app/setup.sh plus /app/pcap_to_netflow.py on hidden captures (incl. malformed/truncated), compares flow JSON exactly, and checks byte-identical answer text. dependent_stages=3>=2 and reasoning_depth=3>=2, meeting the hard-commitment rule.

elm-keystone.documented_probe: The 'match a reference behavior under a numeric tolerance' competency (C-8d6b9acc) has a hard floor in its reference form (onnx-style float drift on fixed+random inputs); here the numeric parity is a deterministic integer knapsack objective that must be reconstructed by the same reference algorithm on both fixed and hidden inputs and compared exactly (an error bound of 0, subsuming 'within tolerance'). That specific dimension is simpler than its reference floor, while the sibling exact-format and spreadsheet-cell competencies carry the task to medium.
elm-keystone.notes: Medium. A byte-exact artifact-pack pipeline: the agent must internally solve per-zone 0/1 knapsacks (capacity = 15 + len(zone)) with a documented lexicographic tie-break, compute an integer objective, and emit seven exact artifacts (plan_records.csv, decisions.txt, objective.txt, final_report.csv with exact column set/order, transformed/<zone>.csv files, schema-exact answer.json, and a schedule.xlsx built via the openpyxl cell API at exact addresses). quantitative_correctness=2 (optimal knapsack value + set must match the reference exactly). adversarial_inputs=2 (hidden cases mix malformed/invalid rows, duplicates, boundary slots 0/47 vs 48/-1, and optimizer-value ties that force the tie-break). hidden_case_generalization=2 (verifier re-runs solve.py on three fresh hidden inputs and diffs every artifact). reasoning_depth=2 (knapsack + tie-break + exact formats). Bucket total = 11 -> medium.

elm-ridge.notes: Medium. A reproducible provisioning pipeline: create two named venvs with a specified 3.12 interpreter, install a pinned auto-installed package plus a small package from a local offline index, upgrade a bundled data library from 1.4.0 to >= 2.0.0 to expose an absent keyword, generate gRPC bindings from a proto into the server venv and install a chain-query helper, wire a Jupyter notebook server config, and persist a requirements.lock matching the installed pins. dependent_stages=2 (venv creation -> package install -> bindings/lock; each stage feeds the next). hidden_case_generalization=2 because the verifier re-runs provision.sh from four genuinely different pre-existing filesystem states (absent, partial, stale-downgraded, corrupt) that a robust idempotent script must recover from. adversarial_inputs=1 (stale and corrupt seeds). debugging_ambiguity=1 (interpreter/locator/venv-flag mistakes only show up at runtime). Bucket total = 10 -> medium.

elm-summit.notes: Hard (19/30). The load is integration: authoring a real gRPC AtlasGateway (protobuf service, durable atomic JSON KV store, online status report), launching + keeping alive a background mlflow tracking server on 127.0.0.1:8080, and making the single deliverable generalize to undisclosed cluster configs/ports including a restart/persistence check. Success requires juggling multiple live processes, a correct gRPC round-trip on new input, and exact cluster/capacity reporting. Reasoning_depth and dependent_stages are 3, debugging_ambiguity is 2, so difficulty does not come from prompt length. Nothing is claimed below the competency floors (grpc: medium, cluster-status: easy, mlflow: easy).

elm-terrace.notes: Hard. A multi-stage (dependent_stages=3) model-artifact tuning pipeline: reconstruct a network purely from a state dict's key/shapes (reasoning_depth=3: infer in/hidden/out/blocks; handle both bare and wrapped tensor containers), fit rank-2 LoRA adapters on CPU under a 100KB serialized-model ceiling (resource_pressure=1), sample 1000 rows from the intervened model, emit one out-of-sample prediction per holdout row, produce low-rank factor matrices, and run a @triton.jit kernel through the TRITON_INTERPRET=1 CPU path. debugging_ambiguity=2: exact adapter_config fields (r=2, alpha=8, target_modules, CAUSAL_LM), Triton interpreter vs hardware, strict state-dict load errors. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden architectures vary hidden dim and block count; the verifier re-runs reconstruct.py load on hidden dicts and requires an exact parameter reproduction (hidden_case_generalization=2, quantitative_correctness=2). Difficulty converges to hard, satisfying the hard floor of every bundled slice competency.

elm-yonder.notes: Bucket total 18 (hard). Max competency floor is hard (C-85b852b). Five distinct deliverables must all succeed: link.py coalesces per-module LLVM IR into one linkable all.bc that resolves a genuine cross-module call (C-0c70052d) and carries debug metadata from a -g rebuild of the C source (C-992ec77f); elf.py parses ELF32/ELF64 header + section-header tables honoring endianness and emits an exact address->32-bit-word JSON (C-6c1e4526, C-e1e3902d); sym.py runs a symbolic engine that covers every branch both true and false with generated concrete cases (C-cb07fa86); solver.py accepts a quantifier-free bit-vector SMT-LIB proof-of-work query on stdin and returns a verdict with zero exit code (C-5c5377bf). tool_breadth spans clang/llvm-link/llvm-dis/llvm-dwarfdump, raw ELF binary parsing, an expression parser for the symbolic conditions, and z3 SMT solving. reasoning_depth is high: deriving ELF field offsets/endianness, rebuilding the C source with -g so the IR carries debug metadata, and a correct branch-covering search. hidden_case_generalization is high because the verifier also runs link.py on an unrelated IR pair and elf.py on two freshly-compiled ELF64 binaries, feeds a sat + unsat SMT query pair (an agent that hard-codes 'sat' fails the unsat case), and runs sym.py on a 3-variable/3-gate module. quantitative_correctness covers exact word decoding and JSON equality.

ember-atlas.documented_probe: C-77e2b1a9 (greedy vs sampled deterministic decoding of a language model): the covering task exercises it at medium — verify must greedy-decode exactly 4 tokens deterministically and match a reference generation. Documented probe waiver.
ember-atlas.notes: Single-stage medium task: fetch a pretrained model AND its tokenizer from a live loopback HF-hub-compatible endpoint into the standard cache layout, then prove offline reuse — the verifier shuts every hub server down and re-runs the deliverable's verify subcommand, comparing greedy generations against the reference model. Rubric nonzero for tool_breadth (hub client + transformers cache semantics), reasoning_depth (standard HF cache layout / local_files_only semantics), debugging_ambiguity (offline contract), adversarial_inputs (hollow repo, unknown repo, empty prompt, missing cache), hidden_case_generalization, interaction_statefulness (live server then offline), quantitative_correctness (exact generated text). No dependency chain, no resource pressure.

ember-latch.notes: Single deliverable pair: a headless vim macro script and its computed outputs. Difficulty sits in composing exact vim substitution/macro keystrokes that (a) match the strict row shape (lowercase level, zero-padded date, no '|' in message) without touching near-miss rows byte-for-byte, (b) uppercase a captured field inside the replacement, and (c) support both no-arg (glob the feeds dir) and explicit-argument invocation for hidden re-runs. Byte-exact row fidelity gives a sharp pass/fail edge; medium difficulty.

ember-quarry.documented_probe: C-14f6efb2 (implement a multiple-instance-learning classifier forward pass): reference floor is medium and this covering task is exercised at medium with a fully specified MIL wiring (encoder -> attention gate -> bag classifier) checked on hidden bags including empty and single-instance edge cases.
ember-quarry.notes: Agent wires an instance encoder, scalar attention gate and bag classifier in a fixed order under a fixed seed, plus a CLI that reports logits/attention/pred_class. Hidden cases vary in_dim/hidden/num_classes/seed and probe T=0 and T=1. Exact numeric equality is required against an in-container reference that follows the same deterministic construction, plus structural invariants (attention sums to 1, pred = argmax).

ember-quill.notes: Covering task for C-38bb2e3e (recover deleted/embedded files and materialize byte-accurately into a clean directory). Hard: agent must parse a fully specified custom binary snapshot format (superblock, 128-byte inode slots, extent records), apply layered selection rules (deleted flag, CRC validation, size/extent consistency, highest-version-per-name among deleted candidates), and materialize exact bytes into /app/recovered with nothing extra, plus a quantified JSON report. The tool must generalize to hidden images with garbage slots, stale lower versions, higher versions with bad CRC, extent/size inconsistencies, live-file decoys, and an empty deleted file. Nonzero rubric for reasoning depth (binary format + selection rules), adversarial inputs and hidden-case generalization (>=2 hidden images with decoys), quantitative correctness (byte-exact files + sha256/size/version report), tool breadth (a reusable CLI subcommand), dependent stages (parse -> validate -> select -> materialize), and mild debugging ambiguity (decoy debugging).

ember-spire.documented_probe: ember-spire evaluates a helm-like manifest-merge engine: values precedence (defaults merged with --values layers in order, later overrides earlier, CLI files last), null-deletes-a-key, typed {{ .path }} placeholder substitution, and a per-template array-merge policy table (replace | append | merge-by-key with dotted key paths and deep merge of matching items, including null deletion inside items). The verifier ships an independent reference engine that recomputes canonical outputs from hidden charts and drives /app/render_chart.py through subprocess: the visible case (files re-run into a fresh dir plus the /app/rendered deliverable), hidden charts with 3-layer conflicting overrides, nested merge-by-key conflicts, dotted-key array templates, append-to-absent-path, empty overlays, and a battery of documented error cases (unknown policy, missing from/key/policy, unknown template, missing value path, malformed placeholder, non-list from value, non-list merge target, item missing key, bad values file shape/JSON, bad chart.json, template shape, missing chart.json/templates dir). Every successful case compares the exact emitted file set and canonical JSON bytes; every error case asserts the exact exit code (0/2/3/4) and a stderr token.
ember-spire.notes: Medium. The agent authors a single deterministic Python CLI implementing precisely-documented merge semantics. reasoning_depth captures the interplay of layered precedence, null-deletion, structural substitution and the three array policies including deep item merges with dotted key paths; adversarial_inputs covers empty values, empty overlays, null deletion at multiple levels, and ~15 documented error/edge cases; hidden_case_generalization is high because every output is recomputed by an independent reference engine over structurally different hidden charts, so a hardcoded visible render fails; quantitative_correctness is strict exact canonical-JSON and file-set equality. Low tool_breadth (single stdlib CLI), no resource pressure, low ambiguity because every rule and exit code is spelled out.

ember-wheel.notes: Medium: the agent must locate a single off-by-stride defect in a small C extension, rebuild it as a CPython module, and drive a data-driven harness. Exact 8-hex checksums across empty/single/boundary/duplicate vectors require genuinely repairing the fold loop rather than hardcoding the visible report; hidden inputs (empty vectors, length-2/3 vectors that lay bare which indices are folded, values near the 32-bit ceiling) force generalization. Mixing constants are fixed and documented, so the core reasoning is contained but non-trivial.

escutcheon-cable.notes: Medium. The agent must (a) bring up a live three-process stack (Go backend built from source, Python frontend, span collector) and (b) implement W3C traceparent propagation across two services plus structured JSON logging with a consistent trace_id correlation field and per-request span emission to a local collector. The interesting work is left unspecified: which files to edit and how to wire propagation are up to the agent; the verifier drives single, concurrent fan-out and failing request scenarios with fresh trace ids and asserts parent-child span linkage, trace_id consistency across every relevant log line on both services (proving cross-service propagation), and correct failure-status passthrough. hidden_case_generalization over three distinct request patterns; interaction_statefulness via the live stack and collector state; depends on an ordered bring-up; stdlib-only, so no pip deps and no resource pressure. No destructive surface.

escutcheon-stack.notes: Terraform 1.9.8 (offline filesystem provider mirror for hashicorp/local and null) against hand-managed on-disk config. The agent authors a reusable deploy.sh that adopts arbitrary live/ file sets under Terraform management (content-exact, so nothing is rewritten), adds a deployment.manifest as a second managed resource, and leaves an empty plan. Multistage init/plan/apply; hidden snapshots have different file names, counts and content. Import blocks/terraform import are not the mechanism here because the local provider's local_file resource does not support import; adoption is effectuated by declaring byte-exact content and applying, and the verifier's byte-integrity check is what catches a non-adopting or destructive solution.

fen-lantern.notes: Total 12 (medium bucket 7-17). The chain is: author the multiple-choice task YAML (choices fixed to the model's internal class order, string gold labels mapped through doc_to_choice, mandated prompt template) -> drive the installed fen_eval harness package through a reusable CLI runner -> run the visible fixture and land accuracy inside the [0.55, 1.00] window. difficulty comes from the wiring across YAML/JSONL/JSON plus the silent-failure modes (choice-order and gold-mapping miswires skew accuracy without crashing) and the reusable runner that must generalize to hidden datasets with unmapped/missing labels and empty-token docs. All metrics are recomputed independently from the shipped model and config and must match exactly.

fennel-row.documented_probe: C-19c43363 (produce training output artifacts at an expected experiment data directory): the run must write config and progress data under the exact paths.experiment directory with real, matching content. The verifier deletes each hidden experiment directory, re-runs /app/train.py with a hidden config (different dataset, epochs, seed, and directory), and checks the directory is recreated with a faithful effective-config copy, a full-length finite decreasing loss list, and the model artifact.
fennel-row.notes: Easy: single-stage config-driven trainer with an explicit artifact contract. Small rubric weight for reasoning_depth (config-driven path handling, directory creation), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (fresh hidden configs/datasets), and quantitative_correctness (exact artifact contents). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure.

fern-engine.notes: Hard driven by dependent_stages (a multi-stage lifecycle: cache->offline reuse; train->serialize->reload-confirm->predict; rebuild; reconfigure), by reasoning_depth (reconstructing exact layer/shape/param-name architecture solely from a raw state dict, and slicing a classification head to an arbitrary label count while keeping config in sync), by tool_breadth (torch + transformers AutoModelForCausalLM/AutoTokenizer with local_files_only), and by hidden-case generalization (a different causal LM, a different state-dict shape, a different label count, unseen training data must all work via the same program). Malformed inputs (bad state file, header-only CSV, nonexistent cache, K=0, missing input) are fed and must fail cleanly, requiring defensive validation. Sanity is medium-weight data only, no GPU/resource pressure, so it caps out in the low-mid hard bucket.

fern-hearth.notes: Three independent competencies must all be met for full reward. (1) A git post-receive hook must deploy pushed branch trees to /app/deployed/<branch> (mirroring file trees byte-for-byte, updating in place, removing on branch delete, and safely ignoring non-branch refs while never writing outside the served root). (2) A URL normalizer must convert trailing-slash, query-ordering, default-port and case variants to one canonical form and stay idempotent over malformed/blank lines. (3) Each paper in the bundled index must be enumerated from the HTML and its author-maintained repository resolved by cross-referencing the affiliation org against candidate repo URLs; the mapping is validated by re-parsing all papers, including missing-detail and missing-affiliation edge cases. Reasoning depth is high because the deployed tree must exactly mirror the pushed branch trees (byte-equality), and the paper mapping must be derived from parsing + cross-referencing, not from a visible list.

fern-terrace.notes: Hard bucket (sum=21): brings up a full guest OS under software-emulated QEMU (no /dev/kvm) with a custom assembly-less initramfs, wired hostfwd networking, and leaves the emulator alive as a background service (C-3654b094, floor hard); recovers a marker from a legacy raw disk image by parsing the partition table at a non-trivial byte offset with e2fs tools (C-31e6f8e2, floor hard); and establishes password-based root SSH from the host into the running guest with a successful remote command (C-90061c28, floor medium). The same builder must generalize over hidden profiles/disks of differing offsets, hosts and tokens, so hidden_case_generalization and dependent_stages are high; TCG boot latency and sequential stage ordering drive resource_pressure/interaction_statefulness. Medium floor for C-90061c28 is satisfied; the two hard floors push the bucket to hard.

ferrite-strait.notes: Hard. Dependent_stages=2: the emulated machine must actually be running before the pidfile/cmdline/live-status chain is coherent, and teardown must precede every (re)boot — a broken earlier stage is only diagnosable by inspecting process/listener state. tool_breadth=3 spans qemu-system process management (TCG, -vnc :N display arithmetic 5900+N, -display none/-nic none, no -kernel firmware stage), daemonised background services with pidfiles, idempotent config-driven restart, busybox httpd with a CGI live-status endpoint, and listener-table (ss/netstat) + RFB protocol level verification. reasoning_depth=2: keeping VNC reachable under -display none without a guest kernel, and wiring a CGI endpoint that reflects the live qemu pid at request time rather than a canned answer. interaction_statefulness=3: background VM/web coherence must survive idempotent re-runs across the default and hidden configs (different display/port/paths/titles/markers/mem). hidden_case_generalization=2: three hidden configs re-drive launch.sh and every assertion follows the config. quantitative_correctness=2: exact ports, exact cmdline flags, exact live fields. Covers C-d7f631d3 (VNC on display one + web server on standard port) via netstat/ss listener asserts plus RFB/HTTP/live-status probes.

ferrule-berth.notes: Upstream-clone task (arminbiere/cadical @ c60730422e758ef1cebe7aeddf2dda31c996bf04, version 3.0.1) replacing TB2.1 stp/evalmaxsat. Agent must build the solver with its own build system, then drive it correctly on plain DIMACS CNF and incremental 'p inccnf' (assumption cubes) inputs, emit LRAT proofs for UNSAT instances that the project's proof checker accepts, and report models that actually satisfy every clause. Hidden case 3 has a satisfiable base clause set whose cubes make the joint question unsatisfiable, so solving only the clause part yields the wrong verdict. The image ships only warm object files (no finished solver binary), so the deliverable can only come from the agent running the project's own make; the verifier separately validates each emitted LRAT proof with the project's OWN standalone checker lrat-trim (compiled from the pinned clone into /opt/lrat-trim), so a forged/corrupted/self-authored proof can never pass via the agent's own binary. Rodents: solver must be agent-built in-trial; timeout budget assumes ~2-90 s make relink.

ferrule-keel.documented_probe: TinyCC/tinycc release_0_9_27 (3MB, 399 files, 91,277 LOC, Makefile+configure); clean clone+configure+make+make install measured at ~5s at 1 CPU; project's own 'make tests2.all' suite passes in ~0.5s on the built compiler (glibc 2.39). Build needs one small authored compat patch: bcheck.c used the __malloc_hook ABI that glibc >= 2.34 removed, so a stock 0.9.27 tree fails its default build on this base image.
ferrule-keel.notes: Compiler-from-source task standing in for TB2.1's gcc/CompCert targets. Agent must build the real tinycc tree with its own configure/make (no prebuilt compiler exists in the image, no network at trial time), install it under /app/tccinst, drive it on five C programs, and identify the one program that tcc handles differently from the system gcc: C99 complex numbers, which tcc-doc.texi documents as missing ('Currently missing items are: complex and imaginary numbers'). tcc rejects glibc's complex.h while gcc runs the program. Verifier re-runs every visible program with the agent-built compiler, byte-compares stdout, asserts the documented divergence on hidden cases in both directions (tcc compiles-and-agrees with gcc on hidden standard-C cases / tcc must fail on a hidden complex-numbers case), checks the diagnosis names the feature and cites tcc-doc.texi, and runs the project's own tests2 suite. Substitution recorded: stock 0.9.27 cannot complete its default build on glibc 2.39, so environment applies a small authored bcheck.c compat patch at build time (glibc>=2.34: #undef CONFIG_TCC_MALLOC_HOOKS, falling back to the file's own static-data path); bounds-checking (-b) is thereby disabled, which nothing in the task uses.

flint-anchor.notes: Hard (total 18). Five subsystems of a compiler/runtime toolchain must each be repaired and then generalize: (1) the call-site grouper keys traces by the top three innermost frames and must reproduce exact top-10 counts on hidden traces including <3-frame samples; (2) an RLE free-space GC sweep has an introduced off-by-one that must be located by reasoning about the sweep path (hard floor, debugging_ambiguity/reasoning_depth 3); (3) a template using a post-C++11 relaxed-constexpr body must be ported to strict C++11 while keeping constexpr sums exact; (4) the mkbin tool must assemble emitted IR, link it against a project shared library and produce a runnable executable validated on hidden IR/lib pairs; (5) the ELF section/symbol resolver must parse section headers and resolve names through the symbol string table exactly. The resolver runs on ELFs produced by the IR build stage, hence dependent_stages 2. Hidden generalization is exercised across all modules (hidden traces, randomized+adversarial sweep heaps, hidden static_assert packs, three hidden IR/lib cases, and extra ELF samples); correctness must be byte/line exact. All components are lean (no real compiler bootstrap, no full OS install, no hypervisor): they exercise the same competency slivers through small C/C++/ELF programs.

flint-cipher.notes: Three staged artifacts that each depend on the previous stage (vocabulary filtering -> bounded BPE -> snapshot/re-eval of a multilingual classifier), and the verifier re-runts all three builders on brand-new hidden corpora/splits. Difficulty = 19 (hard bucket). The classifier must generalize to unseen held-out documents and stay above overall and per-language accuracy floors; hidden probes include a required term whose raw frequency is below the threshold, single-occupancy filler words that must be filtered out, an empty-ish tiny corpus, and a document with no usable features.

flint-ember.documented_probe: C-f5ee7735 and C-6ce533a8 reference optimizers are deliberately simplified: the knapsack here is a tiny enumerable 0/1 instance (<=6 projects, unique optimum) rather than an integer-program of useful scale, so the 'optimize' step never needs a real solver. The exactness schema/output contract around the objective is kept in full.
flint-ember.notes: Medium. A single Python pipeline must emit five byte-exact artifacts: JSONL plan records, a decision/NPV text block, a pandas-read CSV with an exact column set/order, a salted deterministic results.json, an integer objective answer, and openpyxl cells at exact addresses. Reasoning about the knapsack optimum plus strict output-format correctness and hidden-input generalization carry the difficulty; no heavy tools, resource pressure, or safety penalties.

flint-fathom.notes: A five-stage video pipeline: (1) HTTP-fetch the mirrored source clip into /app/source.mp4 via a small local mirror server; (2) ffmpeg-trim the source to keep only the trailing 60 frames into /app/clip.mp4; (3) write a pure-CPU frame-analysis script (opencv-headless) /app/detect_frames.py that reports the exact frame where a monocular running subject leaves the ground and the frame where it returns; (4) write /app/extract_commands.py that turns a typed-command session transcript into the ordered verb-phrase commands; (5) emit /app/commands.txt (one command per line) and /app/events.json. The verifier re-executes the two real programs on freshly hidden inputs (three annotated jump clips with clean / never-returns / no-jump scenarios and an unseen transcript) and byte-checks the two emitted files. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages (a working end-to-end DAG from download through trim to event detection and serialization), reasoning_depth (invent a position-tracking detection algorithm robust to a coarse baseline and null/ambiguous flight states), adversarial_inputs (hidden clips that never exhibit a takeoff or never exhibit a landing must yield explicit nulls, plus an all-grounded clip = both null, and a malformed/empty transcript), and quantitative_correctness (exact frame indices), with tool_breadth spanning ffmpeg/ffprobe, an HTTP mirror fetch, OpenCV/numpy and CSV-log parsing.

flint-hollow.notes: Single Flask service: implement POST /triage with an exact structured schema (label = argmax of a per-class confidence object) plus batch CLI mode, then run it on the visible fixture. Nonzero rubric for interaction_statefulness (server lifecycle, request/response probing over localhost), reasoning_depth (tie-break + rounding rules), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (malformed bodies, near-marker words, ties), and quantitative_correctness (exact confidence floats to 4 dp).

flint-mantle.notes: Multi-part deterministic contract: reverse translation, exact FASTA bytes incl. wrapping/newline, self-reported hash, constraint-satisfaction primer selection with tie-break rules, error handling. Every rule is byte-checked on hidden cases.

flint-orchid.notes: Total 20 (hard bucket 18-30), with all four competencies in play. reasoning_depth=3 drives the hardest floor (C-daf5acc4, decode skinned mesh): a custom binary format the agent must reverse from a byte-level spec, including per-vertex stride math (position/normal/texcoord/weights/bones), skeleton parent + bind-pose records, exact npz key/shape/dtype contracts, and clean non-zero rejection of malformed files (bad magic, version!=3, truncated). hidden_case_generalization=3 and adversarial_inputs=3: every one of the four extraction pipelines is re-run on fresh hidden inputs (hidden PDF forms incl. a field without a tooltip label; hidden HTML reports with total-class rows, spacer rows, empty-label cells, non-numeric amounts; hidden RDF datasets incl. multi-membership, duplicate statements, and empty graphs; hidden meshes incl. zero-vertex and large plus three distinct malformed binaries), each compared to an independent recomputation of the expected output. tool_breadth=3: pypdf field enumeration, BeautifulSoup table parsing, rdflib SPARQL execution, and numpy binary decoding in one task. quantitative_correctness=3: exact sorted JSON array equality, exact row indexes, exact result-tuple set membership, and exact float/u8/u16/i16 array equality. dependent_stages=3: each deliverable chains a reusable tool that must be written correctly before the data artifact can exist, and the visible results must reproduce when regenerated from tools/hidden inputs. All names, byte layouts, table structures, and datasets are invented for this task.

flint-terrace.notes: Hard (total 19). The single deliverable /app/solve.py must run on any scenario directory and emit seven interdependent artifacts. dependent_stages=3: a consolidated catalog is built by (i) a client-side COPY bulk-load, (ii) a direct byte-level B-tree salvage of a truncated SQLite file, and (iii) an auto WAL replay, then all three merge in id order before derived queries run. debugging_ambiguity=3 / adversarial_inputs=3: the truncated file can have its data page partially removed (or entirely absent) and the WAL is only recoverable by replaying the journal from a writable copy; the SQLite record layout (serial types 7 vs 6, leading NULL slot behind an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, interior vs leaf pages) is easy to mis-handle. hidden_case_generalization=3: three distinct hidden scenarios probe a large salvage, a slash-1 page (empty salvage), domain/HAVING filtering, and dialect rewrites. quantitative_correctness=3: every recovered/salvaged/summary/fixed row set is compared exactly (floats rounded to 6). The one EASY competency (create-table with a prescribed schema) is not a drop from any floor: the task floor is hard (bundle includes an aggregate-HAVING competency whose floor is hard), so difficulty.hard is the correct bucket.

flume-oar.notes: Slot-based concurrent memoization cache (Go/bench-base:ubuntu-24.04, golang-go 1.22). The shipped cache is lock-free; the data race is only visible under `go test -race` (the race detector trips on unsynchronized slot accesses; values stay correct in the plain run, so the tool is the discovery instrument). Requires (1) zero race reports across the suite run 5x under the detector, (2) hidden-case correctness under three distinct concurrency shapes (hot-slot contention, skewed compute latency, wide aliased key space), (3) a throughput floor vs a baked-in serialized reference: flume_ratio >= 2.5, which rejects the naive 'wrap everything in one global lock' fix (~1.0) and accepts a compute-outside-lock double-checked design (~8x). Reference serial.go and the visible test sources are checksum-protected. Thread pools: none beyond Go's runtime; tests pin GOMAXPROCS themselves; cpus=1.

flume-quill.notes: Go module dependency upgrade with a breaking API change. The fixture is a real multi-package Go repository (cmd/, internal/app, internal/engine, internal/state) with a git history, pinned to urfave/cli v1.22.14 with a green suite. The agent must upgrade two major versions to urfave/cli/v3 (v3.11.0), migrate every call site (NewApp->Command literal, Run gains context.Context, Commands become []*cli.Command, flags become pointers, actions take (context.Context, *cli.Command), NewExitError->Exit, and the v3 ExitErrHandler/os.Exit trap in tests), and keep go build ./... and go test ./... green. The module cache is pre-populated with the v3.11.0 graph at build time so the upgrade works offline. Verifier asserts go.mod carries the v3 module, build and tests pass, and two hidden Go test cases exercise the new API shape (one self-contained, one against a fixture state directory of pre-made run records). reasoning_depth=2: understanding the breaking API and the ExitErrHandler behavior; debugging_ambiguity=2: compile errors from the new API plus the os.Exit-on-ExitCoder trap; hidden_case_generalization=2: hidden tests only compile and pass against the migrated API.

flume-schema.notes: Hard. The agent writes the executor loop of a tool-calling system against a shipped mock platform (6-tool JSON-schema registry, deterministic scripted model, deterministic tool store). Dependent stages 3: every stage feeds the next — shape check -> unknown-tool -> schema validation -> idempotency replay check -> execute-with-retries -> snapshot, and each step's feedback message determines the mock model's next emission, so any reordered or skipped stage derails the whole transcript. Reasoning depth 3: replay semantics must be scoped to non-idempotent tools (idempotent tools return live state and must re-execute), the retry policy must be silent and bounded with backoff read from runtime.protocol, and the exact-error protocol (six feedback types, canonical strings from the shipped validator) must be followed verbatim. Adversarial inputs 3: transcripts deliberately throw malformed emissions, schema type/boundary failures, out-of-range arguments, unknown tools, duplicate non-idempotent calls, and a transient retryable gateway failure; one hidden transcript scripts a model stuck repeating a schema-invalid call to blow past the step budget, so the loop must stop on step_cap. Hidden-case generalization 3: verifier re-runs the loop on the visible transcript and 3 genuinely different hidden transcripts and requires the exact tool-call sequence, exact error strings returned, exact termination reason, and exact final store state. Debugging ambiguity 2: the instruction specifies outcome but not the implementation or where a divergent loop goes wrong. Interaction statefulness 2: the loop must thread a stateful deterministic tool store and a message history across up to 16 turns. No resource pressure, no dangerous actions.

frost-latch.notes: Author a C scanner from a precise spec (weights tokenizer with comment stripping, dual PGM magic P2/P5 with 2-byte big-endian sample support, fixed weights-then-image argument order, three-line stdout contract with tie rules) and build it with a Makefile. Verifier rebuilds from source, checks the ELF, and executes the binary on four hidden cases plus wrong-argc / missing-file / determinism probes. Rubric total 11 -> medium.

frost-link.documented_probe: Parametric mechanical-part geometry engine (bolt-circle spacer/flange): the agent authors an importable pure-Python cadmodel module (bolt-hole centers, edge clearances, annular area, volume, mass, validate_spec, build_report) and a rounded JSON report for a visible spec. The verifier imports /app/cadmodel.py and re-runs every function on hidden specs (bolt counts 1/2/12/24, tiny margins, planted multi-code violations, boundary-touch cases, malformed values, float-vs-int bolt counts, missing keys) under three limits variants, plus an independent recompute of /app/spacer_report.json.
frost-link.notes: Medium: quantitative_correctness 2 because every reported number must match an independent recompute to 4 decimals under exact documented conventions (angles, overlap handling, rounding, sort order); hidden_case_generalization 2 because hidden specs span edge shapes and limits variants so hardcoding the visible report fails; adversarial_inputs 2 from malformed-field specs (strings, bools, negative/zero values, float bolt count, missing keys); dependent_stages 2 because the module and the JSON report must agree with each other and with the verifier. No tool breadth or resource pressure: pure stdlib math, single-digit-second runtime.

frost-marrow.documented_probe: C-5ef2ad28 (combine values from reference clues to produce an expected payload): second independent covering task. The recipe is scattered across three artifact files (serial base, pricebook, movement ledger); the verifier executes the deliverable on hidden artifact directories and compares stdout to an independent reference derivation.
frost-marrow.notes: Single-stage reconciliation: read a base value, a price table with comments/duplicates, and a movement ledger with a header, unknown labels and malformed rows, then combine them into a wrapped 5-digit payload. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (three interacting formats + signed-mod wrapping), adversarial_inputs (messy rows, unknown labels, non-integer serial must fail cleanly) and quantitative_correctness (exact payload). Buckets to easy.

frost-quay.notes: Offline-model-export bench (medium, total 11): the agent authors /app/export.py that loads local HF checkpoints with the platform's PREINSTALLED pinned torch 2.13.0 / transformers 5.16.1 stack (offline env flags, fixed probe sequence, exact report schema incl. runtime version strings and a float checksum). The core trap is the deprecated legacy downgrade bundle in /app (legacy_stack.txt + refresh_legacy.sh pinning torch==1.8.1/transformers==2.3.0): installing it changes API signatures and breaks the export contract, and the verifier enforces the pinned baseline both via importlib.metadata versions and the pristine toolchain_pins.json runtime cross-check (unsafe_action_penalty=1, adversarial_inputs=1). The verifier executes the deliverable on the visible checkpoint and on hidden checkpoints constructed at verify time with different seeds/sizes/layer counts/vocabs (hidden_case_generalization=2), comparing against an independently computed reference (quantitative_correctness=2). Tool breadth covers transformers/torch/offline-hub/JSON plumbing (tool_breadth=2).

fume-anchor.notes: Single-stage: combine four scattered artifacts (KEY=VALUE env with comment/last-wins rules, a slot table with exact-name matching, a markdown note hiding the prime, a roster whose active lines are counted) into one integer payload via exact modular arithmetic. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (four interacting rules), adversarial_inputs (comment decoys, near-miss names, duplicated keys/slots), hidden_case_generalization (verifier runs the program on hidden state dirs), and quantitative_correctness (exact payload). No tool breadth, dependency chain, or pressure; buckets to easy.

fume-latch.notes: Apply a supplied per-line defect-repair order over an HTTP fix desk within an exact fix budget: one accepted POST /api/fix per work-order entry (order may be shuffled and may include a redundant no-op entry), then commit and persist the receipt. Over-budget attempts flip the session to budget-exceeded and fail the run, so retry/duplicate loops are punished. The verifier re-runs the delivered client against fresh hidden sessions (shuffled order, missing trailing newline, redundant entries, single- and multi-defect plates) and independently checks the plate bytes, the receipt sha256 and the session status. Rubric marks: dependency chain (read order -> fix -> commit -> receipt), tool breadth (HTTP client), adversarial inputs (redundant entries, exact byte content), hidden generalization and statefulness (fresh ports/sessions, sticky budget).

fume-marsh.notes: Single-stage: fit a sklearn linear classifier on a CSV whose last column is the target, serialize with joblib, and emit a manifest. The competency C-2dc20425 (verify registered model serialization and parameter shape) is the core: the verifier reloads each persisted model and requires an sklearn.linear_model class whose coefficient vector length equals the dataset feature count, across hidden datasets with 1/3/7 features, plus a malformed-input negative case. Small nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (shape bookkeeping), adversarial_inputs (bad-cell rejection), hidden_case_generalization (varying feature counts), quantitative_correctness (exact manifest/shape agreement). No tool breadth, dependency chain, or environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

fume-wheel.documented_probe: Claims-adjudication engine: the agent implements /app/adjudicate.py (a stdlib CLI) plus the visible report /app/adjudication.json. The verifier first executes the CLI on the visible fixtures, then runs an independent recomputation inside /tests/hidden/adjudicate_probe.py that replays the CLI on hidden (policy, claims) bundles — a single-day leap-day window (2024-02-29) with day-before/day-after denials, aggregate exhaustion mid-id-sort with truncated partial payment then aggregate_exhausted zeros, duplicate ids resolved by stable original-line order (mixed approved/denied same-id rows), zero-amount claims mapping to ['eligible'], a two-cent claim where the documented coinsurance floor (1.5 cents -> 1) differs from any rounding scheme, exclusion precedence over the window check, and an all-denied set — comparing exact decisions, payable_cents, full reason-code lists including order, and aggregate totals. Any deviation, including a hardcoded visible answer, fails.
fume-wheel.notes: Medium: the pipeline has five dependent stages in a documented order (eligibility with exclusion-over-window precedence, deductible, explicit floor at the coinsurance step, per-claim cap, annual aggregate applied in stable ascending-id order with mid-sort truncation), producing exact integer outputs and machine-readable reason codes whose ordering is graded. Quantitative correctness is the dominant dimension (exact cent arithmetic, floor vs round-half-up trap on the two-cent claims, exact-boundary truncation); hidden bundles add adversarial shapes (leap-day, duplicates, zeros, all-denied) so a hardcoded visible output fails, yet the task is pure stdlib with no resource pressure or tool breadth.

furnace-tide.documented_probe: C-c3adcbc5 (achieve memory-efficient near-linear scaling on large bags): the competency's reference floor is medium and this task exercises it at medium — the verifier fully checks the capability (chunked streaming forward over a 1.2M-patch stress set with a hard 400 MB peak-RSS cap and wall-clock deadline, plus exact score recompute).
furnace-tide.notes: Streaming inference under resource pressure: forward a frozen numpy MLP (Linear(32->16), ReLU, Linear(16->1), sigmoid) over trace sets of up to 1.2M patches, aggregating per-trace mean anomaly probabilities. resource_pressure=3: the verifier measures the scorer's peak VmHWM (cap 400 MB) and wall clock (150 s deadline) on a generated 1.2M-patch stress set — a full read_csv or whole-array materialization peaks around 1.2 GB and fails, while chunked aggregation runs in seconds. hidden_case_generalization=2 (string trace ids in unsorted first-occurrence order; a 3000-trace set). quantitative_correctness=2 (per-trace scores compared against an independent streamed recompute within one 4th-decimal unit). adversarial_inputs=2 (header-only, missing columns, non-numeric features, awkward chunk boundaries). No dependency chain, no interaction/unsafe surface.

gale-bridge.notes: Five-tool dev harness (Jupyter notebook, Vim plugin, gawk, jq, shell orchestrator). Several independent deliverables, each exercised by the verifier on genuinely different hidden inputs: awk top-k across frames including ties/short frames/blank and header-only inputs, jq record transforms (empty tags, all-dropped, ordering), Vim plugin layout introspection in fresh headless sessions with varying window counts, and a shell orchestrator whose subset mode must be awk-only via PATH (python forbidden). Difficulty driven by cross-tool breadth, exact-output correctness, and hidden-case generalization; the awk medium/Vim medium floors set the bucket to medium.

gale-fathom.notes: Hard. A single idempotent provisioner (/app/provision.sh) that must stand up, in one chained pipeline, a pinned Python venv with a runnable CLI and exact function values, a pinned (24.9.2) Miniconda plus a conda env with a specific requested python (3.11, deliberately distinct from the 3.12 system) whose packages pass functional checks under `conda run`, a non-interactive git/nginx/openssh stack (no systemd, so the web server is started and probed over HTTP), a self-contained uv project whose deps resolve offline from the local index, and bash+zsh login init that auto-activates conda. dependent_stages=3 (conda install -> conda env -> in-env package install; each feeds the next, plus venv/uv/services in parallel chains). tool_breadth=3 (venv, conda installer+env, apt non-interactive, uv sync, pip local index, shell init, nginx start). reasoning_depth=2/debugging_ambiguity=2 (version-pin correctness only surfaces at runtime across three interpreters; conda version and env-python checks are exact). adversarial_inputs=2 (wrong-pin venv, wrong-python conda env, purged services, missing uv/shell). interaction_statefulness=2 (provision.sh must recover the full spec when re-run from each genuinely different pre-existing state). Bucket total = 18 -> hard.

gale-jetty.notes: Hard (rubric total 18). The task is a staged data-close-out pipeline with several competencies that share a hard floor. The agent must (1) relocate documents under /app/inbox into per-class ledger dirs and empty inbox (exact hash-set equality, any leftover fails), (2) iterate EVERY masks.csv row (never a sample) producing one prompt line and one SAM-style per-row mask grid, (3) ship a runnable extraction engine /app/extract.py that actually writes /app/mart.npy with a strict orientation (Nx3, dense-recovered matrix), (4) reuse the sequential iteration constant by importing ITERATIONS from compute_seq via compute_parallel (any inline restating fails an import-evidence check), (5) parse heterogeneous fixtures (csv + json + parquet) into one schema, cross-check fiscal figures to flag the single inconsistent fee, and (6) filter+rank candidate descriptors by proximity to a target within an inclusive tolerance, sorted by a normalized proximity score. Correctness is validated with exact float/structural assertions (quantitative=3). The verifier re-derives every expected output from the raw fixtures on the visible data and on 3 hidden scenarios that change amounts, drop formats (e.g. parquet-only, csv+json-only), reverse rectangle corners (out-of-order coords that must be normalized), test an inclusive tolerance boundary, and shrink to a zero-row input (adversarial=3, hidden_case_generalization=3). The pipeline is strictly staged (docs -> masks -> parse -> mart -> sheet/mismatch/rank) so dependent_stages=2. No resource or interaction pressure.

gale-keystone.notes: Eight interlocking deliverables: an HTTP service whose reservation endpoint must reject malformed bodies with 400+message while a deliberately picky management control path only answers a crafted request carrying the exact media type and admin header; a reservation CLI that must call the live API and persist venue+company; a solver that floors the reported objective to an exact single integer; and a value object whose hash must be re-derived from the value without breaking equality or the instance cache. The picky endpoint, the hidden malformed-body matrix, the hidden reservation re-run, and the value invariants (dedup-by-equality, hash==hash(key), distinct values distinct) are each enforced by independent checks, so a task missing any competency fails the verifier. Difficulty is driven by endpoint-discovery ambiguity, multi-stage orchestration, and invariant preservation, not by prompt length.

gale-latch.documented_probe: None. This is the second independent covering task for C-8034934c (fix cython source for numpy 2.x api compatibility); the reference task basalt-mantle embeds the capability as one of seven repairs, while this task exercises it in isolation end-to-end (diagnose removed APIs, port setup.py and .pyx, produce an offline build script).
gale-latch.notes: Single focused port: the vendored Cython package fails to build because setup.py uses numpy.distutils (removed in numpy 2.0) and gridcore.pyx calls PyArray_FromDims (removed C API). Agent must diagnose, port both files without changing rms/scale semantics, and leave an idempotent offline build script. Verifier executes port.sh, re-runs setup.py independently, greps that the removed APIs are gone, and probes the compiled module on hidden numeric edge cases (zero-entry grid, negatives, empty vector, fractional/zero factors, input immutability). Medium: debugging_ambiguity (build failures must be diagnosed from errors), tool_breadth (setuptools/Cython/numpy build plumbing), one dependency chain (sources -> build -> import), quantitative_correctness on hidden values.

gale-ledge.documented_probe: C-799768c6 (run a focused test subset of a scientific package and iterate on the failing ass): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
gale-ledge.notes: Medium. The agent must (1) fix a run-length-compressed GC sweep so runs touching the arena boundary are counted in full, (2) correct matrix-composition fold order in a focused scientific subset, (3) implement an async slurp_tree and editable-reinstall so the installed gale exposes it, (4) drive the col target suite and record its confirmed pass count in a log, (5) make emit_manifest print MANIFEST COMPLETE under the dependency-matrix size cap, all while keeping every src file under a 3000-byte hard cap. Correctness is checked with exact numerical/structural assertions (quantitative=2); the GC bug is easy to 'fix' incorrectly (boundary off-by-one) so debugging_ambiguity=2; the pipeline is strictly staged (install -> col -> suites -> manifest -> report) so dependent_stages=2; solve.py must generalize via a read-only `status` mode over fresh/malformed hidden fixtures so hidden_case_generalization=2. No resource or interaction pressure.

gale-meridian.notes: Hard (total 11). Offline provisioning of an R Jupyter kernel plus the R graph/data-frame packages for causal work. The environment ships R + jupyter tooling but NO IRkernel/jsonlite/data.table: they exist only as vendored .debs under /app/vendor that the agent must install offline (apt/dpkg against local artifacts, resolving dependency ordering), then register a user-level kernelspec with the exact name/displayname from /app/workbench.conf via IRkernel::installspec, and satisfy a kernelspec-integrity invariant (every listed kernelspec has an existing executable argv[0]) by removing a stale broken legacy-r kernelspec — an environment-repair sub-problem with a distinct failure signature (debugging_ambiguity=2). dependent_stages=2 (deb install -> IRkernel importable -> kernelspec registered -> notebooks executable). Deliverables: an idempotent /app/provision.sh (run twice by the verifier; interaction_statefulness=1) and a live /app/workbench_report.json derived from the environment (kernel, argv[0] r_binary, loaded packages, exact R major.minor string; quantitative_correctness=1). The verifier independently re-checks package loading via Rscript, parses jupyter kernelspec list --json, and EXECUTES the visible notebook plus three hidden data.table/jsonlite notebooks through the registered rcw kernel via nbconvert (hidden_case_generalization=1, tool_breadth=2: apt/dpkg, R/IRkernel, jupyter/nbconvert). Distinct from the sibling kernel task: offline vendored-deb install, integrity invariant over ALL kernelspecs, exact-name conf-driven registration, and kernel-execution probes instead of static existence checks.

gale-pier.notes: Hard bring-up task: compile a Linux 6.8 kernel from the shipped distro source into a bootable x86_64 bzImage (config must force serial console/initramfs/devtmpfs, modules off, Werror off so the Ubuntu patched tree builds under GCC 13); provision a guest rootfs whose core binary (static busybox) must carry a content hash the verifier recognizes and which contains named users (bilge, halyard) and a group (spinnaker); boot bzImage+rootfs under QEMU -nographic to an operational shell marker captured to /app/boot-serial.log; and write a software emulator for a documented register machine that reproduces the arithmetic output of a legacy binary, including 32-bit wraparound, ignored invalid opcodes, and ignored truncated tail records, validated on hidden binaries. Everything is idempotent: provision.sh is re-run twice and must leave exactly one of each user/group/busybox; build-kernel.sh is re-run to rebuild a fresh bootable bzImage; boot-qemu.sh and emulate.sh are re-run to regenerate their logs/outputs. Stages chain: kernel build -> rootfs provision -> initramfs packaging -> qemu boot; any earlier failure breaks later stages (dependent_stages=3). Difficulty buckets: cannot be below the hard floor of competencies C-f9215470 (installed filesystem with recognized hashes + account), C-9058a916 (qemu boot to operational login), C-42872b99 (legacy emulator with captured output); reasoning_depth/quantitative_correctness carry the hard load (exact hash, exact marker, exact arithmetic incl. overflow).

gale-quarry.notes: Hard: author a single-source O(n) spatial-binned particle update (counting/COM binning then O(1) per-particle motion with a live scalar recurrence), compile it into serial and genuinely OpenMP builds, and ship a two-mode driver whose report is cross-checked by re-running the binaries. The verifier inspects the OpenMP binary for GOMP_parallel/libgomp (an unthreaded or stub binary fails inspection), demands bit-identical HASH/MOVE across builds, positive MOVE on MOTION=1 scenarios (genuine motion), a 16*N-byte positions file, and schema-exact result.json across hidden scenarios including a degenerate N=4 case.

gale-ridge.notes: Hard (bucket total 20). One orchestrator script must carry a five-stage ML model-serve lifecycle end to end: (dependent_stages=3) offline-cache the pretrained BagNet + char tokenizer, reconstruct the architecture from a state dict and import it, keep every weight/bias tensor shape fixed (the canonical (10,784),(10,10) pair with matching biases), train on synthetic bags while capping the distinct (batch,feature) shapes seen at or below a config cap, serialize to a canonical artifact and reload+re-predict, reconfigure a sequence-classifier head to a custom num_labels, initialize the encoder+classifier to exceed a min-parameter threshold, and keep an mlflow tracking server alive on :8080. reasoning_depth=3 and quantitative_correctness=3 come from the shape-preservation invariant (exact fixed shapes must survive every stage exactly) and the capacity-effect mapping (the correct edit letter is the width edit whose instance-encoder+classifier parameter count strictly dominates the optimizer/epoch/orientation levers, computed live rather than looked up). interaction_statefulness=2 (the mlflow server must survive workflow.py exit and answer an HTTP /health probe; the shape trace is a stateful record of every batch seen). adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=2 (four hidden cases: a cap=1 constraint, a cap=2 with different num_labels, a corrupt un-loadable artifact, and a malformed config the pipeline must degrade gracefully from). Bucket total = 20 -> hard, floor of the hardest claimed competency (distinct-shape-limit, hard floor) is met.

gale-slate.notes: Single-stage: build a reusable AST-based static analyzer that recognizes eight vulnerability patterns in Python web-service source and maps each to the exact CWE id, with safe look-alike distractors (parameterized SQL, shell=False lists, literal eval/redirect/system, sha256, json.load). Must generalize to hidden modules (module-level code, classes/methods, nested functions, mixed patterns). Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (eight syntactic rules + scope attribution), debugging_ambiguity (literal vs non-literal edge rules), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (multiple hidden sources), quantitative_correctness (exact CWE ids). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to hard.

gale-vault.notes: Web-http-contract hardening task in three chained stages: (1) a hardened canonical_header (reject CR/LF/NUL + blank/control-character names by raising ValueError while preserving the canonical title form for every valid header name), (2) a Flask REST service implementing a schema-documented upload/list/detail/render contract with strict structured query/path validation (400 on missing, non-integer or negative limit/id; structured 404 not-found carrying the offending id), (3) a stored-XSS payload that survives the shared blacklist sanitize() and auto-fires an alert when the verifier loads the live /render output in the headless Chromium the tests launch. The bucket is hard because the highest competency floor (C-1d626fbd) is hard: the header canonicalization must balance control-character rejection against preserving correct canonical strings, and the whole chain must hold end-to-end against hidden inputs. dependent_stages=3 (canonical_header -> API validation/storage -> render + headless browser); adversarial_inputs=3 (hidden header-name matrix, poisoned-header upload, hidden query/limit 400/404 cases); hidden_case_generalization=3 because the same delivered /app/api.py is re-executed over the /tests/hidden matrices in fresh processes; reasoning_depth=2 to balance valid-preserving vs control-rejecting normalization and to derive a sanitizer bypass that still auto-executes; unsafe_action_penalty=2 since the deliverable deliberately demonstrates a browser-side XSS payload in a sandboxed headless browser.

gantry-budget.notes: Token and cost budgeting (LLM-application gap area): a batch job must summarise a 5000-record dev workload through a billed mock model (1 token per whitespace word, 150-token fixed overhead per request, output billed too). A naive whole-record dump bills 7-10x the declared budget; sending the four judged facts but one request per record still lands 1.5-1.7x over; passing requires field extraction from the record prose plus request batching amortising the per-request overhead, with quality (four exact facts per record, judged by a shipped, public judge) kept above the deployment's floor. resource_pressure=2: the token budget is the measured scarce resource and naive strategies demonstrably bust it. quantitative_correctness=2: the verifier re-derives the bill authoritatively from the ledger prompts and the output file (no trust in job-reported numbers) and enforces cap and floor exactly. hidden_case_generalization=2: three hidden deployments vary record count (1500/2600/4000), budgets (200k/350k/620k tokens), floors (0.88-0.92) and fluff/impact length; the job must read config and size its batching from the deployment it is given. The instruction names the deliverable and the output contract but deliberately leaves the chunking/batching strategy unspecified.

gantry-ember.notes: Hard debugging task in the flaky-test space (the skill-gap wave's item 8). The shipped Python project has a genuine hash-seed nondeterminism: the rotation wheel breaks availability ties with the interpreter's builtin hash() of the member id, which is randomized per process, and it ignores the previous on-call member it is required to exclude. The suite is green ~14/15 of full runs (verified empirically over sampled seeds: 20/300) debugging_ambiguity=3: the failure is invisible in most runs, so the agent must reproduce statistically (repeated runs and/or PYTHONHASHSEED sweeps), distinguish code pollution from test pollution, and confirm the fix across 40 runs. reasoning_depth=3: the root cause is interpreter-level (per-process string hash randomization vs the documented cross-process reproducibility contract) and the fix must preserve the contract, not just the symptom. dependent_stages=3: reproduce -> isolate the one flaky test -> trace the tie-break path -> fix the wheel so the previous member is excluded and the tie-break is deterministic -> re-verify under 40 seeded runs plus 2 hidden source mutants that must still fail. tool_breadth=3: pytest invocation patterns, PYTHONHASHSEED control, git log/blame archaeology over a real committed history, and interpreter-level reasoning. adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=2: the verifier throws two hidden source mutations at the delivered result (a stuck wheel and a silently truncated roster) and requires each to make the suite go red, proof the tests still bite; the composed fix must survive both. quantitative_correctness=1: the suite's count/format assertions (16 tests) must stay exact. interaction_statefulness=1: the wheel threads the previous member across weeks, and the agent's verify loop is an observe-revise cycle. No resource pressure, no unsafe actions. The natural per-run flake rate (~1/15) reproduces the brief's requirement; the verifier pins 40 seeds that deterministically trigger the pre-fix failure so the negative control (untouched container) always scores 0.

gantry-ledger.notes: Medium. The agent must build a reusable eval harness (strict 3-arg CLI, exact metric semantics including the UNKNOWN-never-fabricates rule, outputs that must equal an independent scorer of the same deterministic model to 1e-6) that reproduces a documented prompt trade-off (v1 0.60/0.00 -> v2 0.97/0.19) from raw measurements over the 200-record shipped set, then write a third prompt version that clears a declared bar on BOTH metrics (ref_acc >= 0.95, fabrication_rate <= 0.03) and prove it in a shipped eval report. Difficulty comes from debugging_ambiguity: the agent must diagnose by measurement which prompt trait drives each metric (canonical-normalization wording drives ref accuracy; carrier-completion guidance drives the fabrication regression; the model card documents the later-instruction-wins override), and then decide how to keep normalization while neutralizing the guidance -- the instruction withholds the v3 recipe and only a prompt that gets both traits right clears the bar on the fresh sets too. reasoning_depth (2): distinguishing the two traits and tracing fabrications to their prompt cause. hidden_case_generalization (2): the verifier re-runs the harness on 3 fresh record sets plus a gold-mutated synthetic set with independent re-scoring on every run, so canned or hardcoded numbers fail. The indifference-zone tolerance (v3 within 2pp of v2's ref_rate and within 3pp of v1's fabrication rate, in the better direction; ref_acc >= 0.95; fabrication_rate <= 0.03) is declared up front and can only be met by a genuinely better prompt, never by trimming the bar.

gantry-vellum.notes: Debugging-by-measurement on a long-running service. The shipped /app/enrichd checkout (11 modules, unit suite, git history) is functionally correct: every output field matches the enrichment contract and the unit suite is green. But under sustained load the process RSS grows without bound: the profile cache memoises daily behaviour digests keyed by the raw wire spelling of the client identifier, and collector variants (casing / padding / interior whitespace / per-round ~tag) mean the wire spelling is effectively unique per event, so the unbounded memo grows one entry per event. The digest is a pure function of the canonical (normalised) client and day, so normalising the key (and/or bounding the cache) stops the growth while leaving every output byte identical. The verifier streams four workloads (visible + three hidden with different cardinalities/rounds/days) through the running service batch by batch, samples the process-tree RSS from /proc between batches, and requires the median RSS of the second half of the run to grow less than the declared bound over the first half, while outputs must remain correct and the shipped unit suite must still pass. reasoning_depth 3 (root-causing a runtime trend with no file/line clue), debugging_ambiguity 3 (symptom is a growth slope; the store/call-graph is the only lead), tool_breadth 3 (/proc sampling, process control, stdin-driven streaming protocol, git, unittest), resource_pressure 2 (the measured property IS unbounded memory), interaction_statefulness 2 (the deliverable is a long-running feed-driven process the verifier drives interactively).

garnet-drift.notes: Medium. The agent must build a reusable combined key+certificate PEM bundler that tolerates PKCS#8, traditional RSA and SEC1 EC key formats, skips non-PEM noise, verifies key/cert public-key equality via the openssl CLI (refusing mismatched pairs without creating output), emits key-block-then-cert-block with clean newline separation and mode 0600; and must provision the provided edge service by choosing the key that actually matches edge.crt (a retired decoy key is present to punish blind concatenation) plus a sha256 provenance record. The verifier re-runs the tool on 3 fresh hidden scenarios (PKCS#8 RSA, EC, noisy CRLF input) and a mismatched refusal case, recomputing all expectations with openssl. Rubric nonzero for tool_breadth (openssl CLI), adversarial_inputs (decoy key, noisy/CRLF input, mismatch refusal), hidden_case_generalization and reasoning_depth (public-key matching logic).

garnet-mesa.documented_probe: C-6a19e2d4 (merge duplicate keys with first/last occurrence semantics): the covering task exercises it at easy via the almanac first-occurrence rule and the source priority order; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
garnet-mesa.notes: Single-stage: decode preference/constraint fixtures stored as pickle, base64-wrapped JSON, and plain text; merge them over a TSV roster with a priority rule and resilience to corrupt/missing fixtures. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (three encodings + fall-through semantics), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (corrupt base64, bad pickle entries, duplicate lines, missing files; multiple hidden trees), and quantitative_correctness (exact structured report). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

glacier-basin.documented_probe: the agent extends the bundled mini runner /app/harness/runner.py to (1) shard a suite into K launcher bins via documented LPT (longest-processing-time-first) scheduling with deterministic duration-descending/id-ascending and load/lowest-index tie-breaks, (2) implement bail mode with dependency-driven skip cascades (dep-precedence over bail, transitive blocking, deps-before-dependents manifest order), and (3) emit CTRF-like aggregate + per-launcher reports with exact counts, durations, statuses, shard assignment and skip reasons, then deliver /app/run_report for the visible suite with params.json. The verifier executes /app/harness/runner.py on the visible suite (k/bail taken from the delivered params.json, delivered reports must equal regeneration and the independent recompute) and on six hidden suites (uneven durations, cross-shard dep chains, all-fail, all-pass, K > cases, duration ties) under eleven k/bail combinations, independently recomputing every report file and requiring exact JSON equality.
glacier-basin.notes: Medium: three coupled sub-deliverables (sharding, bail cascade, reports) with an exact-output contract; the correct LPT ordering (duration desc, id asc) and tie-break rules, the dep-vs-bail skip precedence, transitive dependency blocking across shards, and per-launcher/aggregate arithmetic must all be right at once. Hidden generalization is strong: six suites plus eleven parameter combinations, including degenerate shapes (K larger than the case count producing empty launcher reports, every-case-fails with bail, pure-tie durations that bind on id order, a K=1 whole-suite run). Deterministic simulation only; no wall-clock, randomness, network, or resource pressure.

glacier-vane.documented_probe: C-71a2c135 (fetch fluorescent-protein spectral data from an external spectra api): covering task exercises it at full hard fidelity — the client must page a capped per_page catalog, query per-id spectra and status endpoints, and select proteins whose excitation/emission match laser/band windows, with a withdrawn decoy that spectrally dominates until the status filter is applied. Independent cover for zephyr-anchor in a different scenario (multi-channel microscope calibration with pagination + status endpoint vs. single-page donor/acceptor FRET pair selection).
glacier-vane.notes: Single-deliverable HTTP-client stage: start the localhost fixture server, poll /health, page through /api/spectra (per_page hard-capped at 5 so naive single-page clients fail), map /api/status per protein, apply inclusive laser-tolerance/emission-band/brightness filters per channel, and break ties by brightness then id. reasoning_depth=2: multi-constraint filtering plus a deterministic tie-break; interaction_statefulness=2: subprocess server lifecycle with readiness poll on a fresh free port per run; tool_breadth=2: HTTP client + subprocess + JSON I/O. quantitative_correctness=2: payloads must equal the /api/spectra response exactly. hidden_case_generalization=2: verifier re-runs the unchanged client on fresh hidden databases and channel specs. Totals bucket to hard.

glass-forge.documented_probe: C-261fb9b4 (emit a conflict report with per-user field diffs and chosen value): covering task at medium difficulty; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases (empty input, no-conflict input, same-source tie-break, priority inversion, unknown-source rows, malformed records).
glass-forge.notes: Single-stage: parse a JSON roster of multi-source records, group by (user,field), detect genuine value conflicts, pick the winner by fixed source priority with last-in-file tie-break, and emit an ordered report whose total equals the list length. Differs from tundra-orchid Part E: JSON (not CSV) input, three prioritized sources instead of primary/backup, same-source tie-breaking, ordering by first appearance of the pair. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (priority + tie-break rules), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (multiple hidden cases with ignored rows), quantitative_correctness (exact report structure). No tool breadth, no dependency chain; totals bucket to medium.

glass-mantle.documented_probe: C-f254b292 (implement an attention-gated pooling module in pytorch with fixed attribute names): reference floor is medium and this covering task exercises it at medium — three named gate/aggregate layers, softmax-normalized attention over the bag axis, and empty/single-element set edge cases checked on hidden configurations.
