quill-anchor.notes: Single-stage module+CLI deliverable: parse two CSV transport ledgers (comma- or whitespace-separated, blank lines ignored), validate shapes, take the dot product, root-clamp to non-negative, and return the square root as the metric distance. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (two interfaces + CSV parsing), debugging_ambiguity (unrooted-squared-cost is the classic trap; must root and clamp, and surface errors as ValueError/exit 1 without tracebacks), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (negative clamp, zero plan, transposed mismatch, ragged, tiny magnitudes, rectangular, int/float mix), and quantitative_correctness (float distance compared to independently recomputed values). No dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

quill-fathom.documented_probe: C-d1d1b8cb (write and save a reusable fine-tuning script): covered directly and exercised at hard difficulty; the verifier re-executes the delivered script on hidden folds with unseen sizes, class balances and rule perturbations, enforces the fixed base-checkpoint path, snapshot divergence from base, accuracy >= 0.90 per fold, and the documented error contract (missing label column / zero-row fold must exit non-zero).
quill-fathom.notes: Single focused deliverable pair: a reusable fine-tuning script plus the artifact it produces on the visible fold. Scenario (print-shop press-fold threshold drift over a frozen 3-class 16->24->3 checkpoint) is independent of umber-vault's full split/train/predict/bag pipeline. Base checkpoint is calibrated below 0.90 on every fold (0.82-0.91), so copying base fails; a correct capped-epoch fine-tune reaches ~1.0 (oracle-verified on all folds). Rubric: reasoning_depth (training-loop design, error contract), hidden_case_generalization (3 hidden folds with distinct drifts/sizes), adversarial_inputs (malformed folds), quantitative_correctness (accuracy threshold), dependent_stages (artifact must be produced by running the script).

quill-vane.notes: Core difficulty is reading three photographed snippets with exact fidelity (small, low-contrast, speckled images where OCR mangles operators/underscores/digits) and re-implementing them; a single misread character changes the computed value. Three different function shapes (loop+arithmetic, string scanning with modular char arithmetic, weighted list fold with normalization) exercise reasoning_depth; hidden probes re-run the same program with fresh arguments so hard-coded answers fail. Deterministic, no tool breadth, no resource pressure.

quoin-vellum.notes: In the real gensim codebase (cloned and pip-installed -e from /app/src). The agent must write a generic gensim LDA training pipeline that accepts any corpus directory and serialises a model in gensim's own format. The number of latent topics is not given and differs across corpora, so the agent must discover it by tuning rather than hardcoding; the verifier holds out three unseen corpora of different topic counts and scores c_v coherence plus topic-word purity of the serialised, reloaded model. Naive baselines fail at least one held-out corpus (K=1: coherence collapse on some corpora; fixed K or over-split K=10: purity collapse). Serialisation is asserted by reloading the produced file through gensim.models.LdaModel.load(). Medium bucket via hidden-case generalization and quantitative correctness; single CPU with pinned BLAS threads.

raven-anchor.notes: One /app/clean.py pipeline must satisfy eight coordinated sub-tasks (boolean-column-detected grouped aggregation, a fixed-shape period/severity/count table, a nested dept->emp->project graph ordered by key with de-duplication, a category/product-id groupable table, entity filtering resolved across a closed alias/canonical lookup set including direct-owner and owner-name variants, top-5 URL frequency ranking with count ties, an hourly series filled by linear interpolation with leading/trailing boundary fallback, and per-paper two-field JSON Lines records). Hidden cases (a/b/c) exercise genuinely different data: a boolean column whose vocabulary is broken so boolean-column detection must drop it, duplicate/empty/malformed values, a target entity resolved only through an alias variant, single-point and fully-empty series giving boundary fallback and empty-span handling, empty filtered/paper sets, and whitespace/case noise. The verifier recomputes every artifact from scratch with its own reference and requires a full match, so an agent that memorizes the visible outputs fails all hidden runs. Difficulty is hard because the max competency floor across the spec's three competencies is hard (claimed C-f4c1e942 closed-set entity filter carries a hard floor; dropped C-d3c284ae was also hard), forcing the task above the nominal medium target; total rubric 18 (hard bucket 18-30) with reasoning_depth=3, dependent_stages=3, hidden_case_generalization=3, quantitative_correctness=3.

raven-core.documented_probe: XXE vulnerability analysis and remediation across five XML parsing scripts. The agent runs /app/analyze_xxe.py to produce /app/xxe_audit.json (verdicts per parser with canonical reason strings), then patches every vulnerable parser under /app/parsers/ (rejecting external entity declarations and entity chains deeper than the documented max_entity_depth 6) while preserving documented benign extraction on visible and hidden inputs. The verifier independently probes pristine copies at /opt/pristine/parsers with hidden payloads (a file:// file-read probe referencing a hidden secret, recursive-entity probes at depths 12 and 14), requires the audit verdicts and exact reason sets to match those independent verdicts, requires patched parsers to leak no secret bytes and never expand past depth 6 while reproducing the reference extraction byte-for-byte on four hidden benign documents (nested/unicode, CDATA+char refs, flat declared entity, empty root) and the visible samples, and re-runs the analyzer against pristine copies requiring byte-identical regeneration of the audit.
raven-core.notes: Medium: run a stdlib-only analyzer that sandbox-probes five SAX/minidom parsers to classify two documented XXE classes (file:// external entity resolution only achievable when a SAX driver enables external GES plus an entity resolver; recursive internal entity expansion) and then patch each vulnerable parser so probes are rejected/neutralized without disturbing benign extraction. Rubric: unsafe_action_penalty 2 (missed leaks must be caught by hidden probes; verify-then-patch staging), dependent_stages 2 (analyze first, patch after; verifier stage order), hidden_case_generalization 2 (different hidden secrets, two recursion depths, four hidden benign shapes), adversarial_inputs 2 (empty-root, CDATA-with-markup, predefined/char refs, flat entity preserved), reasoning_depth 2 (independent reference extractor, chain-depth policy, defeating hardcoded verdicts), resource_pressure 0, interaction_statefulness 0, quantitative_correctness 1 (byte-exact benign output).

raven-jetty.notes: Total 19 => hard bucket (>=18), satisfying the hard floor of competency C-b45b6939 (author a compact independent C implementation). The task chains four build stages that must all be produced and all re-verified fresh: (1) a static C clone of the recovered 'shoal' byte transform that is rebuilt by test.sh from source in a clean scratch dir (no /app includes, no reference binary) and must reproduce the documented byte-exact transform on hidden binary inputs, (2) wiring the engine's public header directory onto the preprocessor include path (CPATH) so clang resolves <hull/engine.h>, (3) compiling one source under distinct flag sets and instrumentation (fast -O2 -DNDEBUG vs debug -g -O0 --coverage) and reproducing the mode-specific behavior (different computed value, coverage .gcno/.gcda only where instrumentation is on), and (4) repairing the as-shipped toy compiler so it rejects variable-length arrays (a feature it genuinely lacks) with a non-zero error instead of silently compiling them. debugging_ambiguity=3: the toy compiler ships with its VLA-rejection guard disabled (the bug is easy to miss because the code path compiles and prints ok), and the build-mode stage requires understanding why only the instrumented binary emits coverage artifacts and what each flag set actually changes. dependent_stages=3: each competency gate is a separate deliverable produced by executing its own script, and the clone rebuild, include-path, build-modes, and toycc hidden checks all depend on the agent having produced working sources/scripts first. adversarial_inputs=2 (hidden inputs include empty and NUL-bearing binary fixtures, macro/non-literal VLA sizes, and fresh build-mode start/end ranges); hidden_case_generalization=2 (the clone is rebuilt and re-run on hidden inputs; build-modes runs with fresh arguments; toycc is recompiled and probed with hidden VLA and non-VLA sources).

raven-mantle.notes: Hard (bucket total = 20). One executable adapter (/app/infer.py) must carry the full self-play inference close-out end to end: (dependent_stages=3) load the offline causal LM+tokenizer with local_files_only, reconfigure a seq-classification head to a variable custom count and save it, run a causal-LM forward with a loss floor, apply the bag-MIL forward (encoder + attention gate + classifier returning logits + unit-sum attention which survives even a malformed empty bag), apply the policy/WDL head forward (legal-move logits + post-softmax outcome vector), and bundle a streaming request log into aligned micro-batches under four metric thresholds. Quantitative correctness=3: the loss-txt must equal the reference that 'averages over micro-batches' to within 1e-3 (the trailing short micro-batch makes naive full-set averaging wrong), the reconfigured head config must carry the exact count and give a (1,count) forward, and every /app/engine byte must stay byte-identical (hashed vs build-time manifest). reasoning_depth=3 : correct grad-accumulation rescale plus feasibility reasoning for all four batching thresholds at once. adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=2: three hidden cases re-run every mode with different geometries (bag/state sizes, class counts, request streams), plus edge/malformed inputs (empty bag, zero legal-moves, single stripped request, head count 1) which must remain valid. Bucket total = 20 -> hard, meeting the hardest claimed floor (C-1ca974ef, hard).

raven-orchid.notes: Hard bucket (18/30). Four dependent stages with real tool breadth: ingest.py must run a local HTTP server, fetch+sha256(url)-name media, drive ffmpeg for audio extraction, cover with the bundled vosk ASR model, and normalize transcripts; stack/peaks/animation each implement a precise numeric/structural contract. reasoning_depth=3: exact deterministic hashing, ASR pipeline correctness, stable tie-breaking peak ranking, and declared-vs-actual keyframe consistency must all hold simultaneously. hidden_case_generalization=3: 4 hidden scenarios re-execute all four programs on fresh inputs. quantitative_correctness=3: exact sha256 filenames, exact descending-magnitude bin order, exact stacked arrays/shapes, exact shape strings. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden cases include blank URL lines, ?query strings, 404 URLs, audio-with-no-video, EMPTY/INCOMPATIBLE TIFF dirs, negative/overflow/zero k, zero/negative counts, and invalid-JSON animation specs. Max competency floor is hard (C-f39f2732, C-7c5452ae), so the derived bucket is hard.

redoubt-gate.notes: Hard. The agent receives a Maven project whose JUnit suite dies at runtime with NoSuchMethodError on com.example.formatter.Formatter.format(String, char). Two versions of formatter are reachable transitively through different paths (lib-y -> formatter 2.0.0 at depth 2; greeter -> conventions -> formatter 1.0.0 at depth 3) and Maven's nearest-wins rule picks 2.0.0, which dropped the char-fill API. Everything is offline: /opt/m2repo is pre-seeded at image build time with the five com.example artifacts (authored clean-room for this task, sources shipped at /app/libsrc) plus the JUnit 5.11.4 stack and pinned lifecycle/dependency/enforcer plugins. The agent must reason about Maven's dependency resolution (depth rule, dependencyManagement vs exclusions, effective model) and make the resolution structural in pom.xml. The verifier is multi-stage: (1) deliverable exists; (2) merges two hidden JUnit suites into src/test exercising exactly the previously-missing filled-text format API and the greeting path end to end, then requires `mvn -B -o verify` green with the hidden classes genuinely executed (surefire reports parsed, >=5 tests, 0 failures, GreetingTest may not be deleted); (3) runs `mvn -B -o dependency:tree` and requires exactly one com.example:formatter version, 1.0.0; (4) adversarial: copies the project, surgically restores the conflict (strips formatter exclusions, strips dependencyManagement overrides, re-adds a direct formatter:2.0.0 edge) and requires `mvn -B -o validate` to fail, proving a maven-enforcer rule that fails the build if the conflict returns. No network, cpus=1, no resource pressure, no unsafe actions.

reed-haven.documented_probe: C-ac4a9918 (declare the mailing-list configuration in the canonical file): covering task at the documented medium floor; the verifier fully exercises the capability (config must live at the fixed /etc/listd/config.toml path and actually drive the list manager on hidden command streams; a config anywhere else is refused).
reed-haven.notes: Two-stage: author an idempotent provisioning script that installs the canonical listd config (normalized roster from a messy sign-up sheet, closed/open flags, member caps) and replays the visible stream to produce the roster report. Hidden cases replay unseen administrative streams through the daemon with the agent's canonical config (closed-list refusal, cap enforcement, duplicates, moderator posting, case normalization, malformed commands) plus a wrong-path refusal proof. Small rubric nonzero for the provision->report dependency, reasoning depth (normalization + check-order rules), debugging ambiguity (idempotency + daemon exit codes), adversarial inputs (malformed stream lines), hidden generalization, and quantitative correctness. Totals bucket to medium.

reeve-gate.notes: Upstream-clone family slot reeve-gate (stand-in for TB2.1 sudo-project/sudo). Pinned shadow-maint/shadow v4.11.1 (commit eccf1c569c7ac3b9e3b535c91b6ed3c329e9ec8c) is cloned, autoreconf/configure/make/make-installed at image build time (measured 1m28s at cpus=1, so build_timeout_sec=1800 has >10x margin); the expensive build is a cached image layer and the agent's work is incremental on top of it. The built suite replaces the distribution's account tools at canonical paths; a build-time sha256 snapshot (and the fact that dpkg -V passwd now flags those files as modified) is how the verifier asserts the agent used its own built binaries rather than the distro's. The agent writes a data-driven state engine /app/setup_accounts.sh; the verifier restores pristine /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/group /etc/gshadow from /opt/reeve-gate/pristine and replays the deliverable against 3 hidden scenario fixtures with exact end-state assertions (uid/gid/gecos/home/shell, sha512 password hashes verified with python crypt, lock state, aging fields, expiry epoch, supplementary memberships, home/path/marker ownership and modes) plus an exact-account-set check. No PAM: built with --without-libpam so classic /etc/shadow auth. gpasswd group-password setups were dropped because they require a tty at runtime. Operating the built toolchain is ENFORCED at runtime (review hardening): each deliverable run is traced with strace and every create/write/rename/unlink of /etc/passwd,/etc/shadow,/etc/group,/etc/gshadow must be attributable to one of the shadow binaries built from the pinned source; a python direct-DB editor scored reward 1 before this and reward 0 after. Gaps closed at review: single-'>' and python open('w') DB writes that the old grep-only scan missed are now caught statically (recursive over /app) and, decisively, at runtime; verifier timeout raised 600->900 so 3x240s replay margin holds. Direct hand-editing of account DBs is forbidden and detected; the instruction never names the tool design or script structure.

river-ferry.documented_probe: Exercises the  multi-objective evolutionary optimization capability: the agent authors a deterministic stdlib-only NSGA-II CLI (fast non-dominated sorting, crowding distance, binary tournament, crossover/mutation with feasibility repair, external elitist archive, exact hypervolume) for two documented problem families: a bounded knapsack with (value, -weight) objectives and continuous problems with closed-form Pareto fronts (f2 = 1 - f1^2; 3-objective f3 = 1 - f1^2 - f2^2). The probe runs /app/nsga.py on three hidden params files (different seeds, sizes, including a 3-objective case) and independently recomputes objectives from the returned encodings (feasibility + exact/rtol match), checks mutual non-domination and exact hypervolume consistency, then applies per-problem quality gates: knapsack hypervolume >= 0.85x of an independent same-seed reference NSGA-II run; saddle IGD-to-analytic-front strictly below 0.9x the median of 5 random-search fronts of identical budget; triplane documented front property (mean|f1^2+f2^2+f3-1| <= 0.05, max <= 0.25, spans >= 0.6) — plus a static check that the core NSGA-II components exist.
river-ferry.notes: Medium: implement a complete NSGA-II from scratch in pure stdlib with strict reproducibility (single random.Random(seed) stream), exact objective recomputation, exact 2D/3D union-of-boxes hypervolume, and problem-specific quality gates. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (dominance/crowding/archive/tournament design, closed-form front reasoning), debugging_ambiguity (no per-run oracle; only property-based grading with float tolerances), adversarial_inputs (hidden seeds/sizes and a 3-objective problem with a documented front property), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden param sets spanning all problem families; hardcoded visible fronts and single-objective optimizers fail), quantitative_correctness (exact knapsack objectives, exact hypervolume, IGD metric, tight thresholds). Low tool_breadth/resource_pressure: stdlib-only and sub-second-to-few-second runtimes.

river-ledger.notes: Medium. Sequential replay of a JSONL journal with duplicate suppression, correction-reset semantics, and a rich malformed-input set. Hidden cases force a general, runnable program (executes-deliverable). Debugging ambiguity and adversarial-input handling carry the difficulty; no heavy tools, I/O pressure, or safety constraints.

rose-frame.documented_probe: C-13d03a72 (produce byte-identical converter output across independent runs): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
rose-frame.notes: A compact procedural renderer task. Difficulty comes mostly from required generalization to arbitrary hidden scenes (the tool is re-run on multiple fresh inputs) plus byte-exact correctness: the deliverable must run, be a reusable program, handle clipped/off-canvas/zero-size/adverse geometry, respect painter order, and emit a deterministic P6 PPM matching the reference under binary byte comparison. Cannot be passed by copying a scene-specific answer, so fixed-output cheating is structurally impossible.

rust-bazaar.documented_probe: C-d1d1b8cb (write and save a reusable fine-tuning script): the competency's reference floor is hard and this task exercises it at hard — the verifier fully checks the capability (base-snapshot reuse by shape, capped CPU fine-tune, changed loadable snapshot, fold accuracy >= 0.90 on unseen hidden folds, graceful non-zero exits).
rust-bazaar.notes: Single deliverable pair: a reusable fine-tuning script plus the artifact from one visible run. The script must (1) load a pretrained Linear(24->48)/ReLU/Linear(48->3) state_dict identified by tensor shape regardless of parameter naming, (2) fine-tune on CPU within a capped schedule (<60 epochs), (3) emit a new loadable snapshot that differs from the base, (4) generalize to hidden folds whose labeling rules are independent of the base rule and of each other, each reaching accuracy >= 0.90, and (5) exit non-zero with a stderr diagnostic on missing columns, zero-row folds, or non-finite features. Rubric: hidden_case_generalization=3 (three hidden folds with independent rules), adversarial_inputs=2 (malformed/empty/unbalanced-schema folds), quantitative_correctness=2 (accuracy bar plus snapshot validity/differs checks), reasoning_depth=2 (shape-based loading + adaptation), dependent_stages=1 (script -> artifact chain), debugging_ambiguity=1. No resource pressure, interaction, or unsafe surface.

rust-orchid.documented_probe: : systematic test-case generation via the Category-Partition Method over a TSL-like specification. The agent must implement the documented frame-generation algorithm (base choices per strategy, [default]/[single]/[error] property rules, constraint repair by minimal deviation with lexicographic tie-break, canonical frame order, frame_limit truncation, and the documented unsatisfiable-with-reason result) as a CLI, and produce the visible frames.json. The verifier recomputes frames with an independent implementation for the visible spec and three hidden TSL specs (conflicting constraints, all-single parameters, an unsatisfiable combination) under several hidden params.json files (both strategies plus a frame-limit cap), compares exact JSON, re-checks byte determinism across repeated runs, and probes the documented exit codes on malformed specs/params.
rust-orchid.notes: Medium: the core is a single self-contained Python deliverable implementing a multi-part deterministic algorithm (parse TSL with properties/values/ranges; strategy-dependent base and default-fill computation; constraint satisfaction via documented minimal-deviation repair; canonical grouping base/single/ordinary/error; unsatisfiable handling; id renumbering under frame_limit). reasoning_depth and debugging_ambiguity are moderate because the exact semantics (fill vs base, exclusion of non-base singles from repair, lexicographic tie-break) are documented but require careful reading and cross-checking against the visible fixture; adversarial_inputs covers malformed specs/params exit codes plus degenerate all-single and unsatisfiable specs; hidden_case_generalization is high because the deliverable must generalize to unseen TSL specs and params variants (hardcoding the visible 9-frame output fails every hidden case); quantitative_correctness enforced by exact JSON equality against an independent recompute and byte determinism between runs.

rust-quay.notes: Covering task for C-ce46ee62 (reverse a single-key byte transform to recover the valid WAL). Medium: agent must recover the XOR key from the WAL magic (both checksum-endian variants allowed), invert the transform over the whole file, and replay never-checkpointed rows from the restored WAL via SQLite. Dependent stages (decode then extract), mild reasoning (unique-key argument over 256 candidates), adversarial awareness (SQLite may checkpoint/delete the -wal if opened in place; the tool must operate on copies), quantitative correctness (byte-exact WAL, exact JSON rows). Hidden cases use different keys, lengths and row sets; a hard-coded tool fails. No resource pressure or statefulness.

rust-quill.documented_probe: Covering task for C-446b41c3 (compute the sqrt wasserstein distance from the transport cost). Distinct from iris-terrace: standalone freight-desk module+CLI with a single rooted-distance deliverable and root-clamp/negative-dot probes, instead of one section of a multi-part numerics fitting task.
rust-quill.notes: Single module + CLI: dot product of plan and cost, clamp to non-negative, square root, JSON out. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (metric vs squared-cost distinction), debugging_ambiguity (the classic unrooted bug is the trap), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (zero plan, negative dot, rectangular, larger matrices), quantitative_correctness (exact float distances recomputed independently).

rustic-ledger.notes: Medium. Core is a git-like reachability walk over a content-addressed store combined with a self-hash verification (filename must equal sha256 of canonical payload) and regex credential scanning confined to reachable blobs. Difficulty lives in hidden-case generalization (must handle arbitrary stores) plus adversarial fixtures: corrupt objects, objects stored under mismatched filenames, a dangling or missing refs/HEAD, an AKIA/PRIVATE-KEY-style credential intentionally placed in an unreachable blob that must not be reported. Quantitative correctness is required to recompute digests from decoded bytes and report sorted unique IDs.

sable-codon.documented_probe: C-3f9a7c11 (reverse-complement / strand-orientation reasoning on nucleotide sequences): the covering task exercises it at hard — a misoriented or misordered reverse primer fails every hidden case. Documented probe waiver.
sable-codon.notes: Single-stage hard task: QuikChange-style centered mutagenic primer design over a possibly multi-record FASTA template with variable-length inserts (substitution/insertion/deletion), whole-primer Wallace Tm and GC windows, a three-level tie-break, and a strict ordered error taxonomy. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (strand orientation, 2-D flank search), debugging_ambiguity (tie-break precision), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (six hidden scenes incl. error tokens), and quantitative_correctness (exact sequences, integral Tm, rounded GC). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure.

sable-gauge.notes: Author a reproducible-archive packer: sort members by raw UTF-8 bytes (never locale collation) and normalize all owner/group identity out of the archive (uid/gid 0, uname/gname empty, mtime 0, fixed modes, ustar format) so identical input trees yield byte-identical tar output and a stable sha256 identity digest. Medium floor: deliverable is a runnable packer (/app/pack.py) plus the two artifacts from the shipped tree (/app/bundle.tar, /app/bundle.sha256); the verifier executes the packer on hidden trees whose names break locale collation (uppercase-before-lowercase, non-ASCII UTF-8), with empty files/dirs and deep nesting, and byte-compares archives and digests. Nonzero rubric for adversarial_inputs (collation traps), hidden_case_generalization (two distinct hidden trees), and quantitative_correctness (exact byte equality).

sable-heron.notes: Single-stage with a dependent artifact: write a reusable merge tool, then run it on the visible fixtures to emit the conflict report. Medium reasoning: two-sided normalization (greatest synced_at wins, last-occurrence tie-break within an export), cross-export conflict detection (values differ AND both sources present), and a dated-precedence winner rule with payroll winning ties. Adversarial: malformed array elements, missing/non-string fields, unparseable exports, duplicate rows, solo/agreeing pairs, empty results. Verifier reruns the program on hidden export pairs and checks pairs_considered, total_conflicts == len(conflicts), ordering, entries layout, and winner/winner_export.

sable-hook.notes: Multi-stage binary-re: locate and decode two XOR-obfuscated byte tables in a stripped ELF (objdump/hexdump work), validate the recovered passphrase against the real binary, then RUN the target application with the derived deploy secret so the vault body executes and emits its side-effect file. The verifier deletes the side-effect file and re-executes the runner, cross-checks the app's genuine output, verifies the binary and application are pristine and still reject wrong inputs, and replays hidden probes (self-sufficient runner without the passphrase file, fresh output dir, wrong-secret rejection). Nonzero rubric for dependency chain, RE tooling, disassembly reasoning, statefulness (must really run the app) and correctness; totals bucket to hard.

sable-journal.documented_probe: diagnose-and-repair of a seeded race condition in a concurrent asyncio service. The agent must identify the non-atomic read-modify-write across the simulated slow I/O await in the shipped word-count service (naming the exact read/await/write lines of the pristine original in /app/diagnosis.md), repair the merge into a synchronous critical section in /app/svc/wordcount_service.py, and demonstrate that the documented 40-worker load then matches the sequential ground truth. The verifier independently recomputes expected counts from the deterministic schedule rule (seeded randrange draws, round-robin workers), runs the pristine load generator unmodified, re-runs the pristine original service under the same load and requires it to still corrupt, hash-checks the fixtures, and probes 3 hidden corpus/load configs with different worker counts (24x9, 60x5, 12x25) including blank-line, huge-token, mixed-case and whitespace-padded documents.
sable-journal.notes: Medium: the race is invisible under a sequential run (workers=1 is exact even with the bug), so the agent must reason about cooperative asyncio scheduling to explain why 40 concurrent workers lose increments. Nonzero debugging_ambiguity (bug only manifests under load; exact lost value is nondeterministic), reasoning_depth (interleaving analysis, fix classes: atomic sync merge vs asyncio.Lock), hidden_case_generalization (hidden corpora+worker counts recomputed independently, so hardcoding fails), quantitative_correctness (exact integer equality on every hidden case), resource_pressure (40+ concurrent workers through loopback), interaction_statefulness (shared dict accumulates across many requests), dependent_stages (diagnose -> repair -> verify under documented and hidden loads).

sable-marsh.documented_probe:
C-2dc20425 (verify registered model serialization and parameter shape): reference floor is easy; the covering task exercises it at easy. The verifier loads the persisted model with joblib, checks it is a genuine sklearn linear model, and checks the coefficient vector length equals the input feature count on visible and hidden cases, including a malformed input that must fail cleanly. Documented probe waiver.
C-4d2f3c04 (hit a documented held-out accuracy floor): exercised at easy with a recomputed independent accuracy check at 0.80. Documented probe waiver.
sable-marsh.notes: Single-stage: schema-driven LogisticRegression fit, serialize with joblib, register a JSON manifest. The agent must generalize to hidden datasets with different feature counts (3/4/6) and column names, keep the persisted object a genuine sklearn linear model with coefficient length equal to the feature count, match the manifest, clear a 0.80 holdout floor recomputed by the verifier, and fail cleanly on a missing-target column. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (header-driven feature discovery), adversarial_inputs (malformed case), hidden_case_generalization (4 hidden cases), quantitative_correctness (exact shape/accuracy checks). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

sable-mesa.notes: Single-stage: author a flat-layout setuptools package (pyproject.toml with dotkit package discovery), a dotkit/core.py scalar-product kernel, and a root-module re-export. Medium floor from packaging structure + import-path requirements; hidden cases cover ints/floats/negatives/tuples/empty and a ValueError length-mismatch, so hidden_case_generalization and quantitative_correctness are nonzero. No environment pressure, no statefulness; totals bucket to medium.

sable-orbit.notes: Single-stage: isolate objective.reported among decoy fields and persist its integer part (floor) as exactly the digits plus one newline; byte-exact match punishes float formatting or stray whitespace. Hidden cases probe fractional floor-down, exponent notation, already-integral values, and sub-unit values. Small rubric nonzero for adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (four hidden reports) and quantitative_correctness (exact byte match). No tool breadth, dependency chain, or environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

sable-prism.notes: Medium: the agent must pip-install the vendored (not pre-installed) prismval harness offline, author the JSON task wiring (ordered choices list plus a gold_map that translates the deliberately scrambled label-codebook into choice indices), write an argument-driven eval driver, and run it so the visible baseline lands exactly on the independently recomputed accuracy window. The failure mode is mis-wired choice order / gold mapping, which collapses accuracy to near chance (0.03 vs 0.94 on the visible set), far outside the window. Hidden cases generalize the driver to fresh datasets with skipped rows (missing ids, out-of-range codes), empty and unknown-token texts that fall back to the class bias, and tie-breaking by model class order.

sable-quill.documented_probe: C-f01d36d3 (expose required entry-point functions under required names): the verifier regex-checks the obliged definitions at line start in the R source and re-runs both entry points (numeric hidden cases, error edge, reproducibility, self-test exit/PASS) in fresh R processes. Verifier fully checks the capability.
sable-quill.notes: Single-stage data_science task: author an R module exposing tide_estimate/tide_selftest under exact names (line-start regex), a seeded exponential Monte-Carlo estimator with argument validation, and a recorded PASS/FAIL self-test log. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (seeding/validation contract), adversarial_inputs (error edge cases), hidden_case_generalization (fresh n/rate combos in fresh R processes), quantitative_correctness (estimate vs 1/rate); buckets to medium.

sable-ray.notes: Hard single-focus reverse-engineering task: a compiled, source-free C target (/app/target/raycaster, built at image build time from an aux source removed from the image) renders a two-stage scene operation on a heightmap - a horizontal median-of-3 despike with clamped windows, then a west->east raycast shadow pass with slope-1 clearance falloff and STRICT comparison, emitting 'LIT <count>' plus a #/. mask. The agent must recover every semantic detail purely by probe grids and/or objdump/gdb (median window+clamping, ray direction, exact falloff, strict-vs-tie behavior, exact output bytes) and reimplement it in pure Python that matches byte-for-byte on hidden grids probing ties, descending-by-1 ramps, edge spikes, W=1/W=2 rows, 0/255 extremes, and 512-wide grids. Differs from calm-hearth's RE subtask (3x3 blur convolution, space-separated integer output): different operation class (morphological filter + ray march vs linear convolution), different output contract (mask art + summary line vs integer grid), and the reimplementation is pure-Python-only (no native invocation). Rubric total 15 -> hard; reasoning_depth 3 (two interacting passes + strictness corner), debugging_ambiguity 2 (multiple plausible models fit partial probes), quantitative_correctness 2 (byte-identical output).

sable-vellum.notes: Wire a 3-way multiple-choice classification task into an installed micro lm-eval harness: author the YAML config (choice order defines gold indices, so a wrong order or gold mapping collapses accuracy far below the graded 0.60-0.95 window), write a generic HTTP dataset driver, and produce the visible result over loopback HTTP. The verifier re-runs the driver on hidden corpora served over HTTP and recomputes every metric independently. Rubric marks: dependency chain (config -> driver -> served run), tool breadth (YAML + HTTP + harness import), reasoning depth (argmax/tie/skip semantics), adversarial inputs (skipped labels, empty text, decoy columns, case folding), hidden generalization and quantitative correctness (exact recomputed metrics), statefulness (loopback server lifecycle).

sable-wharf.documented_probe: : online learning for a nonstationary multi-armed bandit with delayed feedback and abrupt drift. The agent writes /app/policy.py (a Policy class with choose(t, history) and change_point_estimate()) plus /app/eval_report.json. The verifier re-implements the documented seeded bandit simulation independently, re-runs the policy on the visible fixture and three hidden parameter sets (no-drift, three-way rotation, long per-pull delays, different K/seeds/drift steps) and requires regret <= max(0.50 * static_baseline_regret, 0.10 * T) per case, where the static baseline always pulls argmax(pre_probs) and the oracle best-arm schedule is recomputed from the reward matrix. The report must recompute exactly (cumulative/oracle/regret) against the visible re-run and its change-point estimate must match the policy hook and lie within 250 steps of the true drift_step; hardcoded visible fixtures crash or overshoot on the hidden sets.
sable-wharf.notes: Medium: the core skill is delayed, out-of-order reward attribution plus drift adaptation (restart/sliding-window reasoning) with a quantitative regret bar that discounts the naive always-initial-best baseline by half and floor-budgets the no-drift trap. Delayed feedback makes local debugging genuinely ambiguous (evidence about past pulls arrives late and reordered), and the hidden sets are adversarial (no drift at all, three-way rotation, 30-70-step delays, varying K). A plain UCB1 policy passes the drifting cases but not the long-delay one; an over-explorer fails the no-drift floor; the visible-overfit shortcut fails hidden K/drift checks. Stdlib-only, deterministic seeded runs, cheap CPU loop (T<=3000).

sable-wicket.notes: Total 6 (easy bucket 0-6). Five audited single-line defects, each located by an exact line number and excerpt; the agent must transcribe one correct fix request per finding and apply them through the stateful patchdeck applier under a hard budget of one attempt per finding (any rejected or extra attempt fails the run). difficulty comes from the precise request protocol (statefulness) rather than from reasoning depth; the delivered library is re-tested on hidden vectors per the docstring contracts, and the log is cryptographically tied to the delivered file's lines.

saffron-chain.notes: Implement a real bounded random-walk Metropolis sampler for a truncated normal and generalize to fresh configs (different support/center/scale/n/seed). Difficulty comes from the statistical-correctness requirements: hidden cases probe support enforcement, heavy truncation (moments far off center/scale require truncated-normal math, not naive untruncated samples), exact retained count after burn-in, and fixed-seed reproducibility. A plausible-looking but wrong sampler (uniform draws, ignoring truncation, or leaking burn-in) fails the moment/count checks, so quantitative_correctness, hidden_case_generalization and adversarial_inputs carry the score. Single self-contained stdlib file; no external deps.

saffron-dial.documented_probe: C-f01d36d3 (expose required entry-point functions under required names): covered here at medium; the verifier discovers the two required R functions by line-anchored regex, then fresh-loads the file and exercises them on hidden survey vectors plus error and self-test cases.
saffron-dial.notes: Two required top-level R definitions discovered by regex, then genuinely executed on hidden inputs (varied log bases, zeros, empty/all-zero/single-species vectors, fractional abundances, invalid-input error cases, and a fresh self-test rerun). Rubric credits the R toolchain, edge-case numerics, hidden generalization, and exact quantitative agreement.

saffron-ember.documented_probe: C-d1d1b8cb (write and save a reusable fine-tuning script): reference floor is hard; this covering task requires a reusable CLI fine-tuner that reloads a shape-identified deployed snapshot, adapts it to previously-unseen drifted folds (accuracy >= 0.90 where the base scores near chance), writes new valid checkpoints, refuses over-cap epochs and malformed folds, and never mutates the base artifact.
saffron-ember.notes: Drift-adaptation fine-tuner: the base model (built into the image, trained on last season's water-mass layout) scores ~0.33 on the drifted folds, so a copy-the-base or dummy-snapshot solution fails the 0.90 threshold; genuine SGD adaptation within the 30-epoch cap is required. hidden_case_generalization=2 (two unseen drift regimes with different fold sizes), adversarial_inputs=2 (missing label column, zero-row fold, non-numeric feature, --epochs over cap must all exit non-zero), unsafe_action_penalty=1 (the base snapshot must remain byte-identical), quantitative_correctness=1 (accuracy threshold + printed metric), modest reasoning_depth/tool_breadth (torch stack, CSV handling), dependent_stages=1 (load base -> fine-tune -> save).

saffron-loom.notes: Two-stage: write a reusable CLI exporter, then run it on the visible fixtures to produce the delivered JSONL. The competency (filter one locale subset, export requested columns as JSONL with exact row count/column names) is checked at medium floor: two dataset shapes (bare array vs {'records': ...} wrapper), missing/non-string/wrong-case locale rows, missing columns emitted as '', empty dataset, zero-match locale, exact row count and column order on every hidden case. Rubric nonzero for dependent_stages (program + delivered artifact), reasoning_depth (two shapes + field-absence semantics), adversarial_inputs and hidden_case_generalization (4 hidden cases), quantitative_correctness (exact rows/columns). No tool breadth, resource pressure, or statefulness; totals bucket to medium.

saffron-mesa.notes: Fit a multinomial Naive Bayes model from a CSV corpus (exact tokenization, Laplace smoothing, priors) and persist it to a pickle file at a fixed path. The verifier reloads the pickle and checks the exact dict layout, sorted class/vocab lists, and smoothed log-probabilities against a reference, then re-runs the deliverable on hidden corpora (different class set, punctuation-only documents). Nonzero rubric for the fit-then-persist chain, adversarial empty-token documents, hidden generalization, and numeric correctness.

saffron-quay.notes: Single Flask service with an exactly-specified lexicon classifier: label tie-breaking (positive/negative/mixed/neutral) plus add-one-smoothed per-class confidence rounding, one batch-scoring CLI mode that must generalize to hidden inputs, and HTTP contract details (content-type gate, 400 error bodies, health endpoint). Nonzero rubric for tool_breadth (HTTP server + CLI), reasoning_depth (tie-break + smoothing arithmetic), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (empty text, ties, punctuation/case, malformed requests), quantitative_correctness (rounded float confidences), interaction_statefulness (live server polled by the verifier). No dependency chain or resource pressure; totals bucket to medium.

saffron-rune.documented_probe: C-57f213ee (featurize SMILES strings into model-input arrays; min difficulty hard): the task demands a byte-exact reproduction of a published multi-stage tokenization + rolling-hash featurization (bracket spans, two-letter tokens, invalid-character and unclosed-bracket zero vectors, positional binning) exercised on three hidden SMILES lists plus a catalog-derived features.npz. The covering task exercises the capability fully on hidden cases.
saffron-rune.notes: Single-stage: implement the exact deterministic featurizer and run it on the visible catalog. Hard floor from adversarial inputs (unclosed brackets, whitespace, non-ASCII, tabs, foreign tokens), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden lists) and quantitative_correctness (byte-exact float32 comparison). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure.

saffron-vine.documented_probe: C-4c743935 (LoRA adapter train/save/merge lifecycle): second independent covering task. A corrupted (zeroed) fc2 weight must be recovered by training a rank-constrained LoRA adapter to a holdout accuracy target, persisting a self-sufficient reloadable adapter directory (weights/config/tokenizer feature spec), and merging the adapter into the base weight per an exact equation that the verifier checks numerically. Hard: multi-stage lifecycle, exact merge-equation + freeze constraints, hidden-fixture generalization.
saffron-vine.notes: Distinct from larch-cipher (stalled-head scenario): here the base model's fc2.weight is zeroed by a failed checkpoint restore and the agent must run the full LoRA lifecycle. The verifier executes /app/restore.py on the visible case and three hidden fixtures with different vocab/embed/hidden/seq-len/seed, validates the adapter directory reloads onto the base and reproduces merged outputs, checks the merge equation tensor-exactly, enforces that non-fc2 tensors are untouched, and enforces the >=0.86 holdout accuracy bar. Rubric: dependent stages (train->save->merge->eval), reasoning depth (LoRA math + freeze discipline), hidden generalization + quantitative correctness (accuracy bar and exact merge), moderate resource pressure (CPU torch training).

sage-canyon.notes: Hard (total 18). A staged exploit chain, each stage gated by the previous one (dependent_stages=3): (1) craft a working SQL-injection payload to authenticate as a target account; (2) craft an exact byte-level overflow payload that flips an adjacent gating field inside a fixed struct to a specific magic constant, unlocking the protected branch that prints the lone deployment secret; (3) run the Flask service's authorize_deployment() with that secret so its body actually executes and writes a side-effect grants file; (4) harden /app/app.py so any unknown /lookup/<id> returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body and no HTML or stack trace. Reasoning is threefold (reasoning_depth=3): deriving the SQL tautology (easy) and C struct offset/magic-constant layout so the 20-byte payload lands exactly on the gate (quantitative=3, exact bytes and exact value), and the 404 hardening. The overflow symptom is ambiguous: an underrun or wrong-length payload prints only locked, so the agent must infer the buffer/field layout from source alone (debugging_ambiguity=2). generalization=3 because the verifier replays the payload against several target accounts, re-runs the deployment check against a fresh hash verification, and hits a battery of malformed/special-case not-found IDs (adversarial=2, ids with spaces, dots, SQL-ish text, long strings) that must not 500. Hard floors: C-1f4f846b requires actually running the app to emit the side-effect file (hard); C-1aefef55 and C-9c9c34df are medium. Correctness is numeric/exact (magic constant 0x9E1C, sha256 digest match, exact 20-byte payload).

sage-keystone.notes: Hard bucket (total 19). Three independent extraction sub-tasks the verifier re-runs on fresh fixtures: (1) a pypdf form-field enumerator re-run on three hidden forms (with-label, one with NO /TU label, and one with zero controls); (2) a rdflib SPARQL walk from Recruit->firm running on two hidden graphs with decoy triples (un-named recruit, un-typed seconded entity, firm with no name, duplicate secondments requiring DISTINCT), asserting exact result-variable binding; (3) a byte-faithful skinned-mesh decoder compared against an independent struct/numpy reference read of the same binary across three valid layouts and one torn/malformed file that must fail cleanly. reasoning_depth + dependent_stages of three chained independent competencies drive the hard bucket; generalized hidden inputs in every gate require runnable deliverables, not one-shot answers.

sage-wharf.notes: Hard (total 18). The crux is the range coder (C-e41d6ebb, floor hard): the agent must implement the exact 32-bit arithmetic-coded decoder AND an encoder that inverts the decoder's reads bit-for-bit (the renorm high/low update order is the classic off-by-one trap), confirmed by an encode->decode round-trip on unseen bytes. reasoning_depth 3 and debugging_ambiguity 3 come from the renorm boundary conditions and the greedy interval-split selection; hidden_case_generalization 3 from fresh blobs, round-trips, layers, WAL transforms and digest inputs; quantitative_correctness 3 from byte-exact decode and exact digest. Adversarial 2 via empty/0x00/0xFF-run blobs, noise and short WALs, empty pay/command. resource_pressure 0 (small fixtures, stdlib only).

scupper-lock.notes: React 18 data-table component on bench-base:node-22 (first frontend task in the suite): sorting, filtering, controlled/uncontrolled selection, grid keyboard navigation and a documented prop API. The verifier renders the deliverable under jsdom with @testing-library/react across 4 hidden prop/data fixtures (distinct datasets and prop combinations from the visible fixture), asserts DOM roles, ARIA attributes and event payloads, and strict type-checks 2 hidden consumer files against the exported prop types. All npm deps are pinned and baked into the image; no network at trial time.

scupper-sail.notes: Hard. A static-architecture CSS task with no renderer in the image: the agent authors /app/dashboard.html and /app/styles.css from a written spec and correctness is decided by a tinycss2-based cascade resolver that (a) parses the stylesheet into media/container/plain layers, (b) resolves declarations per hidden viewport fixture (media bands, container-width bands from engine-reported widths, selector specificity, source order, custom-property inheritance and recursive var() substitution), (c) asserts media-query structure (exact (min-width:1280px)/(max-width:767px) conditions cross-checked against the --scupper-bp-* properties), container-query structure (blocks at 480/720/960px targeting the right classes), the 14 named --scupper-* custom properties with exact values and var() consumption, and the specificity ordering of .sidebar.open over .sidebar, and (d) checks the HTML vocabulary. dependent_stages=3: HTML instantiation, sheet parse, media layer, container layer, specificity, and var resolution are each necessary. reasoning_depth=3: the agent designs where each declaration lives (base vs media vs container layer) so that three viewport regimes and two nested container contexts (stats resolve against the sidebar, cards against the card-grid) all resolve to the contracted values, including source-order requirements among equal-specificity container rules. debugging_ambiguity=3: no browser, no screenshot; the only feedback is normalized resolved-value mismatches, and misplacement, typos in var names, breakpoint literal drift, or a flipped source order each surface as a terse diff the agent must invert mentally. hidden_case_generalization=3: four fixtures covering desktop (1440, container equality at exactly 960px and 480px), tablet (1024, sidebar railed, card-grid 939 < 960), mobile-open (600, open sidebar proving the specificity override), and desktop-mixed (1440 viewport with engine-reported 460px sidebar / 880px card-grid: an expanded media band over sub-threshold containers, so viewport-keyed media approximations cannot satisfy the behavioral table; all four hidden and never shown). quantitative_correctness=2: 4+8, 1+11, 12 column math, and threshold membership at 480/720/960 for widths 640/480/1280/1080/939/600. adversarial_inputs=2: the resolver forgives formatting (case, whitespace, comments, extra rules, unsupported constructs are warnings) but a stylesheet that only passes behaviorally and misses the required media/container structure, a named property, or the specificity ordering fails; boundary fixtures sit exactly on the min-width semantics. Low resource pressure; nothing stateful; no destructive surface.

sedge-hearth.documented_probe: Token-based auth service skill: HMAC-signed JWT-style tokens with claims, expiry, rotation and a revocation blacklist. The deliverable /app/token_service.py is a loopback auth service (login/refresh/logout/me) that must mint tokens byte-identical to an independent recomputation of header.payload.signature (HMAC-SHA256 over the config secret, exact compact claim JSON, per-process jti counter), enforce iat/exp windows with a documented X-Onyx-Now time header and clock skew, rotate refresh tokens (old refresh blacklisted), and persist revocations in /app/state/blacklist.json across process restarts. A hidden flow harness drives the running service over loopback, crafts its own valid/expired/future/tampered/wrong-key/wrong-issuer/missing-claim/wrong-typ/malformed tokens, replays rotated refresh tokens, restarts the process mid-test, and re-runs the whole battery against three generated hidden configs (different secrets, lifetimes, clock skews, users, ports). A hardcoded-response stub fails the recomputed signatures; an in-memory-only blacklist fails the restart probe.
sedge-hearth.notes: Medium (rubric 13): the security contract is exact and checkable (byte-exact token strings, claim order, HMAC recomputation, jti counter), which drives quantitative_correctness=2; adversarial_inputs=2 from the crafted-token matrix and tamper/replay tests; interaction_statefulness=2 because rotation+logout mutate a persisted blacklist that must survive a mid-test restart; hidden_case_generalization=2 because three hidden configs re-run the identical flow battery through the same deliverable, so any config-hardcoding or visible-only shortcut fails. Moderate reasoning_depth for the claim/clock/blacklist check ordering, moderate debugging_ambiguity for boundary tolerance semantics. No resource pressure.

sedge-vault.documented_probe: C-92072676 (connect to a postgres service using compose-provided credentials): the second covering task; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases (different db names, roles, passwords, and stack-file formatting against a live password-authenticated instance).
sedge-vault.notes: Medium: derive host/published-port/db/user/password from a compose-style stack file (nonstandard port 5541, scram-authenticated TCP), connect to the live Postgres, and export the specimens table as JSON. Hidden cases re-execute the deliverable on other stack files (other database, other role+password, noisy multi-service formatting), so hard-coding any connection parameter fails. Rubric nonzero for dependent stages (parse -> connect -> export), tool breadth (psql/postgres client), reasoning depth, debugging ambiguity, hidden-case generalization, quantitative correctness (exact rows/types), and interaction statefulness (live DB).

silt-barrow.documented_probe: C-4a3a4fa1 (selectively stream a single archive member without expanding the whole archive): reference floor is easy and the covering task exercises it at easy; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
silt-barrow.notes: Single-stage: stream one named member (crash.mkd) out of a gzip tar to an output file while a sensitive member (hostkeys.pem) must never touch disk and a coexisting live recorder.log (plus a same-named archive member) must not be clobbered by full extraction. The verifier re-executes the deliverable script on hidden bundles and fails if any non-wanted member is materialized, the archive or live log changed, or the member bytes differ. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (member targeting without extraction), tool_breadth (tar streaming), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (distinct hidden bundles), quantitative_correctness (byte-exact member), and unsafe_action_penalty (sensitive-member materialization).

skiff-berth.documented_probe: C-759c32c0 (enable password-based authentication): the covering task is authored at easy, matching the reference floor; the verifier fully checks the capability (hash generation on hidden secrets, crypt verification of the wired credentials, idempotent re-provisioning, and live HTTP probes of the gateway).
skiff-berth.notes: Easy: generate a sha512-crypt hash and wire it into the gateway's credential file so the configured secret is accepted. The wrong-scheme/mismatch failure mode is covered: the verifier crypt-verifies every hash (visible plus two hidden secrets run through the agent's generator), rejects locked/malformed entries and plaintext leakage, and probes the live server for 401/403/200 behavior. Nonzero rubric: dependent_stages (hash generator must be written, then provisioning run, then credentials consumed by the server), reasoning_depth (correct crypt scheme and idempotent provisioning), adversarial_inputs (hidden secrets, wrong-password/unknown-user probes), hidden_case_generalization (fresh secrets and a re-run). No tool breadth, quantitative, resource, or unsafe-action pressure; totals bucket to easy.

slate-anchor.notes: Configure the legacy plotsmith build so the non-graphical engine compiles while the X11-based frontend and its library linking are excluded entirely (./configure --without-x + make, exact deliverable name plotsmith). Medium: requires discovering the shipped configure/Makefile knobs (docs hint), understanding the two build modes, satisfying the no-X11-linkage check (dynamic section + symbols), and running the engine on jobs. Hidden generalization covers clipping edges, dense overlaps, malformed job lines, and mid-job clear, byte-compared against an independent reference.

slate-hollow.notes: Covering task for C-4e83076b (inject an init script that enables serial login under an authenticated name): author an injected guest init that mounts the pseudo-filesystems (proc/sysfs/devtmpfs), registers a getty on ttyS0, and provisions a passwordless (unauthenticated) account, then repack the initramfs and drive the serial console. Rubric: dependent_stages (init authored -> repacked -> booted -> login driven -> captured), interaction_statefulness (live serial login session with an emulator), tool_breadth (QEMU TCG, cpio/gzip repacking, busybox userland, programmatic console driving), debugging_ambiguity (getty controlling-tty/setsid, empty-password semantics, prompt timing), hidden_case_generalization (verifier rebuilds the appliance for unseen usernames and independently boots + logs in, checking mounts, uid 1000 and the exact name).

slate-quarry.documented_probe: C-05d7fbec (exploit a misconfigured sudo rule to run a privileged command): the covering task executes the delivered script AS the unprivileged operator, so elevation through the configured sudo rule is the only path to the required end-state; hidden cases re-run it over wiped/stale/idempotency states. Verifier fully checks the capability.
slate-quarry.notes: Single-stage system_administration task: author an idempotent rotation script that mints a seal via the sudo-allowed snapshotctl and destroys a protected ledger via the sudo-allowed shred rule, then writes a labeled report. The verifier executes the deliverable as dana (no root powers), enforces pristine hashes of the sudoers rule and tool, and probes three hidden degraded states. Nonzero rubric for tool_breadth, reasoning_depth (privilege model), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (degraded states), interaction_statefulness (idempotency); buckets to medium.

slate-ratchet.documented_probe: C-aded17a5 (keep the answer independent of a recompiled binary): this task is the covering exercise at hard difficulty; the verifier recompiles the checksum-verified source at -O0/-O2/-Os and grades the answer against every fresh build plus negative controls, so a value that only works against a tampered binary fails.
slate-ratchet.notes: Single deliverable: recover the activation codes by reversing the obfuscated validation logic in the provided C source. The verifier enforces the no-tamper rule via sha256 on the source, rebuilds three fresh binaries, requires ACCEPT on every enabled profile under every build, and requires REJECT on hidden probe codes. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (deobfuscation + reimplementation of the per-profile chain), adversarial_inputs (tamper/negative probes), hidden_case_generalization (multiple profiles + multiple build levels), quantitative_correctness (exact code strings).

sorrel-hasp.documented_probe: None. This is the second independent covering task for C-2d0e9195 (generate and protect a 2048-bit rsa private key); the reference task plum-seal touches key generation only as a sub-step of X.509 certificate issuance, while this task centers the full key-generation contract: exact bit-length policy, unencrypted PEM, explicit 0600 mode under any umask, overwrite semantics, and precise exit codes.
sorrel-hasp.notes: Two-stage: build a reusable validating generator (policy gate on bit size with exit code 2, umask-independent chmod 0600, overwrite semantics) and then actually run it to leave the 2048-bit /app/deploy_key.pem. Hidden cases execute the script on accepted sizes (2048/3072/4096, incl. umask 000), rejected sizes/inputs (1024, 0, negative, non-numeric, 16384) that must exit 2 and create nothing, and an overwrite case. Medium: adversarial_inputs and unsafe_action_penalty (permissions are the core), quantitative_correctness (exact bit length and exit codes), one dependent stage (script then key), tool_breadth (openssl + shell + stat).

sorrel-marsh.notes: Single-stage: group JSON sync records by (user, field), decide conflicts by value divergence, apply a two-level tie-break (recency then device priority then input order) for the winner, and emit a structured report whose total_conflicts must equal len(conflicts). Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (tie-break cascade), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (hidden tie/duplicate/empty cases), and quantitative_correctness (exact counts and winner identity verified structurally).

sorrel-quay.documented_probe: C-e37bcb4d (configure a single-node cluster to listen on a designated port via site/core config files with complementary namenode/datanode functions): covered at easy with Hadoop-style core-site.xml/hdfs-site.xml placeholders and a designated rpc endpoint; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases (textual checks plus live daemons and probes). Documented probe waiver.
sorrel-quay.notes: Single-stage: fill seven designated property values across two Hadoop-style site files; miswritten strings fail the textual check and starve the shipped daemons, which then fail the live bind and hidden probes. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (fs.defaultFS URI encodes the rpc port) and adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (three independent live probes re-read the agent's files). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

sorrel-tide.notes: Format-constrained enumeration probe: honor a compact duty-roster gate (never brute-force the full serial space), apply the exact well-formed-keycard predicate (exact length, required prefix/suffix fragments, uppercase+digits only) to every rostered emission — including near-miss decoys (off-by-one length, lowercase prefix/body, dash separator) and valid tokens riddled with the confusable characters O/0/I/1 that punish over-tightening — write EVERY retained candidate to the result file in ascending serial order, and only then select the unique SHA-256 residue match as the vault keycard. The solver is reusable: the verifier re-runs it unchanged on hidden generator modules with different serial ranges, lengths, fragments, alphabets and pins, and re-derives the expected candidate list and selection independently. Hard: the failure mode is precisely dropping the matching candidate by tightening the format (or guessing the final value instead of enumerating), and the hidden modules break any hard-coded format constant.

spume-ferry.documented_probe: C-9316fd7f (call an http endpoint carrying a computed payload): reference floor is easy and this covering task is authored at easy; the verifier re-runs the deliverable script against the live in-container service on hidden dock ids (open, closed, non-integer) and checks the printed final message against the documented formula.
spume-ferry.notes: Single flow: start a shipped local kiosk service, discover the claim route and receipt list, compute a sha256-based rendezvous payload for a dock id, POST it, and deliver the returned pier-pass string plus receipt JSON. Hidden cases re-execute the script with unseen open ids (catches hard-coded outputs), a closed id (409 -> non-zero exit, no pierpass on stdout), and a non-integer arg. Easy: no multi-step auth, no auditing, straightforward documented formula.

stanchion-bell.notes: Web/a11y remediation on a self-authored React 18 app. The shipped site carries eight real defects spread across shared components (missing labels, wrong role/name on the menu toggle, aside-before-main focus order, no live region on the announcement, colour-only status dots, no skip link, skipped heading level with brand h1, images without alt). The verifier renders pages under jsdom, runs axe-core (WCAG A/AA + best-practice; color-contrast and target-size excluded as unmeasurable under jsdom) asserting zero moderate+ violations, and adds targeted DOM assertions axe cannot see: skip link first, main-before-complementary tab order, role=status/aria-live announcement, textual non-colour-only state, explicit labels (placeholder alone rejected — axe 4.10's label rule accepts placeholder, so this is asserted directly), exactly one h1, every data-declared form control rendered, and every data-declared content image rendered with its data alt. Three hidden pages render unseen data through the same components, so only root-cause component fixes generalize; the oracle repairs the components and proves the visible suite green. Hidden-case generalization is the core difficulty: axe reports 4 of the 8 categories, the other 4 require the targeted contract to be read and implemented. No stateful interaction and no resource pressure: the verifier is a one-shot jsdom render. Medium bucket (12).

stanchion-compass.notes: Medium (11/30). Vite build engineering on a working-but-bloated React app. The shipped app builds and runs but emits one ~1MB entry chunk: all three heavy route views (charts/reports/admin) are statically imported into the entry. The agent must introduce route-level code splitting (React.lazy dynamic imports), configure a manualChunks rule so the react/react-dom vendor code lands outside the entry, and get the statically-reachable initial JavaScript under 400,000 bytes while keeping every route functional. The verifier rebuilds the app itself, parses the emitted chunk graph from dist/index.html (static-import BFS from the entry), asserts chunk count, per-view chunk identity via unique markers embedded in each generated heavy data module, dynamic-import references in the entry, vendor separation via a react-dom internals token, then boots the built bundle in three separate jsdom processes (visible charts route + hidden reports and admin routes) asserting the route chunk is actually fetched and executed (ready-content + DOM interactions driven by the heavy module's own exports). Hidden cases differ: distinct routes, data and interactions. Untouched container fails the byte budget and chunk-count gates immediately. Tool breadth: vite config, rollup manualChunks, React.lazy, jsdom, chunk graph inspection.

tarn-mesa.notes: Reverse-engineer a specified binary container (magic/version/flags header, variable header length with junk padding, optional 2-byte repeating XOR mask over the payload, either float32 endianness, row- vs column-major storage, 4-byte CRC trailer that must not be read as data) and ship a runnable extractor that numpy.saves the recovered matrix. Hard floor: the deliverable must be a general executable (/app/extract.py) plus the persisted /app/recovered.npy, verified by executing it on hidden containers that flip every flag combination (big/little endian, C/Fortran order, masked/unmasked, padded/unpadded headers) and checking exact values, shape, dtype, and orientation. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (multi-field header + mask + order/endianness interplay), adversarial_inputs (trailer trap, junk padding), hidden_case_generalization (flag-flipped hidden containers), quantitative_correctness (exact float matrix equality), and small tool/dependency credit for the two-stage write-then-run flow.

tarn-quay.notes: Medium. Single-stage: merge three snapshot export formats (CSV with RFC quoting, JSONL, JSON array), normalize types (zero-padded id/value strings -> int, whitespace-padded names stripped), skip malformed rows, resolve duplicate ids by min (value, name), and serialize one complete JSON array sorted ascending by id. Adversarial_inputs=2 (quoted/comma names, malformed rows, zero-padding, negatives, empty dir); hidden_case_generalization=2 (four distinct hidden snapshot sets incl. empty dir and reverse-ordered sources); quantitative_correctness=1 (exact content/order match); tool_breadth=1 (csv/json parsing); reasoning_depth=1 and debugging_ambiguity=1 (dedup tie-breaking). No dependency chain, environment pressure, or statefulness; totals bucket to medium. Covers C-5df6a315 (JSON list export sorted by primary key) via distinct asserts on types, order, duplicates, and completeness.

teal-assembler.notes: Core is a two-pass assembler over a fixed 5-mnemonic instruction set: pass 1 must collect labels (including forward references and label-only lines) while computing byte addresses, pass 2 emits byte-exact machine code with packed ADD registers, big-endian 16-bit JMP addresses, and load immediate range checks. Difficulty comes from the sequential label-then-encode dependency (dependent_stages=2), exact byte-encoding correctness (quantitative_correctness=2), and generalizing one program to arbitrary inputs (hidden_case_generalization=2): hidden cases cover forward/backward jumps, r15, hex and 0/255 boundary immediates, and six documented error classes (duplicate label, unknown mnemonic, wrong operand count, register out of range, immediate out of range, jump to undefined label), each required to abort nonzero with a line-numbered diagnostic and no output file.

teal-macro.notes: Single-stage: record a Vim macro register set whose combined getreg length stays at or under a fixed 40-keystroke ceiling while performing a field-reordering rewrite (WORD,NUMBER,WORD -> WORD3 WORD1 (NUMBER)) that must generalize to hidden source files with different values and field widths. The verifier sources /app/macros.vim in a clean headless Vim, checks the buffer was not modified by sourcing, measures the budget via getreg over registers a-z, applies :%g/^/normal @a itself, and compares byte-for-byte against the expected target; a static scan forbids functions/autocmds/maps/interpreter bridges so the work is genuinely done by the recorded keystrokes. Rubric nonzero for quantitative_correctness (exact output bytes and hard budget), hidden_case_generalization (three distinct hidden sources), reasoning_depth (very-magic regex economy), interaction_statefulness and tool_breadth (headless vim sourcing mechanics), adversarial_inputs (no buffer edits at source time, no-modify on source.txt).

tenon-orbit.documented_probe: qutip/qutip @ c95e637e0e3f9c0d3279b5fbff2c150e0de6bf9a (tag v5.3.1, annotation = commit). Build on bench-base:python-3.12 requires build-essential (qutip compiles C++ extensions) + numpy/scipy/cython pinned, then `pip install .` off the shallow clone. Measured cold build at 1 CPU: ~285 s wall (apt + wheels + qutip C++ build), image 1532 MB (runs as uid here; -e installs a normal byte-compiled package so import is offline-clean). sesolve on the Rabi model matches the closed-form reference |<1|exp(-iHT)|0>|^2 = (w^2/W^2) sin^2(W T/2) to ~6e-6 worst case across the chosen hidden parameter sets, so a 2e-4 tolerance is safe.
tenon-orbit.notes: Upstream-clone scientific-computing task (v4.2 family), the quantum-python shape standing in for TB2.1's jcmgray/quimb. Clones qutip/qutip pinned and installs it from source at /app/src. The agent must write /app/quantum_dynamics.py that builds the driven two-level Hamiltonian H = -(delta/2) sigmaz + (omega/2) sigmax with QuTiP operators, evolves |0> to time T with a QuTiP solver, and prints the excited-state population P1(T). The verifier refuses any deliverable that does not import qutip, build qutip operators and call a QuTiP solver (grep-level check), then runs the deliverable on 3 fresh hidden parameter sets and asserts the printed P1(T) matches an independently computed closed-form Rabi-flopping reference within 2e-4. An agent cannot pass by writing a fresh numpy script that ignores the clone: numeric correctness against the closed form alone is not enough -- the deliverable must genuinely use the installed qutip package's machinery. The instruction fixes the physics, the CLI and the output contract but not which solver to use or how to express the operators, so it exercises finding the qutip API in the real /app/src tree.

tern-delta.notes: Focused single-competency task: produce a probability array over a fixed vocabulary meeting both forward- and reverse-KL budgets, via the documented mixing-with-uniform halving method. The verifier re-runs the deliverable on seven hidden priors/budget pairs (zero budgets returning the exact normalized prior, length-1, huge budgets, a very tight pair needing many halvings, numpy/list input polymorphism) and validates the visible /app/calibrated.json against the agent's own function. Shape/value failures (wrong length, non-finite, non-positive, unnormalized) are all probed.

thwart-cinder.notes: Hard. Live PostgreSQL 16 with a 3.2M-row two-table analytical warehouse shipped stopped at /srv/pgdata; nothing named about the index columns, the function-on-column defect in the shipped query, or the migration contents. The agent must (a) deliver a start script that boots the cluster under a documented connection contract, (b) design the right index(es) on BOTH fact tables so month-window tenant reports use index-based plans, (c) rewrite the shipped report with semantics byte-identical to the original (grader compares result rows, hashes the untouched original), and (d) write forward/backward migrations that the grader applies forward -> backward -> forward while fingerprinting the table heap files after every step (any row loss fails). EXPLAIN is run on 3 hidden month-window reports over both tables: index-based plans are required after forward AND the same reports must revert to sequential scans after backward (the migrations must be doing real work). A relative execution-time gate (rewritten report >= 3x faster than the original, measured back-to-back on the same host, plus an absolute cap) is host-calibrated and generous (measured margin 9-90x). Resource pressure is real on this box: on a loaded host a sequential scan of the 239MB events heap takes minutes while the indexed month-window scans take ~seconds, and every data check is a checksum of the live table files. Unsafe-action penalty is structural: any destructive migration (bare DROP TABLE, truncate/reload) or data mutation fails the fingerprint checks outright with a binary 0. os: docker host disk is heavily shared; gates are all relative or EXPLAIN-based so they hold under load. hidden_case_generalization=3: three hidden queries with different tenants/months/tables/groupings and a second fact table the agent must generalize to.

thwart-lantern.notes: A shared-main preservation task inside living git repositories. Three scenario repos (tally/stockpile/gatewatch) each start in the same broken state: a colleague's unmerged feature branch was pushed onto origin/main by mistake, so a plain push of the completed local hotfix is rejected as non-fast-forward. The naive fixes (git push --force, git branch -D, rebasing/amending/re-creating the hotfix) each violate one of the five verifier invariants: hotfix-commit and colleague-tip must both be ancestors of final origin/main, every pre-state commit must stay reachable by its original SHA in BOTH repos, workspace main must equal origin main (fully published by an ordinary push), and colleague-added/hotfix-changed blobs must be byte-identical at the final remote main. The verifier derives all expectations per scenario from that scenario's own pre.bundle (cloned with git), so no branch name, SHA, author or path is hardcoded. unsafe_action_penalty=3: the destructive path (force-push to the protected shared main; deleting the colleague's branch) is genuinely available in the environment and is precisely what the verifier punishes. Hidden cases genuinely differ in kind: case1 has three colleague commits and the branch exists only locally (no origin rescue ref, so a force-push orphans the work entirely on the remote), case2 has a different service/version/author set, and both differ in file layout, branch names and commit hashes from the visible fixture. Correct fix is deterministic and conflict-free (disjoint files), so the oracle is a real fetch+merge+push done three times.

thwart-quarry.notes: Medium. The agent implements a live cache layer against a real daemonized redis-server: cache-aside reads with per-key TTL, single-flight stampede protection (N concurrent misses on the same key must cause exactly one backend call), and an atomic compound read-modify-write (debit-if-sufficient) done as one server-side Lua script, enforced both by a static source check and by a runtime EVAL/EVALSHA wire-presence check via redis-cli MONITOR so a spoofed source marker cannot satisfy it. The verifier starts redis from the agent's own /app/start_redis.sh, then drives the workload described in the visible fixture and 3 hidden fixtures (different ports, key sets, TTLs, concurrency, spend budgets) with real threads, asserting exact per-key backend call counts per round, key TTL windows, generation-fresh values (stale data is caught because backend values change every round), and the no-lost-update balance invariant (final balance equals start minus acknowledged debits and never goes negative). interaction_statefulness=2: live daemonized redis (a real service the agent's own deliverable starts per case) whose TTL expiry windows the verifier waits through and whose balance state must survive concurrent mutation across rounds. Failure modes an agent hits: deadlock/timeouts from a broken single-flight lock (thread-hang detection), over-fetching (call count > 1), stale reads across TTL windows, overdraft/lost updates from a check-then-write race, and non-Lua spend implementations (WATCH/MULTI or Python-side GET/SET races fail the MONITOR wire check). Difficulty derives from concurrency correctness (reasoning_depth), debugging_ambiguity (races only reproduce under load), hidden_case_generalization (3 fresh workloads), and quantitative_correctness (exact counts, TTL windows, balances). Low resource pressure; live redis state is confined to a port per case.

tide-ember.notes: Hard. The agent must combine lookup (instruments gain table, unit factor table), parsing (multi-file JSON catalogs with many malformed-record shapes that must be skipped without crashing), descriptor normalization (value * unit_factor * gain, rounded to 6 dp), inclusive-tolerance filtering against a target, and proximity ranking (score = 1 - distance/tolerance, ascending distance with obs_id tie-break), plus a mandatory normalization-reporting string per record.
