The pipeline is a long chain of dependent stages that must stay mutually consistent: learn a BPE tokenizer (vocab + merge rules in the loader's exact formats), train a 300-dim word2vec-style embedding matrix whose rows exactly equal the vocab and are distributionally meaningful (verified by within-class vs cross-class cosine separation on frequently co-occurring anchors), build a fasttext-style linear classifier over mean-pooled word embeddings that clears a holdout-accuracy floor while its serialized model stays under a size budget, emit a per-model metrics table (model, correlation, error, penalty, dof) with internally consistent values, and serialize a Vocab dataclass whose word<->index maps are exact inverses sized to the embedding rows. Difficulty comes from coordinating tokenizer/embedding/classifier/metadata so every invariant holds simultaneously, generalising the whole runner to fresh and malformed synthetic corpora (blank, punctuation-only, digit-only, short, duplicate, and missing-TAB rows), and respecting the accuracy-vs-size budget and verifier time budget. Leaning implementation: a gensim+scikit-learn rapid pipeline stands in for the classic C++ fasttext binary (no compiled-toolchain step), but every competency is genuinely exercised for real.

zephyr-cipher.notes: Five medium-floor DSP competencies chained in one pipeline: exact-parameter scipy STFT magnitude export, wavelength->wavenumber conversion, localized-decimal spectrum parsing, RMS-normalized 16-bit multitone wav synthesis, and vosk mp3->text transcription. Quantitative rigor dominates: STFT magnitudes must equal a scipy gold to 1e-4, wavenumber peak centers to 1 cm^-1, wav RMS inside a band, all requested tones present in the spectrum. Hidden cases vary STFT window/nperseg/nfft/boundary settings, sample rates, spectrum peak counts/wavelengths, tone frequencies/RMS levels, and spoken phrases, so generalization to fresh scenarios is required. Transcription is exercised for real (preinstalled vosk model + ffmpeg decode of mp3), keeping the speech competency honest rather than faked. Sum 13 => medium, matching the medium floor of every competency.

zephyr-engine.notes: End-to-end recovery pipeline: enumerate candidate flare passphrases under the compact commissioned-seed gate (the naive full 24-char alphanumeric token space is hopeless; you must honor the subkey/seed gate and the exact 24-char ZEPH...CORE uppercase-digit format and write every well-formed candidate); select the active vault passphrase via a sha1 hex letter-count structural beacon (K=17); run a password-hash probe of the AES-256 7z to confirm it is a protected/crackable target; crack and extract the member with the recovered password; then a parallel defensive leg sanitizing the leaked credential out of a repo with a reusable scrubber and patching a jar-upload filename filter against traversal and dangerous-extension masks. True to 'hard': two hard-floor competencies (format-constrained enumeration, subkey-seed search-space shrink) require reasoning to avoid an infeasible brute force; the long dependent_stages chain means one wrong password/format/fingerprint propagates to a failed extraction; debugging_ambiguity and adversarial mask/traversal inputs plus hidden scrub dirs drive generalization; quantitative_correctness matters for the exact digest count, exact answer.json keys, and exact decrypted creds bytes. No unsafe actions are demanded and no interaction statefulness is required.

zephyr-forge.notes: Hard (total 19). Six distinct competencies must each be genuinely solved: (1) provision a real MIP solver that reads standard .mps and returns the exact integer optimum (hidden models carry an integrality gap, so an LP-relax-only solver fails); (2) exact weighted MAX-SAT optimum over 2^n assignments with a hard-UNSAT case that must be reported specifically; (3) formulate and minimize a convex quartic + per-vector quadratic penalty + global coupling objective numerically to a near-stationary optimum matching a reference minimizer; (4) enumerate every distinct basic-feasible corner of nonnegative LPs with exact rational arithmetic (duplicate columns, m>n and negative-rhs edge cases); (5) classify solver verdict text using a documented token rule incl. empty-file and case-mixed edges; (6) choose a literal-vs-back-reference segmentation (fixed self-delimiting format) that decodes byte-exact and stays strictly under a byte ceiling that a naive all-literal encoding always exceeds. tool_breadth 3 (HiGHS/CBC MIP, scipy numeric optimizer, exact Fraction linear solve, text classification, custom LZ packing); reasoning_depth 3 (the generalisation contract, the exactness of the optima/counts, and the DP over coding costs in F); hidden_case_generalization 3 (three hidden case dirs probe HARD_UNSAT, empty/to-be-over-255 verdicts, m>n and singular/duplicate corners, tight ceilings, and a fresh MIP with a general-integer variable).

zephyr-gasket.notes: Difficulty total 12 -> medium (matches task.toml 'medium', >= the max competency floor 'medium'). The maze side is a navigation-constrained, feedback-only unknown-maze explorer: the agent may only peek the cell it stands in and move a single cell through open passages, so it must run a real DFS with backtracking over cycles and dead ends within a move budget and reconstruct the full wall map plus a legal path to the far exit. This exercises explore/infer layout, per-id instance targeting, and navigation with constraints. The reference-maze selfcheck (offline known fixture) forces the same flood logic to generalize before it is trusted on the live unknown instances. The game side is mate-in-1 search over a precisely-specified chess subset (K,Q,R,B,N, no pawns/castling): the agent must generate legal moves, filter self-check, verify check, and prove the opponent has no reply, writing all winning moves in src-dest square notation. Every result is equality-checked against an independently re-deriving engine, and hidden cases vary maze size/layout/cycles and game piece/game configurations including zero-mate and missing-opponent-king edge positions (adversarial=2, hidden_generalization=3, quantitative=3). reasoning_depth=2 from the search + legality proofs; a single shared exploration core generalizes across all instances (hidden uncertainty). No heavy resource or interaction pressure beyond the single-file CLI contract.

zephyr-grove.notes: A single reusable scheduling engine must jointly solve three independent deterministic problems from one config: an exact subset-sum counting objective (one-use-only + allowed-number semantics, duplicates handled as distinct elements, negative/zero target gates), a 9x9 Latin-square arrangement serialized to strict two-digit zero-padded row-major tiles, and an availability overlap finder that enforces the weekday business-hours window with a lunch exclusion across every person simultaneously and emits only windows that reach the required duration. Reasoning depth (hard): designing the exact-count DP so duplicates and off-by-one sum handling are right, plus interval semantics (lunch slice, inverted/ignored intervals, exact-boundary inclusion) are easy to get subtly wrong. Adversarial_inputs: hidden cases force a zero-count answer, an all-busy empty plans list, a lunch-gap split at the exact == duration boundary, and malformed busy/multipce entries plus duplicate and non-positive numbers (all of which our daemon must tolerate). Debugging_ambiguity: three outputs must all be correct at once; a wrong assumption in any sub-problem fails an independent gold. Hidden generalization: the grader re-runs the executable on four fresh configs and compares to independent recomputation. Sum 18 => hard, meeting and exceeding the max floor (medium) among the five competencies.

zephyr-helix.documented_probe: C-01d6c7ae is intentionally exercised only through the integrator's discretization choice (atol/rtol/method) required to stay inside the state/right-hand-side budget for randomized initial states; it is not an autonomous full-physics simulation of its own, so that dimension is subsumed by C-5149cd00 rather than graded twice.
zephyr-helix.notes: Hard (18/30). Two independent scientific kernels must be authored from a bare contract and generalize to unseen inputs. integrate.py must numerically solve a linear first-order system under a hard ceiling on RHS-evaluation calls while every grid state stays within a max-absolute-error tolerance of the exact matrix-exponential solution and stays finite; tuning atol/rtol/method to fit the budget is genuine quantitative reasoning. eig.py must select the largest-magnitude eigenvalue (magnitude, not real-part ordering, so complex-conjugate and negative-real spectra are traps) and emit per-index leading principal-minor spectra ordered by magnitude. Both CLIs must reject malformed cases with a clean ERR exit. Hidden-case generalization and exact-output correctness dominate; moderate build/steps make it run cleanly CPU-only.

zephyr-notch.notes: Three chained stages: (1) author a reusable secure eraser that overwrites each file in place before unlinking and finally removes the whole directory tree, then run it on /app/vault to produce /app/erased_ok.txt; (2) consult `man openssl-enc` to identify the exact -aes-256-ctr option and decrypt /app/handoff/msg.enc, documenting the option in capability_notes.md; (3) persist the exact recovered plaintext to /app/results.txt. dependent_stages=3 because the marker emission depends on the eraser succeeding, the decryption depends on the man-page-derived option, and the results file depends on that decryption. tool_breadth=2 for shred/find (erase), man + openssl enc -K/-iv (crypto), bash scripting. adversarial_inputs=2 because the hidden erase trees include dot-files, names with spaces, a read-only file, an empty tree, a broken symlink, and a missing target, and hidden crypto re-runs the documented option on fresh ciphertexts including an empty plaintext. hidden_case_generalization=2 because both deliverable programs are re-executed on unseen hidden material. quantitative_correctness=2 because the final message and the cipher option must match byte-for-byte. unsafe_action_penalty=2: the eraser must never walk out of its target (blast-radius checks fail a wildcard rm), matching the secure-erasure competency's requirement to destroy only the designated tree. Medium floor from competency C-51021b37.

zephyr-orchid.notes: A three-stage media+ASR pipeline is gated stage-by-stage (download must yield a real mp4 before trimming; the ASR model must be unpacked before transcription), spans three tools (curl, ffmpeg/ffprobe, python3/vosk over a local HTTP mirror) and requires numeric content agreement (trailer PSNR>=30dB, transcript strings must normalize-exactly against independent expected text). Hidden cases replay the downloader on unseen fixtures (different durations/resolutions, query-string URLs) and push voice recognition over fresh audio at odd sample rates (44.1kHz) - real generalization rather than output-file guessing. Rubric sum 13 lands in the medium bucket (10-17) and is at least the max competency floor (medium) for C-a13c3ba1, C-361f3946 and C-494accea.

zephyr-summit.notes: Rubric total 20 -> hard bucket, matching task.toml 'hard' and >= the max competency floor (hard, from the formal-proofs competency C-047ea557). The task is a staged toolchain build-out (dependent_stages=3): a clean-room C compiler (zcc, authored for the task, at /app/cc-src) is installed as /app/vendor/bin/cc, /app/sections.txt is derived by compiling a probe with that very compiler and dumping its ELF sections and symbol tables with readelf, the Coq proof module is completed and compiled to a .vo proof object, the Scala 2.11 project is packaged into a standalone assembly JAR (bundle scala-library so java -jar works), and a symbolic execution engine with the z3 constraint solver is implemented and installed on PATH. tool_breadth=3 covers the compiler install/build pipeline (python front-end + as/ld via binutils), coqc, scalac+jar, readelf, z3, and the LLVM-16 toolchain. reasoning_depth=3: completing the formal proofs requires real tactic work (induction; the gauss identity needs polynomial arithmetic that plain lia cannot close, forcing nia/ring), and writing a correct symbolic executor over an IR with ITE path conditions. hidden_case_generalization=3: the engine is re-run byte-for-byte on hidden IRs (including a NO_SOLUTION case), the compiler is re-run on hidden C programs, and sections.txt is byte-compared to a rebuilt readelf dump. debugging_ambiguity=2 from compiler/codegen and proof tactic failures; adversarial_inputs=1 (the NO_SOLUTION engine case and scala arg variants); resource_pressure=2 from the multi-toolchain install/build budget and 1-cpu build. quantitative_correctness=2 for exact numeric outputs (solver models, jar arithmetic, compiled program stdout).

zephyr-vault.notes: Total 15 = medium, at/above the max competency floor (medium). ballast-berm.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on Mbed-TLS/mbedtls at parent commit dd48f0f23f8b5189031d6f3ac519b2b6113bd9e7 (real upstream issue #9314, fixed by 7b6ddfcd25d95a1c6a452158db9205a6372b4426). psa_cipher_decrypt() special-cases PSA_ALG_CCM_STAR_NO_TAG with an extra guard that rejects any nonce-plus-ciphertext input shorter than one AES block (16 bytes), even though this implementation's CCM* fixed nonce is 13 bytes and the only real minimum is PSA_CIPHER_IV_LENGTH; the fix removes the CCM*-specific check so only the IV-length minimum remains (inputs of 13..15 bytes must now decrypt instead of failing INVALID_ARGUMENT, while sub-nonce inputs still error). ballast-bollard.documented_probe: Real upstream tree PyCQA/bandit@7e6f580d (parent of the upstream fix 72fa5a7 for issue #880), shallow-fetched in the Dockerfile, installed editable via pbr, git metadata stripped
ballast-bollard.notes: SWE-bench-shaped debugging task on a real upstream security tool. The seed is the actual upstream bug: bandit/core/tester.py only consults nosec_lines.get(context['lineno']) so a # nosec comment on a non-first line of a multi-line construct is ignored, even though context['linerange'] already carries the whole region. The upstream fix (three small edits: utils.get_nosec scanning the linerange, the tester lookup switched to it, and the blanket-nosec bookkeeping moved from the pre-visit phase to the test phase so the metrics stay exact) is what the oracle ports; a fix that only widens the lookup still fails the golden test's nosec/skipped metrics. The agent gets a repro file, a failing behavior, and the project's own test suites as oracle guides, but no file names and no issue/commit reference. The verifier runs the project's own golden regression test extracted from the fix commit, the project's own unit suite (179 tests) and functional suite (72 tests), plus 4 authored hidden cases that put the nosec on the closing line of % -built SQL, on the closing line inside a sqlite conn.execute call, on the closing paren line of exec(), and on a middle line of eval() -- each case also stripped of its nosec to prove the construct is genuinely flagged. ballast-boom.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on PyCQA/flake8 at parent commit 2a811cc4d2aaed3e8eb5a9f04f08ccc8af7c0791 (real upstream bug, issue #1948). On Python 3.12, when a source line contains an f-string that uses escaped (doubled) curly braces, flake8's string-content redaction step in the logical-line construction path miscounts the braces: an FSTRING_MIDDLE token's parsed text is shorter than the raw token span, so the line handed to logical-line plugins is misaligned, with raw characters leaking in where filler text should be and filler text where code should be. A plugin that reports content extracted from the linted line therefore prints a corrupted snippet. Agent must reproduce, localise and fix the real tree; the verifier asserts provenance (HEAD still the pinned parent, fix commit not reachable from the clone, only source files under src/flake8/ modified, nothing deleted), runs the upstream regression test extracted from fix commit bdcd5c2c0afadaf7c92a4b26d96055cecdd38cf3 into /opt/golden at image build time, runs the project's own full test suite, and runs authored hidden cases over f-string escaped-brace shapes the upstream test does not use (escaped braces alone, adjacent to fields, inside call args, two f-strings on one line, format-spec braces) plus a non-f-string regression guard. Pure Python, offline; ~65 s full suite at 1 CPU in-image. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping.

ballast-brackish.notes: Upstream-clone soundness bugfix in Z3Prover/z3 (v4.2 family): seq_rewriter::mk_seq_nth_i resolves elements of a concatenation by comparing the absolute target offset against the loop index over concat pieces instead of a cumulative character position, so when an ite element is skipped the counters desynchronise, a wrong element is picked, a false equality axiom is asserted and satisfiable (Seq Int) formulas with seq.extract over nested concatenations become spurious UNSAT. Verified in-image at parent 5fcd89bf: reproduction and hidden cases print unsat (wrong); at fix 8fd4b73a they print sat. Upstream's own regression addition to src/test/seq_rewriter.cpp is planted from /opt/golden at verification time (note: that C++ test constructs the concat flat and passes even on the buggy tree; the discriminating gates are the authored nested-concat SMT2 hidden cases, verified parent=unsat/fix=sat). Build is warm in the image (cmake build/ shipped); agent rebuilds incrementally at 1 vCPU. Verifier: provenance (HEAD==parent, byte-identical tree except the one source file), summary.md, planted golden seq_rewriter module (test-z3 seq_rewriter), 3 hidden SMT2 cases expecting sat + 1 expecting unsat through the agent-built build/z3. Oracle applies the authored one-file patch (the real upstream fix).

ballast-caboose.documented_probe: Real upstream tree apache/commons-lang@596269f16d33cd4a20223978c245a15c898c5084 (parent of the upstream fix 1d6ef29ce004309e50bd91e27f0f5e80e1a57a76 for issue #1775), shallow-fetched in the Dockerfile, detached at the parent so the fix commit is out of reach, with the offline Maven repository at /opt/m2repo warmed and the module compiled at build time. ballast-caboose.notes: Easy SWE-bench-shaped debugging task on a real upstream JVM library. ballast-chartroom.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on aquasecurity/trivy at parent commit 3dc5f8768b343a07694ba1cc09425f485d4c1b0f (real upstream bug #10955, fixed by f964fa2bb61e1b59088d2b35397ca8fd39045b00). The conda environment.yml parser replaces version operators with spaces and then indexes the first field of the split; a dependency line made up only of operators ('=', '==') leaves an empty split and the parser panics with 'index out of range [0] with length 0', aborting the whole scan on a harmless malformed entry. The image ships the parent tree with the fix commit's regression test (parse_test.go case 'dependency line contains only operators' and testdata/operator-only-dep.yaml) overlaid exactly as the mining reproduction did, so the failing state is present from the first `go test` run; the fix commit itself is never reachable from /app/src (single shallow parent commit, golden bytes extracted via a throwaway clone that is deleted). The agent must reproduce, localise and fix in the real tree; the verifier asserts provenance (HEAD still the pinned parent, single commit, fix commit absent, only the conda environment parser source modified, nothing deleted, regression test and fixture byte-identical to the golden copies), runs the project's own conda parser test scope (environment + meta packages, the upstream regression test included), and runs two authored hidden cases with operator-only dependency lines the upstream test does not use ('===', '===' interspersed entries, '= =' and ' = ' spacing forms, mixed pins) asserting exact parsed package lists. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping: parent fails with the mined panic, fix passes the whole conda parser scope. Review (v4 wave): issue re-confirmed from a fresh clone in a container on the base image (parent FAILs with 'index out of range [0] with length 0', fix f964fa2b PASSes, guard grep 0->1); hidden cases proven to panic at the parent without the golden test present; verifier hardened after a root-trial bypass was demonstrated (a stub /opt/go/bin/go that reported success earned reward 1 on the buggy tree): the go binary and the two golden regression files are now sha256-pinned in test.sh and asserted again at Dockerfile build, assume-unchanged/skip-worktree bits are cleared before a git-diff-based blob provenance check, and nothing may be staged; fake-go, assume-unchanged hiding and golden tampering are all rejected (reward 0), honest oracle still 1, nop still 0.

ballast-current.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on astral-sh/uv at parent commit 6353b242d2774244ae2c6b4be1b95c70f84e97ab (real upstream issue #19799, fixed by 48c4357fe2517cce464ffa040d75c92be6a7dc71). deserialize_cache_policy_len() guards the trailing cache-policy length with `bytes.len() < len_usize + 8`, but when the 8-byte trailer is 0xFF..FF, len_usize == usize::MAX and the +8 wraps to 7, so the guard never fires and the follow-up slicing panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' at cached_client.rs:967. The fix compares len_usize against the number of bytes before the trailer and returns the existing ArchiveRead error for malformed entries. The image clones uv SHALLOW at the parent, extracts the fix-era regression test (crates/uv-client/tests/it/cached_client.rs + the `mod cached_client;` wiring, both byte-pinned by sha256) into /opt/golden and copies it over tests/it, prebuilds the uv-client `it` test harness (cargo test -p uv-client --test it --no-run) so the agent's fix cycle is one incremental recompile (~10s at 1 CPU), and fails the build if the mined failing state (panic 'attempt to add with overflow', 0 passed; 1 failed; 26 filtered out) is absent. The fix commit is fetched only into a throwaway bare clone that is deleted, so it is never reachable from /app/src/.git; cargo is configured offline. Hidden cases: 4 authored overflow vectors that panic at the parent exactly like the golden test (trailers 0xF8FF..., 0xFEFF..., and 0xFF..FF with 3-byte and 8-byte payload prefixes; all must yield ArchiveRead instead) plus one authored round-trip case: a real on-disk cache entry produced by uv's own cache writer at this revision (7 msgpack payload bytes, 344-byte validated policy archive, LE trailer) that the reader must load intact -- this also catches a reader that errors on everything. Measured host: cold clean 1-CPU build of the it harness ~7 min, incremental ~4s; full offline it suite 26/26 (remote_metadata excluded: it needs files.pythonhosted.org); rustup channel 1.96.0 pinned by the repo's rust-toolchain.toml. DOMAIN: packaging-release; uv is not in specs/tb21_source_repositories.json.

ballast-deepwater.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on duckdb/duckdb at parent commit 8616efa9da9921b9111fe46373af7936a5d96d16 (real upstream issue #25084, fixed by b94555b59e58941bf42da1aeb8f3251850b85e8f). SubtractTimeOperator::Operation negates right.micros with no bounds check, so subtracting an interval whose microseconds component is INT64_MIN (e.g. INTERVAL '-4611686018427387904 microseconds -4611686018427387904 microseconds') from a TIME or TIMETZ value silently wraps (signed negation overflow) and returns a wrong time (07:59:05.224192 for 12:00:00) instead of raising an out-of-range error. Interval::Invert has the same unchecked negation for days/micros/months and is on the DATE/TIMESTAMP minus interval path. The image clones the repo at the parent, overlays the upstream regression test added by the fix commit (test/sql/types/test_interval_negation_overflow.test) into the tree so build/release/test/unittest 'test_interval_negation_overflow' fails exactly as mined, prebuilds the release engine + unittest runner so the agent's fix cycle is an incremental recompile/relink of two files, and keeps the fix commit unreachable. Agent must make the regression test pass and all interval/date/time subtraction correct, without naming fixed: verified both directions inside the task image (see report). Hidden cases: CLI-driven vectors the upstream test does not use - TIME '00:00:00' and '23:59:59.999999' minus the INT64_MIN-microseconds interval, TIMETZ '12:00:00+05:30' minus it, DATE/TIMESTAMP minus it (Interval::Invert path), DATE minus INTERVAL '-2147483648 days' (days == INT32_MIN), plus a normal-arithmetic sanity case; each asserts the exact 'Interval ... value out of range' Out of Range Error rather than a wrong value, and the sanity case asserts the arithmetic still produces the correct time.

ballast-drift.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in eslint/eslint (v4.3 family): rule `new-cap`, configured with the option that suppresses property-access checks (properties: false), still reports member calls whose name ends in 'UTC' (foo.UTC(), foo?.UTC(), a.Date.UTC(), foo().UTC(), foo["UTC"]()) because the rule's UTC special case (allow only Date.UTC) runs before the skipProperties branch of isCapAllowed, so skipProperties never shields member expressions whose callee name is 'UTC'. Agent gets the real repo checked out at the parent commit, a repro that exits 1, and the project's own RuleTester/mocha tooling; must localise the one function, reorder the branches so skipProperties short-circuits all MemberExpression callees, and keep Date.UTC exemption + bare-capitalised-call reporting intact. Verifier: provenance byte-check (only lib/rules/new-cap.js may differ from the pinned blob) + planted upstream regression test (the rule's own test file as of the fix commit: 97 cases incl. the three added valid cases) + 985-case selection of the project's existing rule/rule-tester tests + three authored hidden RuleTester cases (deeper member chains, computed access, semantics-preserved controls). Oracle applies an authored one-hunk patch.

ballast-fathom.notes: Real upstream git/git at the parent of fix 1366c78c (git-for-windows/git#2037). Agent must reproduce (git stash -u -- ':(glob)...' exits 1 with 'fatal: pathspec ... did not match any files', leaves untracked files), localise the defect in the real 2.21-era tree, and fix it so `git stash -u` with glob magic succeeds and stashes/removes the matched files. The upstream root cause: push_stash parses pathspecs without PATHSPEC_PREFIX_ORIGIN and add_pathspecs() pushes ps.items[i].match (parsed form, magic stripped) to the internal git add/diff/ls-files children, so the glob/prefix magic is lost. Fix = parse with PATHSPEC_PREFIX_ORIGIN and push ps.items[i].original. Verified both directions in the task image: parent tree -> golden t3905 reports 'not ok 26 - stash -u with globs' (direct repro exit 1, file left); repaired tree -> 26 ok (exit 0, file removed, stash pop restores). Hidden cases exercise the same code path with inputs the upstream test never uses: multiple root-level files with ':(glob)**/*.md', a subdirectory-cwd ':(glob)**/*.tmp' variant, and two magic pathspecs given to one stash -u command. Verifier rebuilds the tree (touch builtin/stash.c + make -j1), runs the golden fix-commit t3905 plus the tree's own t3903-stash.sh, runs the hidden cases, checks /app/diagnosis.md names builtin/stash.c, and asserts the fix commit object is absent from the agent repo (provenance).

ballast-foresheet.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on gohugoio/hugo at parent commit 5f0d88b8a3652bbee992f4cbba2b018527f16a15 (real upstream issue #15285, fixed by 24d5e42ffa33eebdf906c495713f0d2bae30c0cb). Three default-policy SSRF holes in config/security: (1) the IP-literal URL deny rule '! ^https?://\d+\.' is case-sensitive, so a mixed-case scheme (HTTP://127.0.0.1/) bypasses it; (2) CheckAllowedHTTPAddress gates only on netip IsGlobalUnicast()/IsPrivate(), so CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, 192.0.0.0/24, TEST-NET-1/2/3, 198.18.0.0/15, 240.0.0.0/4, 2001:db8::/32, 3fff::/20 and 2001:2::/48 all count as 'public'; (3) NAT64 prefixes (64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48) and IPv4-mapped forms are not unwrapped before classification. Fix: (?i) on the deny rule plus an isPublicAddr helper that unwraps NAT64 and denies the special ranges. Image: shallow clone at parent pinned with a 40-hex assert, golden regression test (the fixed securityConfig_test.go, sha 85e6b0f7...) extracted from the fix commit in a throwaway bare clone (deleted; fix commit never in /app/src), overlaid into the tree so `go test -vet=off ./config/security` fails exactly as mined (HTTP://127.0.0.1/ and 100.64.0.1:80 denied-cases get nil errors; TestToTOML also fails as cosmetic collateral at parent); go1.27.1 pinned per dependency_pins, module+build caches warmed as layers; no cgo/extended tags needed. Agent must localise in config/security and repair the default policy without touching test files; verifier asserts provenance (HEAD==parent, fix commit unreachable, porcelain exactly M config/security/securityConfig.go + M ..._test.go, golden hash) then runs golden filtered tests, gated full package, and three authored hidden cases (mixed-case schemes on loopback/private/CGNAT hosts plus public-host allowances; CGNAT/TEST-NET/benchmark/reserved/2001:2::/2001:db8 documented address-layer vecs; NAT64-embedded and IPv4-mapped private + special + public vecs, and a URL-text-vs-resolved-address cross-layer check) each of which fails at parent and passes at fix. Measured: golden filtered run ~7s cold; full package ~1s warm at 1 CPU.

ballast-hull.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in google/guava (v4.2 family): reusing an ImmutableSet.Builder created with an expected size to build additional sets hangs, or misreports elements, because review() shrinks the internal hash table without resetting maxRunBeforeFallback / expandTableThreshold. The observable symptom is an infinite loop in contains() on the freshly built set once the retained table packs 100% full; localisation requires reading the nested builder implementation inside the collection source, so the bug file is deliberately not named. Verifier: provenance (HEAD pinned, every tracked file except the single fixed source byte-identical to parent, no untracked files) + /app/summary.md + the project's own upstream regression test (testReuseBuilderReducingHashTableSizeWithPowerOfTwoTotalElements, extracted from the fix commit at build time into /opt/golden) run under a timeout via the project's JUnit3 harness + 12 of the project's own existing ImmutableSetTest methods + the direct reproduction + three authored hidden cases (different expected sizes, element counts/types and a three-build reuse) with different inputs than the upstream test. ballast-keel.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on librosa/librosa at parent commit a0d0374370183d93ad7a4a348da034ab5b3e1687 (real upstream issue #1945, fixed by 86d728a4fae31c5e80ef112f895c70af228d1637). librosa.note_to_hz passes **kwargs straight to note_to_midi, whose round_midi kwarg defaults to True, so a note spelled with a cents deviation such as 'C2-30' is silently quantized to the nearest equal-tempered semitone and note_to_hz('C2-30') returns exactly note_to_hz('C2') (65.40639132514966); the upstream fix adds a keyword-only round_midi: bool = False parameter to note_to_hz and forwards it, so the default call preserves the -30-cent deviation (64.2827486708685). The image clones the repo with only the parent commit in the object store (fix commit unreachable, rev-list --all --count == 1), installs the project editable so edits to /app/src are live, and extracts the upstream regression test tests/test_convert.py::test_note_to_hz_default from the fix commit into /opt/golden at build time. Hash of the golden (fix-commit) test file: 3b5b30a5adb54fb8ed39a86073d7ec906e0f8071497dd5db576591ceac5beb97. Verifier: provenance (HEAD==parent, fix commit absent, exactly one commit, only librosa/core/convert.py modified, import resolves to /app/src), then copies golden test over the tree and requires it to pass, runs the project's own tests/test_convert.py in full, and runs three authored hidden cases (deviated single notes across octaves/accidentals/flats, list-typed inputs mixing deviated and plain notes, and the round_midi=True legacy quantization path plus the default==round_midi=False identity); all hidden expectations computed from the independent formula 440*2**((midi-69)/12). Typical run: pytest on test_convert.py ~2s at 1 CPU. Verified env: numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, numba 0.67.0, python 3.12.13, setuptools 72 (setup.cfg-era project; newer setuptools dropped setup.cfg). pytest collection of the tree's test suite needs a pre-import of librosa.core.convert under lazy_loader>=0.4 ('No librosa.core attribute convert'), applied in both oracle and verifier.

ballast-longshore.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on matplotlib/matplotlib at parent commit 91d115ec161286b70da1447f53844b909247741f (real upstream issue #29532, fixed upstream by commit 05a66bb2a46a67d0bb716239ecafa681b2832ea3). ScalarFormatter.set_useOffset dispatches on `val in [True, False]`, which matches the numeric values 0 and 1 by value equality (1 == True), so set_useOffset(1) silently sets _useOffset=True and offset=0 instead of forcing a numeric offset of 1. The upstream fix is one line: `if isinstance(val, bool):`. The image clones the repo with only the parent commit in the object store (fix commit unreachable, rev-list --all --count == 1), builds and installs it editable with meson-python (freetype/harfbuzz/qhull vendored as meson subprojects, fetched at build time), and extracts the upstream regression tests TestScalarFormatter::test_set_use_offset_int and test_set_use_offset_bool (fix-commit lib/matplotlib/tests/test_ticker.py) into /opt/golden at build time, never into this tree. ballast-pilot.notes:

REVIEW (v4 wave, ballast-pilot): issue re-verified independently in a fresh container: reset --hard to parent a167389c reproduces ZeroDivisionError at ribes_score.py:57 (sentence_ribes empty hypothesis) and :119 (corpus_ribes empty), silent -1.0 for empty references and silent 0.0 for mismatched corpus; reset --hard to fix 06c0e2cc returns 0.0 for all three empty shapes and raises the mandated ValueError; the fix-commit regression test fails 4/6 at parent and passes 10/10 at fix; in-tree test_ribes.py stays 6/6 at both. /opt/golden/test_ribes.py byte-identical (sha be5c54fce...) to the fix-commit file. ballast-roadstead.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on python-poetry/poetry at parent commit b760721672011534ca3607d17e3bf61a4dc6ed90 (real upstream issue #10807, a.k.a. PR/fix commit 89aaee9d60cae20775d3c40e4f243f9945f718e1). `poetry debug resolve` builds each result row as a two-element list [name, version] and then, for any resolved package whose environment marker is not 'any' (e.g. a package restricted to certain platforms or a Python-version range), executes `row[2] = str(pkg.marker)` on a two-element list, which raises IndexError: list assignment index out of range right after printing 'Resolution results:'; the upstream fix is the one-token change to `row.append(str(pkg.marker))`. The image ships a probe (/app/probe_resolve.py) reproducing the crash, keeps the fix commit unreachable from /app/src (depth-1 init+fetch of the parent alone; golden test extracted from the fix commit at image build time into /opt/golden/), pins poetry-core to the exact lock ref b9663e42c808543377ae523611c4cfad68016f30 so `pip install -e .` cannot drift, and pre-installs the project venv at /opt/poetry-venv. ballast-rudder.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on python/mypy at parent commit 5bb72b788d5c031244f04f30f571f6fa199871ad (real upstream bug, issue python/mypy#21830, fixed upstream in 0221c8018430c27607ff5e41d3127bd48a3e6170). When the rvalue of a multiple-assignment statement (`a, b = f(...)`) is a call to an overloaded function and the assignment-target context makes mypy re-infer the callee's return type with a different overload selected, the re-inferred type is not always a fixed-length tuple. The code at the parent asserts `isinstance(reinferred_rvalue_type, TupleType)` unconditionally (mypy/checker.py in check_multi_assignment_from_tuple); when the context selects an overload whose return type is e.g. a homogeneous `tuple[Any, ...]` instance or a non-tuple, the assert fires and the whole type-check run aborts with 'INTERNAL ERROR' (exit 2, mypy/checker.py:4412 AssertionError), so the file under check gets no diagnostics at all. The upstream fix replaces the hard assert with a guarded `if isinstance(..., TupleType):` that keeps the originally inferred tuple in the fallthrough. Agent must reproduce, localise and fix the real tree; the verifier asserts provenance (HEAD still the pinned parent, exactly one commit reachable, fix commit not present in the working clone, only source files under mypy/ modified, nothing deleted, nothing under mypy/test or test-data touched), runs the user-visible repro (no INTERNAL ERROR, exit 1 with the real 'Incompatible types in assignment' diagnostic), copies in and runs the project's own regression test extracted from the fix commit into /opt/golden at image build time (testMultipleAssignmentWithOverloadReinferredAsHomogeneousTuple, testMultipleAssignmentWithOverloadReinferredAsNonTuple), runs a meaningful slice of the project's own existing checker suite from the tree to prove nothing else broke, and runs authored hidden cases exercising the same reinference path from inputs the upstream regression test does not use (method receivers, star/unpacked targets, non-tuple overload returns). Pure Python, offline; ~2s per CLI mypy run, single-digit seconds for the golden pytest run at 1 CPU in-image. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image before shipping.

capstan-anchorage.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on pytorch/vision at parent commit df421b423f714eb3ae22cab2b0e6e7a6f6bb29be (real upstream bug, issue #9357). torchvision.ops.masks_to_boxes computes torch.where(mask != 0) and then unconditionally calls torch.min/torch.max on the extracted coordinate tensors, so any mask with zero foreground pixels raises RuntimeError (min(): Expected reduction dim to be specified for input.numel() == 0) instead of yielding the degenerate [0,0,0,0] box; a batch mixing empty and non-empty masks crashes on the first empty mask. capstan-brackish.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on sharkdp/fd v10.4.2 (2026-era tree: rust 2024 edition, jiff time handling) at parent commit fb0426fed164c5fa9cd04b5e4aa8d8c375efa1d0 (real upstream bug, issue #2081). The fix (upstream 5becb9d52cb532c35b68421075e4d8ee8d6c77cd) replaces the addition with UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(...), which returns None and lets the value be rejected like any other unparseable date. The verifier asserts provenance (HEAD still the pinned parent, exactly one commit object, fix commit not reachable, only tracked source files under src/ modified, at least one such modification, nothing deleted, the embedded upstream regression test left byte-identical to the fix-commit golden copy extracted into /opt/golden at image build time), runs the golden test with the project's own cargo test runner, runs the full project test suite (unit + integration, both self-contained and offline), and runs three authored hidden CLI cases exercising inputs the upstream test does not use: --changed-before with @9223372036854775808, --changed-within with @18446744073709551614, and an in-range huge timestamp guard (@9223372036854775807 must keep working). capstan-current.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on syncthing/syncthing at parent commit 119d5e72efcf7d4c003664640ca0db6f472edfa4 (real upstream issue #10834, fixed by 703b185982e5cdcff26a119bfa932165d60bda19). replaceRawPath() in lib/upnp/upnp.go indexes p[0] without an empty-string guard, so a discovered IGD device whose control URL is a bare query string (e.g. '?control=...', empty path component) makes the program crash with 'panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0' during URL normalization; the fix adds 'p != "" &&' to the guard. capstan-deepwater.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in BurntSushi/ripgrep (v4.2 family), upstream issue #2990. Image clones the real repository SHALLOW at the parent commit ba23ced8178496263af013117b70c09ce39c18e5 with the bug present; the agent must localise and fix it in the real tree. Bug: globset's file_name() in crates/globset/src/pathutil.rs returns None whenever a path's last byte is '.', so the candidate basename (and, via basename, the extension) becomes the empty string for any file or directory whose name ends in a dot (e.g. a directory literally named 'asdf.' or a file 'foo.'). Glob matching strategies that compare against the candidate basename/ext (BasenameLiteral / Extension / RequiredExtension, i.e. globs whose final component is a literal ending in a dot, with no embedded slash so the '**/' prefix applies) then silently stop matching: a negation glob '-g !asdf./' excludes nothing (files under the trailing-dot directory still appear in --files and in search results) and an inclusion glob selects nothing. Fix (4df1298127695ed1e76937f16de1a0135677ccf5): only an empty path or a final component of exactly '..' has no file name; a trailing dot is a perfectly normal file name. Re-confirmed both directions in this author's own build: at the parent commit the reproduction (mkdir asdf asdf.; touch asdf/foo asdf./foo; rg --files -g '!asdf./') lists both files; with the one-file fix it lists only asdf/foo. Verifier: provenance (HEAD is the pinned parent, every tracked file except pathutil.rs byte-identical to the parent blobs, no untracked files, /app/summary.md non-empty) + rebuild of rg and the project's own test harness + the project's own upstream regression test r2990_trip_over_trailing_dot (extracted from the fix commit at image build time into /opt/golden, sha256 48708bd6aa3534e703a11b101de09a66794206ffc043be966abba3cfde07801e; never part of this task tree) + eight of the project's own existing glob integration tests (misc::glob, glob_negate, glob_case_insensitive, glob_case_sensitive, glob_always_case_insensitive, include_zero, include_zero_override, preprocessing_glob) + four static hidden CLI cases with fixture names (mubla., nxq., grxv.) that appear in NO agent-visible artifact and fail at the parent / pass at the fix: a negated literals-glob on a FILE named 'mubla.', an inclusion literals-glob selecting 'mubla.', a '**/'-prefixed negation against a nested trailing-dot directory 'nxq.', and a search-mode run -g '!grxv./' over a tree with a trailing-dot directory, plus four DYNAMIC hidden cases whose trailing-dot name is generated from $RANDOM at verifier time (same four shapes), so no fixed name can be hardcoded even by an agent that could read /tests. Oracle applies the authored one-file patch (a copy of the upstream diff). Toolchain: rustup 1.98.1 (same recipe as the sibling ripgrep #3180 task), reproduction observed both directions in the author's own build of the exact parent/fix commits; image smoke step fails the golden test at build time to prove the image ships the bug.

capstan-fathom.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on PyCQA/flake8 at parent commit d25cc10e382bcbd59cea47e0172f1e35cd3ee90d (real upstream issue #1372, fixed by 85c2be3b5291a73a2e737219c040019c14cf3eee, flake8 3.9.2 era). On Python 3.10+ the parser attaches end-position fields to the SyntaxError detail tuple; src/flake8/checker.py::FileChecker._extract_syntax_information assumed the old 4-element layout and read token[-1] (now an integer end-offset) as the physical line, then called .rstrip on it, so any file that failed to parse crashed with AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'rstrip' instead of reporting E999. The image clones the repo at the parent with a single-commit shallow fetch (fix commit unreachable), extracts the fix commit's tests/integration/test_checker.py into /opt/golden through a deleted throwaway bare clone, overlays it into the working tree exactly as the mining reproduction did, and the build end-to-end re-runs the regression test requiring the mined AttributeError. Repro/pass confirmed inside the image with era deps pyflakes 2.3.1 / pycodestyle 2.7.0 / mccabe 0.6.1 / pytest 6.2.5: at parent the golden test fails (1 failed, AttributeError at checker.py:463), at fix 1 passed; note the era CLI cannot start on 3.12 (importlib.metadata EntryPoints has no .get), so the task is driven purely through pytest/imports. Oracle applies the minimal upstream-equivalent fix (guard the adjustment block on len(token)==4 and read token[3]); verifier asserts provenance (HEAD, single commit, fix commit absent, golden file byte-identical, porcelain exactly checker.py + test_checker.py), runs the golden test plus a 135-test slice of the project's own suite, and 4 authored hidden cases: real 3.12 parse failures of multi-line modules ((5,20),(6,9),(5,9) crash at parent, exact positions at fix), six-element tuples with text=None or offset end-fields (crash at parent, exact positions at fix), the legacy 4-element layout ((3,8),(7,0),(1,3) unchanged), and TokenError/fallback branches ((4,12),(1,0) unchanged). Whole check <2s at 1 CPU on the host.

capstan-foresheet.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in Z3Prover/z3 (v4.2 family), upstream issue #10609, fix commit 384d2d881f544e0f3abfa21e0e3ebe6beb9821d7 (parent d1f10234c50a49ee1cc7d08c87a680daf430017c). Image clones the real repository SHALLOW at the parent commit with the bug present; the agent must localise and fix it in the real tree. Bug: fpa2bv_converter::mk_rem() computed a wrong IEEE 754 remainder for fp.rem whenever the divisor is subnormal: the dividend significand was widened by only max_exp_diff = 2^ebits - 3 bits, but a subnormal divisor can lower the normalized exponent such that the exponent difference x_exp + y_leading-zeros exceeds that width, so the high bits of the dividend are shifted out before the remainder computation and the bit-blasted result is wrong (for the pinned half-precision repro: -0.0, encoding #x8000, instead of the true remainder #x000a). With the pinned repro query answered via the check-sat-using (then fpa2bv simplify bit-blast smt) pipeline, the parent returns sat (operands fully pinned -> must be unsat). Fix (upstream): widen both significands by sig_ext_amount = max_exp_diff + sbits - 1, drive the zero-extension loop and the following bit-vector-width arithmetic from sig_ext_amount instead of max_exp_diff. Re-confirmed both directions in this author's own build of the exact commits with the same toolchain (g++ 13.3.0 + cmake 3.28.3 on ubuntu 24.04) and again inside this task's own image: parent build answers sat for the repro, fix build answers unsat; the project's own regression test added by the fix commit (src/test/fpa.cpp, extracted at image build time into /opt/golden, golden sha256 b5bed2720afa7cdbba4ad9ddc22ed68f03f84b758a1f9c9a5a8147d3530ddba9; never part of this task tree) fails with an assertion on the parent build and passes on the fix build; independent exact-rational IEEE-754 computation in Python matches the fixed solver on every probed operand pair. Verifier: provenance (HEAD is the pinned parent, every tracked file except src/ast/fpa/fpa2bv_converter.cpp byte-identical to the parent blobs, no untracked non-ignored files, /app/summary.md non-empty) + incremental rebuild from the warm image (shell binary and, after planting the golden file and the two one-line test-registration edits, the test-z3 harness) + the project's own regression test (test-z3 fpa) + the project's ENTIRE existing unit suite (test-z3 -a; at 1 CPU the whole suite runs in 34s) + three authored hidden SMT cases (half-precision operands with bit patterns, signs and expected encodings different from every visible case; each independently cross-checked by exact rational arithmetic; fail at parent with sat, pass at fix with unsat). Oracle applies the authored fix.patch (a copy of the upstream diff for fpa2bv_converter.cpp). Toolchain: apt g++ cmake make on bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (no dependency pins).

capstan-hull.documented_probe: Real upstream tree apache/commons-lang@9d1f110190081801754a8a0b447693ad2407a502 (parent of the upstream fix 10f4421456b891d5a426348511383f387c99f3e1 for issue #1769), shallow-fetched in the Dockerfile, detached at the parent so the fix commit is out of reach, with the offline Maven repository at /opt/m2repo warmed and the module compiled at build time. capstan-inlet.documented_probe: aquasecurity/trivy pinned at parent f06520353fc632e69eaf9d669ecdd785e770305a (shallow single-commit clone; the fix commit 3c6a1a2aca33893f231412a34d3dfddc4f64b456 is never fetched into /app/src and is provably absent from its object store). capstan-keel.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on astral-sh/uv at parent commit 64c73b115b544e8424a8c69f44131e21d66e629c (real upstream bug, issue #21261; fix fab2c0c0d2992217ff8768d11558f4b668d02501). Domain: packaging-release. `uv cache clean`/`uv cache prune` report the logical byte length of removed entries as the reclaimed space: hard-linked files (a surviving link elsewhere keeps the storage, so 0 bytes are freed) and sparse files (holes are charged as data) are both misreported, and nothing is printed when the reclaimed figure is 0. Agent must localise the bug in the real tree (Removal::add_file in crates/uv-cache/src/removal.rs uses metadata.len(); the cache_clean/cache_prune call sites gate the printed figure on the byte total), fix it so the CLI '(X)' suffix is blocks*512 when the file is the last hard link and 0 otherwise, and always print a figure when files/directories were removed. The upstream fix additionally RENAMED the internal accounting API (logical_bytes/physical_bytes -> coarse_bytes/fine_bytes, RemovalMode -> RemovalAccounting), so the extracted golden test crates/uv-cache/tests/removal.rs only compiles against a tree reproducing that rename; the verifier accepts EITHER the exact upstream-style rename (extracted golden) or a name-preserving functional fix (sed-translated golden variant, coarse_bytes->logical_bytes), and falls back between the two. The CLI-observable '(X)' suffix is the common oracle via three authored hidden end-to-end cases (retained hardlink -> 0B; mixed hardlink+regular -> 1.0MiB; sparse 512MiB -> tiny) that the upstream CLI tests do not use. Rust 1.98.0 pinned by in-tree rust-toolchain.toml; Cargo.lock committed. Full debug CLI build (~1 min at 64 cores in the Dockerfile, ~20-45 min at 1 CPU) is pre-warmed into the image so the agent's rebuild is incremental. Both directions verified inside the task image before shipping: parent reports (1.0MiB) for the retained-hardlink scenario, fixed tree reports (0B), golden crate tests 4/4 pass on the fixed tree.

capstan-longshore.notes:
Upstream-clone debugging task on duckdb/duckdb at parent commit 9c21294d984dfe9a1da5d055b5fce3e8a0d634b2 (real upstream issue #25299, fixed upstream by commit c306b47b18095823f22774a972e7cda1170f87a0). PreparedStatement::MissingValuesException in src/include/duckdb/main/prepared_statement.hpp collects the names of parameters not supplied to an EXECUTE into an identifier_set_t (std unordered_set) and joins them in hash-bucket iteration order, so the error 'Values were not provided for the following parameters: ...' lists names in an order unrelated to the statement (observed at parent: ee, cc, dd for a statement declaring aa,bb,cc,dd,ee and supplying aa,bb). The upstream fix collects (declaration-index, name) pairs and sorts by index before building the message; it touches the header only. The image clones the repo at the parent via git init + single shallow fetch so the fix commit is unreachable (rev-list --all --count == 1), overlays the fix-commit regression test (test/sql/prepared/prepared_named_param.test, sha 14da4c35...) into the tree so it fails inside the image with the mined symptom (the q03 block expects 'cc, dd, ee', the buggy engine prints 'ee, cc, dd'), and prebuilds the release engine + unittest runner with the pinned build recipe (cmake -G Ninja -B build/release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNITTESTS=1 -DEXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 -DBUILD_EXTENSIONS=core_functions; ninja -j24) so the agent's fix cycle is an incremental header recompile + relink (measured ~16 min at one CPU: 169 objects). Verified both directions inside the task image (see report): at parent the reproduction prints 'ee, cc, dd' and the golden test fails; after the fix it prints 'cc, dd, ee' and the golden test plus the whole test/sql/prepared/* suite (40 sqllogictest cases, 1651 assertions) pass. Hidden cases are CLI-driven inputs the upstream test does not use: 7-name fruit set with middle gaps, t1..t7 with two supply sets, an empty supply on x1..x7, repeated declaration names (b,a,c,b,...), a more-than-3 missing set (p1..p8), and an all-supplied success sanity check asserting the values come back in declaration order; six of the nine hidden queries provably fail at the parent binary (hash order) and all nine pass with the fix. The verifier asserts tree provenance (HEAD == parent, exactly one commit, fix commit absent, only the header fix and the byte-identical golden overlay differ from the pinned commit, /app/explanation.md present and on-topic), rebuilds with ninja -j1, requires the project's own unittest runner to pass the golden test and the prepared suite, requires the CLI reproduction to print the declared order, and runs the hidden cases with exact error-text assertions. Difficulty medium: the fix is a one-file header change but requires locating the message in a real C++ codebase, rebuilding, and reasoning about hash-vs-declaration order. Environment: bench-base:ubuntu-24.04, apt g++/gcc/make/cmake/ninja-build/python3/git, cpus=1, OMP numeric pins, no dependency pins beyond the image ({}).
Review hardening (capstan-longshore review): verifier now removes build/release/duckdb and build/release/test/unittest before its ninja rebuild and requires both to be ELF executables afterwards (kills wrapper/fake binaries that would let the checks pass with the bug still in the sources); verifier timeout_sec raised 1800 -> 3000 to cover the measured ~978s one-CPU incremental rebuild with 3x margin; instruction wording tightened: dropped the explicit 'hash representation' root-cause hint and fixed the duplicate-name promise to match the actually observable contract (supplying a repeated name satisfies every occurrence, so it is absent from the error).

capstan-mooring.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in eslint/eslint (v4.2/v4.3 family, upstream issue #21251, parent ad74a8dada..., fix 1e641c919fc...): the no-loss-of-precision rule reports literals written with a trailing decimal point and no fractional digits (e.g. `var x = 0.` is falsely flagged although 0, 0.0 and -0 are all accepted) because baseTenLosesPrecision feeds getRaw(node).toLowerCase() (which keeps the trailing '.') into convertNumberToScientificNotation, so '0.' normalizes to the empty coefficient and a literal that is exactly representable reports 'This number literal will lose precision at runtime.'. The upstream fix strips a single trailing '.' from rawNumber before normalizing; genuinely lossy trailing-dot literals (9007199254740993.) must still report. Agent gets the real repo at the parent commit, a repro (valid 'var x = 0.' / invalid 'var x = 9007199254740993.') that exits 1, and mocha + RuleTester; must localise the one function and change one line in the one source file. Verifier: provenance byte-check (only lib/rules/no-loss-of-precision.js may differ from the pinned blob) + planted upstream regression test (the rule's own test file as of the fix commit: 131 cases incl. valid 'var x = 0.' and invalid 'var x = 9007199254740993.') + a 8-file selection of the project's existing rule/rule-tester tests + three authored hidden RuleTester cases (trailing-dot literals in array/object/call/expression positions, unary-minus and numeric-separator forms, and still-lossy trailing-dot literals) whose inputs the upstream test does not use. Oracle applies an authored one-hunk patch (the one-line .replace fix). Review hardening (independent reviewer pass): node_modules (gitignored, hence invisible to the tracked-file scope check) is locked read-only in the image, a full-tree sha256 manifest is recorded at build time (/opt/node_modules.sha256) and replayed by the verifier, espree/mocha are version-pinned and their entrypoints additionally tripwired with embedded sha256 constants (a proved bypass that swapped a patched espree into node_modules to make every test pass with the rule untouched now fails with reward 0); /opt/golden, /app/repro.js and the hidden-case scripts are sha256-asserted before use; an inline copy of the repro is run so tampering /app/repro.js cannot satisfy step 4; git provenance checks run with GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1.

capstan-overtake.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on explosion/spaCy at parent commit f5d04868e1e66d0acd6417b1c8099bcd4068fff7 (real upstream issue #13876, fixed upstream by 94d6be8a9b1dbecc92820bd7996cd8c75e186320 with a one-line import move; that fix commit ships NO regression test, so the golden test here is authored from the reproduction and lives in /opt/golden, outside the agent tree). displacy.render(..., jupyter=True) imports the IPython display helper from the deprecated IPython.core.display path, which IPython>=9 removed, so every notebook-bound render call crashes with ImportError before reaching IPython. (editable; pure-Python edits are live without reinstalling), pins ipython==9.17.1 (the bug only reproduces on IPython>=9), plus pytest==9.1.1 and hypothesis==6.168.0 which spaCy's own tests/conftest.py requires. capstan-pilot.notes: Real upstream git/git (2.46 era) checked out at the parent of fix 8b426c8 (upstream_issue_ref ddiss/icyci#12). Agent must reproduce (git notes add -C <empty-blob> --allow-empty / -m "" / -F /dev/null with --allow-empty invokes the configured editor; with GIT_EDITOR=false it errors 'there was a problem with the editor' and exits 128 storing no note), localise the defect in the real 2.46 tree and fix it so contents supplied via -m/-F/-c/-C never open the editor and --allow-empty stores the empty note. Root cause: the editor decision in the notes add/append path was switched (by 90bc19b3ae, 2023) from 'was any -m/-F/-c/-C supplied' to a zero-length-buffer check (the d.given flag); the fix decides on d.msg_nr instead and removes the flag. Re-confirmed both directions in the task image: parent tree -> direct repro exits 128 with the editor error, and the golden fix-commit t3301-notes.sh reports 'not ok 149 - empty notes do not invoke the editor' with the other 148 tests ok; repaired tree -> direct repro exits 0 storing the empty blob note, golden t3301 fully ok (149 ok). Verifier rebuilds the tree (touch builtin/notes.c + make -j1), runs the golden fix-commit t3301-notes.sh in full (the project's own notes suite; the regression test postdates the checked-out tree) plus hidden cases, checks /app/diagnosis.md names builtin/notes.c, and asserts the fix commit object is absent from the agent repo (provenance, since the trial container has no network the fix cannot be fetched at trial time either). Hidden cases exercise the same code path from inputs the upstream test never uses: -C <empty-blob> --allow-empty on a tagged non-HEAD commit, -f overwrite of an existing non-empty note with -F /dev/null --allow-empty, and -m "" --allow-empty from a subdirectory cwd; all three use an editor script that records invocation and fails, proving the editor was literally never launched.

capstan-quay.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on gohugoio/hugo at parent commit a7b93e6564e6a4a7a3043b431e255ba716940408 (real upstream bug, issue #11406, fixed by 3a8aad6b190bb3d7cecc8ec6bc8379a01ec547cb). A page consisting only of front matter leaks the raw front matter (delimiters and keys) into output that prints {{ .RawContent }}, because hugolib/page.go only records the main-content byte offset when the parser has not reached end-of-input, so RawContent() falls back to slicing from offset 0. Go 1.27.1 pinned (tarball from go.dev), module cache and build cache warmed in the image so a 1-CPU offline trial recompiles incrementally in seconds (full warm pass measured ~3 min on 1 core). Verifier asserts provenance (HEAD still the pinned parent, fix commit unreachable, exactly one commit, only non-test source under hugolib/ modified and the test-harness helper integrationtest_builder.go untouched), runs the upstream regression test extracted from the fix commit into /opt/golden at image build time (fix-commit version of hugolib/page_test.go, TestPageRawContent), runs two authored hidden cases (TOML front matter in a section dir; long YAML block in a dated path) plus the probe, and re-runs 14 existing hermetic page/front-matter tests from page_test.go/frontmatter_test.go. Both directions re-confirmed inside the measurements: golden test + authored cases FAIL at parent and PASS with the fix applied. REVIEW (independent): re-verified both directions in a container on the task base image (golden FAIL at parent matches the mining observation byte for byte; PASS with the fix). Hardened tests/test.sh after demonstrating two full bypasses that scored 1 with the bug intact: a swapped /usr/local/go/bin/go that fakes PASS output, and a neutered integrationtest_builder.go hidden by `git update-index --assume-unchanged`. The verifier now binds sha256 of go, git, /opt/golden/page_test.go and /app/probe_test.go to constants, rejects assume-unchanged/skip-worktree index entries, and rewrites /logs/verifier/reward.txt unconditionally in the EXIT trap (pre-written reward file attack). capstan-reach.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in google/guava (v4.2 family), issue #3501: SlicedByteSource.slice() recurses into ByteSource.this.slice(offset+offset, min(length, maxLength)) with a negative length when the requested offset is past the current slice's length, tripping the public length>=0 precondition and throwing IllegalArgumentException ('length (-1) may not be negative') where the javadoc promises an empty source. Direct repro: ByteSource.concat().slice(0,3).slice(4,3) crashes at parent, prints 'no exception; isEmpty=true' at fix. Agent must reproduce (javac-only pipeline, no Maven, no network), localise (bug is in the private SlicedByteSource.slice inside guava/src/com/google/common/io/ByteSource.java, discovered, not named), and fix the mechanism (return ByteSource.empty() when maxLength <= 0). Verifier: provenance (HEAD == pinned parent, only the bug's source file may differ), /app/summary.md, full recompile of guava/src + guava-testlib/src, the project's own regression test testSlice_returnEmptySource planted from /opt/golden (extracted from fix commit 82b3e980 at build time) and run via a JUnit3 harness, the whole fixed-version ByteSourceTest class (project's own existing suite) run green, the direct reproduction, and three authored hidden cases with inputs the upstream test does not use (wrap() non-empty source, 3-level nesting, ByteStreams.readAll consumption). Oracle applies an authored two-line patch matching upstream's fix. Sibling android/guava copy allowed in scope but not required (never compiled).

chainplate-anchorage.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on matplotlib/matplotlib at parent commit 74c7f9a598c4e32b3f551f75ed965f446d786ab1 (real upstream issue #28383, fixed upstream by commit 00cbd9cd3255dcbcb75e3090b144a8e18a900247). Transform.contains_branch_seperately documents a per-axis containment answer (pair of booleans), but CompositeGenericTransform has no override and falls back to the base Transform implementation, which returns [contains_branch(other)] * 2 — a two-element list whose entries are BOTH the whole-composite answer, so a composite whose right-hand side is a blended (per-axis) transform reports (False, False) even when the y branch genuinely contains the other transform; upstream's axes limit-tracking code (e.g. axvspan in non-rectilinear cases and fill_between with a custom transform) then skips limit updates. The upstream fix (2 hunks in lib/matplotlib/transforms.py): add a contains_branch_seperately override to CompositeGenericTransform (identity shortcut (True, True) + delegation to self._b) and change the base class return from a list to a tuple. The image clones the repo with only the parent commit in the object store (fix commit unreachable, rev-list --all --count == 1), builds and installs it editable with meson-python (freetype/harfbuzz/qhull vendored as meson subprojects, fetched at build time), and extracts the upstream regression test (fix-commit lib/matplotlib/tests/test_transforms.py, containing the added assertions in TestBasicTransform::test_contains_branch) into /opt/golden at build time, never into this tree. Dependency pins identical to sibling matplotlib task ballast-longshore: pyparsing 3.1.4 (must stay < 3.2.0: matplotlib's pytest config turns warnings into errors and pyparsing 3.2.0's resetCache deprecation otherwise aborts collection), pytest 8.4.2, numpy 2.5.3, pybind11 3.1.0, meson-python 0.16.0, meson 1.12.0, ninja 1.13.2, contourpy 1.3.3, kiwisolver 1.5.1, cycler 0.12.1, fonttools 4.65.0, packaging 26.3, certifi 2026.7.22, pillow 12.3.0, python-dateutil 2.9.0.post0, setuptools-scm 10.2.3, setuptools 84.0.0. Verifier: tree provenance (HEAD==parent, fix commit absent, exactly one commit, byte-level equality of every tracked file except lib/matplotlib/transforms.py against the parent blobs, no untracked non-ignored files), imports matplotlib from /app/src, copies the golden test file over the tree and requires TestBasicTransform::test_contains_branch to pass (fails on the parent tree: assert y is sy is True with sy False), runs a subset of the project's own existing TestBasicTransform node ids (test_transform_depth, test_left_to_right_iteration, test_transform_shortcuts, test_affine_simplification, and the identity/equality checks in test_contains_branch's unchanged portion via TestBasicTransform::test_transform_depth etc.) to prove nothing else broke, runs the issue reproduction, and runs three authored hidden cases with inputs the upstream test never uses: an x-axis mirror of the blended containment (x contained, y not), deep composite nesting two levels deep with identity (self-containment -> (True, True)) and all-contained / none-contained matrix, and the return-type contract for plain affine/non-affine/identity transforms (must be a 2-tuple of real bools, never a list). The hidden cases fail against the parent tree and pass only with the upstream two-part fix. Typical trial runtime: pytest ~15-30s at 1 CPU, no image comparisons involved. Verified env: python 3.12.13, bench-base:python-3.12.

chainplate-berm.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in netty/netty (v4.2 family, real repository, shallow clone of pinned parent commit 87d2f750, JDK 21 + maven 3.8.7, warm /opt/m2, fully offline trial). The bug: JdkZlibDecompressor sizes every output buffer from the number of input bytes still unread (inflater.getRemaining() << 1); for highly compressible raw-deflate streams the inflater pulls the final input bytes into its internal state while a large run of decoded output is still pending, getRemaining() hits zero, the decompressor reports NEED_INPUT and endOfInput() then rejects the complete stream with 'Compressed stream ended before the end-of-stream marker', silently dropping the tail. Upstream issue #17191, fixed by commit 7681affc (min 512-byte output buffer + inflaterHasPendingOutput state tracked in status()). The project's own regression test (testHighlyCompressibleStreamIsFullyDecompressed) was added with the fix and is extracted into /opt/golden at image build time, never committed to the task tree. Both directions observed inside the task image at build time: parent fails on the NONE-wrapped run of the planted regression test with the 'End of stream marker not found' style DecompressionException (BUILD FAILURE); the fixed tree passes the whole parameterized class offline. Agent must reproduce via the public Decompressor/JdkZlibDecompressor API, localise the sizing/state logic, make the smallest source change, and verify through the project's own Maven tooling. Verifier: working-tree provenance (HEAD pinned; every tracked file except the single JdkZlibDecompressor source file byte-identical to the parent blobs; no untracked non-ignored files), /app/summary.md, the planted upstream regression test run together with six authored hidden cases (250k/500k byte streams of other repeated bytes, chunked input feeding in 128- and 7-byte chunks, and ZLIB_OR_NONE wrapper resolving to raw deflate -- all inputs the upstream test does not use) plus the project's own JdkZlibTest/ByteBufChecksumTest/DefensiveDecompressorTest/InputBufferingDecompressorTest staying green. Binary reward on every exit path.

chainplate-bollard.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on networkx/networkx at parent commit 5d160909eeb42e9844496dd2bbd19b826d2242d7 (real upstream bug, issue #8584 / PR fix 46a639aeb9bd4db8da444bd6a532df567b9a73cc). nx.SpanningTreeIterator advertises itself as an iterator but initialises its internal partition priority queue only inside __iter__; calling next() directly without iter() (both spellings are legal per the protocol) raises AttributeError: partition_queue on the first call, so the first spanning tree is unobtainable. The fix moves the one-time initialisation into __next__ behind a lazy 'if self.partition_queue is None' guard (partition_queue is pre-set to None in __init__) and keeps the StopIteration + cleanup behaviour. The pre-existing mst test file is fully green at the parent (all its iterator tests go through for loops) so the agent must reproduce with the given one-liner, read mst.py's iterator class, and reason about the protocol contract. Verifier: provenance (HEAD == parent, fix commit unreachable from the clone, every tracked file except networkx/algorithms/tree/mst.py byte-identical to parent blobs, no untracked files) + /app/summary.md + module-origin check + golden regression test extracted from the fix commit (digest-checked) planted over test_mst.py with the whole file green + three authored hidden cases (cycle_graph(4) exhausted via direct next() counted against Kirchhoff, weighted wheel_graph(6) in min and max directions, MultiGraph input). Pure Python, no numpy/scipy, no network; whole suite ~0.3s at 1 CPU. Both directions verified inside the task image before shipping: golden 1 failed at parent / 1 passed at fix, hidden cases exit 1 at parent / 0 at fix.

chainplate-boom.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on nltk/nltk at parent commit 52227d2afe764648864e59c851e991cf1d6cb77e (real upstream bug, closed by #3693; fixed upstream in 27b8ad6cd50a484590cb9409e5d2a891ab56e16c). chomsky_normal_form binarizes any node with more than two children by reading a label from every child; a plain terminal among the children (a word, punctuation such as '+', or a non-string value such as the integer 7) has no .label() and raises AttributeError at nltk/tree/transforms.py:148. chainplate-brackish.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in pylint-dev/pylint (v4.2 family): false-positive protected-access (W0212) when a protected member is read through self.__class__ inside an instance method; the same read via type(self) is already accepted. The agent must find the emitting check (visit_attribute path in the classes checker), understand that self.__class__ is the class of the method's first parameter, and add a guard so only accesses through another object's class still warn.
