chainplate-caboose.notes: Upstream-clone debugging/security task on pypa/setuptools at parent commit bb1b38189eed960bdb4f4789926472d05e43d335 (security advisory GHSA-grgh-hr87-3jpw, fixed by 72974110e29d53080dcf23cfa52d9c17299dbae4). unpack_archive()'s path-traversal guard splits member names on '/' alone, so archive members whose names use '\' instead of '/' (or carry a drive letter or UNC prefix) slip past the '..' check and are extracted: on Windows they resolve outside the extraction directory, on Linux they land as surprising literal backslash names. The fix funnels both tar and zip drivers through one _resolve_dest() helper that rejects backslash/drive/UNC names and, as defense in depth, verifies via os.path.commonpath that the resolved destination is inside the extraction directory; unsafe members are skipped, safe ones still extracted. The image clones the repo at the parent, overlays the project's own regression tests extracted from the FIX commit into setuptools/tests/test_archive_util.py so `python3 -m pytest -q setuptools/tests/test_archive_util.py` fails inside the image exactly as mined (7 failed, 7 passed, 1 xpassed), keeps the fix commit unreachable from /app/src, and installs the stdlib `test` package (CPython 3.12.13 Lib/test) the project's test collection needs via .compat.py39. Agent must localise in setuptools/archive_util.py and fix it. Hidden cases are authored vectors with archive member names the upstream regression tests do not use: a zip with UNC ('\\server\share\evil.txt'), drive-letter-plus-backslash ('C:\windows\evil.txt') and bare drive ('D:evil.txt') members; a tar with deep '..' chains mixed with backslash-relative members plus nested safe directories; and a zip mixing valid exotic names (spaces, non-ASCII, deep nesting) with backslash-relative escapes to prove safe members still extract while unsafe ones are skipped; at parent all three fail (unsafe members leaked into dest), at fix all pass with byte-exact safe content.

chainplate-chartroom.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on python-poetry/poetry at parent commit e54180064368c2f9d9ad5ff4771d8b33538cc372 (real upstream issue #10808, fixed by e6f1ded9902d1fa17fc74e6562cb423e84fa7752). Config.process() resolves {dotted.config.key} templates inside string config values by looking up the referenced key and substituting its value, but guards the substitution with `if config_value:`, so falsy referenced values (int 0, False, empty string) are treated as unset and the placeholder is returned literally; the fix checks `if config_value is not None` and substitutes str(config_value). The image clones the repo at the parent with no git remotes, overlays the fix commit's tests/config/test_config.py byte-for-byte (sha256 3f93019026b8546d337b53ba2dd264ff145dec187196d66b23d54d728f16359a), keeps the fix commit unreachable (extracted via a deleted throwaway bare clone), and installs the project editable into /opt/poetry-venv with all deps pinned at the versions resolvable on bench-base:python-3.12. Agent must reproduce, localise and fix in the real tree: the failing golden case asserts config.process('{requests.max-retries}') == '0' where the default config holds max-retries=0. Hidden cases: (a) falsy booleans (installer.parallel=False, virtualenvs.options.always-copy=False) and a zero int (installer.max-workers=0) plus a zero injected through the POETRY_INSTALLER_MAX_WORKERS environment route, and a surrounding-text template; (b) empty-string values (installer.no-binary='', cache-dir=''). Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image: parent gives '1 failed, 82 deselected' with the mined AssertionError at tests/config/test_config.py:61; fix gives golden 1 passed and the whole tests/config dir 102 passed in ~0.6s. Build measured at ~4.5 min cold on the host (venv install of ~30 pinned deps dominates); image ~2.2 GB. deepdiff is required at collection of the config tests and is installed.

chainplate-current.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on python/mypy at parent commit 1730c9535e464be8a1eee4d74f74156d75a6c0b2 (real upstream issue #21428, fixed by 3f0c355b7b5fbce50fc192a697bbe4f214e01253). With --allow-redefinition on, a module-level unannotated empty-list assignment (a partial type) combined with a function that names the variable in a `global` declaration makes the TypeChecker crash with INTERNAL ERROR (exit 2): visit_global_decl unconditionally calls self.binder.assign_type(n, sym.node.type, sym.node.type) with sym.node.type still a PartialType, and the binder's is_subtype path asserts on the partial type ('Unexpectedly encountered partial type'); the fix guards with typ = get_declaration(n); if typ is not None, which is None exactly for partial types. Verified in-image both directions: parent gives 'INTERNAL ERROR' exit 2 on the CLI repro and 1 failed golden test; fix gives exit 1 with 'Need type annotation for "x" (hint: "x: list[<type>] = ...")' and 1 passed golden test; full mypy/test/testcheck.py suite 8018 passed / 26 skipped / 7 xfailed in ~234s at 1 CPU after the fix. The image clones the repo at the parent (fix commit unreachable, asserted at build), overlays the fix commit's test-data/unit/check-inference.test so the regression case exists and fails as mined, and pins the project's own shipped dependency versions (typing_extensions 4.15.0, mypy-extensions 1.1.0, pathspec 1.0.0, librt 0.10.0, ast-serialize 0.3.0, pytest 8.4.2, pytest-xdist 3.8.0, lxml 6.0.2). CAVEAT verified: sibling case ...Redefine1 (no global declaration, added by the same fix commit) passes at BOTH parent and fix, so only Redefine2 is an oracle. Hidden cases (each crashes with INTERNAL ERROR at parent, clean need-annotation output at fix): global x, y with list+dict partials and a method call on x; dict partial with subscript assignment after global; nested function declaring global x with a bare use. All pytest invocations clear mypy's -nauto addopts with -o addopts="" so xdist cannot fan out inside the one-CPU container.

chainplate-deepwater.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on pytorch/vision at parent commit 6940e19087cecb5108370703e207f7a33d9b478d (real upstream bug, issue #8887, fixed upstream in 74d128539ddf17c58a955468abe85e062c293ed9). torchvision.transforms.v2.functional._meta._cxcywh_to_xyxy computes half-extents on integer tensors with div(-2, rounding_mode='floor'), which rounds the half of an odd dimension up (away from zero), so an int64 CXCYWH box whose height is odd converts to XYXY with y1 = -1 even though the box lies inside the canvas; the float path and torchvision.ops._box_convert._box_cxcywh_to_xyxy (true division + truncation back to the integer dtype) are correct. Agent must reproduce via the public convert_bounding_box_format API with the pinned torch 2.10.0+cpu / torchvision 0.25.0+cpu venv (whose transforms/v2/functional modules are overlaid from the checkout), localise the integer-division rounding in the real tree, fix it (float arithmetic then cast back), reflect the fix into the installed package, prove it with the project's own pytest and the upstream regression test (extracted from the fix commit into /opt/golden, never committed), and write /app/summary.md. Both directions re-confirmed inside the task image at build time: golden test + direct repro fail at parent (y1=-1) and pass at fix ([[0,0,10,12]]). Verifier: HEAD pin, working-tree provenance (every tracked file except the single fixed _meta.py byte-identical to parent blobs, no untracked non-ignored files), venv mirrors the fixed source file, golden upstream regression test plus the project's own TestConvertBoundingBoxFormat class (reference-compared against torchvision.ops.box_convert) stay green, and four authored hidden cases the upstream test does not use (odd width, odd width+height in a batch, inplace=True on int tensors, float/int16/int32 dtype preservation and ops-equivalence). Binary reward on every exit path.

chainplate-drift.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on scikit-image/scikit-image at parent commit fff7deabe28fb6039c26588f751e9cad88354f19 (real upstream issue #7648, fixed by 96834cf3d57c4a9bad82a471a5548be3ad53a4fa). EllipseModel.estimate() (skimage/measure/fit.py) has no minimum-points check: with 4 arbitrary points it returns True and fabricates meaningless parameters (the five ellipse parameters xc, yc, a, b, theta are underdetermined by 4 points), and with 3 collinear points it returns False with no warning (silent failure). The upstream fix adds 'if len(data) < 5: warn("Need at least 5 data points to estimate an ellipse.", RuntimeWarning); return False' at the top of estimate(). The image clones the repo with only the parent commit in the object store (fix commit unreachable, rev-list --all --count == 1), installs the project editable with meson-python (numpy==2.1.3, scipy==1.14.1, Cython==3.0.12, meson-python==0.16.0, pythran==0.16.0, python 3.12.13) so edits to /app/src are live, and extracts the upstream regression test skimage/measure/tests/test_fit.py::test_ellipse_model_estimate_failers from the fix commit into /opt/golden at build time. Hash of the golden (fix-commit) test file: 5a8c9222b5ff03a5d4d28a4a80b7b77795ba9a6b2b403f1e342f70c3bcae904a. The Dockerfile smoke re-confirms BOTH directions inside the image: at parent the 4-point repro prints True and the golden test fails with 'DID NOT WARN'; after applying the guard the repro prints False with the RuntimeWarning and the golden test passes, together with the project's own -k 'ellipse or circle' subset of test_fit.py. Verifier: provenance (HEAD == parent, fix commit object absent, exactly one commit, the only modified tracked file is skimage/measure/fit.py, no tracked test doctored, import skimage resolves to /app/src/skimage), runs the golden (fix-era) test_fit.py::test_ellipse_model_estimate_failers and then the whole golden test_fit.py (30 tests, the project's own estimator suite) against the agent's repaired tree, and runs three authored hidden cases the upstream test does not use: 4 arbitrary non-degenerate points (fabricated-fit vector, asserts False + exact warning + params stays None), 3 collinear points plus 2- and 1-point inputs (silent-failure vector, asserts the exact warning is the only diagnostic), and a genuine 5-point ellipse that must still fit True with the true parameters and near-zero residuals (guard against over-fixing; expectations computed from the independent parametric ellipse formula, not from predict_xy). The checked-out test_fit.py is deliberately NOT used for the suite proof: its test_ellipse_model_estimate_failers still asserts the pre-fix contract, so under the project's pytest filterwarnings=[error] config a correct fix makes exactly that outdated test fail (upstream updated it in the same commit). All hidden expectations and the exact warning text were verified standalone (without building skimage) and again inside the built image, in both directions.

chainplate-ebb.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on scipy/scipy at parent commit 68942fb357ee133e75709e91959d322325fffb90 (real upstream issue #25880, fixed upstream by commit b92b297a5a0c372600bffffd4dc83513be9bfd39 with a 2-line change to scipy/optimize/_minimize.py: `import copy` and `bounds = copy.copy(bounds)` in `_validate_bounds`, which had been broadcasting lb/ub onto the caller's Bounds object in place). The bug: minimize() silently rewrites a caller's dimension-agnostic Bounds object built from scalar limits - the scalar lb/ub are replaced with np.broadcast_to arrays sized to the current problem, so a Bounds reused across problem sizes is corrupted from the second call onward and inspection afterwards shows data the caller never assigned. Image: shallow clone with only the parent commit in the object store (fix commit unreachable; rev-list --all --count == 1), meson submodules (array_api_compat, array_api_extra, cobyqa, HiGHs, unuran, xsf, boost_math, scipy-mathjax) fetched at build time at the parent-pinned SHAs, full scipy 2.0.0.dev0 source build + `pip install --no-build-isolation -e .` (system libopenblas-dev provides BLAS/LAPACK; build toolchain pinned: numpy 2.5.3, meson-python 0.21.1, meson 1.12.0, ninja 1.13.2, Cython 3.3.0, pybind11 3.1.0, pythran 0.19.0, setuptools 84.0.0, pytest 9.1.1; OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/NUMEXPR threads pinned to 1). The golden regression file (fix-commit scipy/optimize/tests/test_optimize.py, containing test_minimize_does_not_mutate_bounds parametrized over 8 methods and test_minimize_bounds_reusable_across_sizes) is extracted from the fix commit at build time into /opt/golden, never into this tree. Verifier: tree provenance (HEAD == parent, fix commit absent, exactly one commit, every tracked file except scipy/optimize/_minimize.py byte-identical to the parent blobs - gitlink submodule entries skipped - no untracked non-ignored files, import scipy resolves to /app/src), the project's own existing tests (test_bounds_with_list, test_all_bounds_equal, test_all_bounds_equal_writable, test_minimize_maxiter_noninteger), the golden regression node ids run against the agent's tree, the exact issue reproduction, three authored hidden cases with inputs the upstream test never uses (reuse across sizes with l-bfgs-b, five methods with keep_feasible plus scalar-state shape checks, a mixed three-call sequence across methods/sizes ending with value+shape assertions), and the /app/explanation.md deliverable. Hidden cases fail on the parent tree (identity asserts raise or the second call raises ValueError on stale broadcast shapes) and pass only with the fix. Both directions were re-confirmed inside the task image (see report). Typical verifier runtime: pytest collection of test_optimize.py ~20-40s at 1 CPU plus the quick node ids. Verified env: python 3.12.13 on Debian trixie, bench-base:python-3.12.

chainplate-fathom.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on semgrep/semgrep at parent commit a8b650dffe910d7b8903fe05ceeb75fdc7983197 (real upstream issue #9849, fixed by e3062fc251448ffcf16a38245e5e6a8dca894df5). get_project_url() returns git ls-remote --get-url verbatim, so when GitLab CI injects a job-token remote URL (https://gitlab-ci-token:glcbt-...@host/...), the whole token is copied into published rule metadata; the upstream fix routes get_project_url() through a new clean_project_url() (urlsplit + re.sub stripping the user:pass@ part of netloc). The image clones the repo with ONLY the parent commit in the object store (fix commit unreachable, rev-list --all --count == 1), checks out the cli/src/semgrep/semgrep_interfaces submodule, installs the CLI editable so edits to /app/src are live, and extracts the upstream regression test cli/tests/unit/test_clean_project_url.py::test_git_url_clean from the fix commit into /opt/golden at build time (sha256 7d1f46c1e26081e0c2655ecc9e1de6f8ad8c7f475f87922f512603715aa87e8b). Build-time smoke asserts the mined failing state: get_project_url() still leaks the token and the golden test cannot collect (ImportError: cannot import name clean_project_url). All hidden expectations computed from the upstream implementation's exact behavior (regex ^.*:.*@(.+) on urlsplit netloc). chainplate-foresheet.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on sharkdp/fd at parent commit 7027d45303b412be6fa9c09d689cc6276748fb38 (fd v10.4.2), real upstream bug (issue #1900), fixed upstream at d3a500af7aee3a9f099b09e1831da3fc39980c61. When the working directory a search was launched from is removed mid-search, fd --full-path calls env::current_dir() (through filesystem::path_absolute_form) for every matched entry; after the cwd is unlinked, getcwd returns NotFound and the `.expect("Retrieving absolute path succeeds")` at src/walk.rs:528-529 panics the whole process (exit 101) instead of finishing, skipping or reporting. The upstream fix adds WorkerResult::FatalError, extracts search_str_for_entry() returning io::Result, and propagates fatal errors through the receiver loop (streaming), the exec job loop (src/exec/job.rs) and the batch path, returning ExitCode::GeneralError, plus the regression unit test full_path_search_returns_error_for_invalid_cwd (which deletes the cwd and asserts the helper errors). The regression test only exists at the fix commit and references the new helper, so the parent-side demonstration is the CLI repro (timing-controlled: fd walks a >=120k-file tree through a symlink in a cwd that is deleted ~0.2s in; reproduced 3/3 at parent in the mining phase and 6/6 in the 1-CPU trial container and re-confirmed inside this task image). The verifier asserts provenance (HEAD pinned parent, exactly one commit object, fix commit not reachable, only tracked source files under src/ modified with at least one modification, nothing deleted, no new files under src/), builds the tree, runs the golden test when the tree accepts it (upstream-shaped fix) or relies on the CLI hidden cases (all three fix handler arms: default streaming receiver loop, -x single-command job loop, -X batch path, each asserting exit 1, no panic, and the engaged '[fd error]: ... No such file or directory' message under --show-errors), runs the project's full unit+integration suite (skipping the 1-CPU timing-sensitive test_exec_nulls, same as sibling fd task capstan-brackish), and three authored hidden CLI cases from inputs the upstream test does not use. Toolchain pinned rust 1.98.1 via rustup; Cargo.lock committed upstream pins every crate (tempfile 3.24 already a dev-dependency); full dep graph prebuilt in the Dockerfile (cargo build + cargo test --no-run) so trial builds are incremental; CARGO_NETWORK=off. Both directions re-confirmed inside this task's own image (parent: CLI panic exit 101; fix: golden unit test passes and CLI exits 1 without panic) and again by the oracle run (solution applies the upstream two-file fix via git apply and rebuilds).

chainplate-hull.notes: Upstream-clone bugfix in starship/starship (v4.2 family): an empty prompt format textgroup such as [](bg:#9A348E) is dropped entirely at parse time, so it can never establish the style that a later segment references through prev_fg/prev_bg; [](bg:red)[X](bg:prev_bg) renders a plain 'X' with no background. chainplate-inlet.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on statsmodels/statsmodels at parent commit 3c102982fecc91782d7836b9ae456fe869dd3578 (real upstream bug #9805, fixed by 0a347973915a2a28ec795cb670343c37ab3d0d92). chainplate-keel.notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on syncthing/syncthing at parent commit ee275fee65b37ea75802c8fc3c9decd5a66cb065 (real upstream issue #10743, fixed by f1d631d66e1c3101a8968e0713fac29e67329134, minimal 8-line change). checkFileInfoConsistency() in lib/protocol/protocol.go rejected ANY non-file entry with nonzero Size ('non-file type with nonzero size'), but scanning nodes of other Syncthing versions stamp directories with the fixed SyntheticDirectorySize constant (128), so the receiving node's consistency checker flagged those directory index entries as invalid protocol data and mixed-version synchronization of directory entries broke. The fix splits the check: directories may carry size 0 or SyntheticDirectorySize; symlinks stay size 0. The image clones the repo shallow at the parent, overlays the fix commit's lib/protocol/protocol_test.go (which adds six table cases to TestCheckConsistency: directory 0/synthetic/42 and symlink 0/synthetic/42) exactly as the mining reproduction did, keeps the fix commit unreachable (throwaway bare clone), and pre-warms the Go module cache and test-build so the agent's cycle is a one-file incremental recompile. Agent must localise in lib/protocol and let directory entries with the synthetic size pass while keeping size-0 directories and symlinks valid and all other rejections intact. Hidden cases: two authored Go test files driving checkFileInfoConsistency with inputs the upstream test does not use (nested directory name with synthetic size + mtime/permissions; deleted directory with synthetic size; directory at synthetic-1 and at 1 MiB; symlink with multi-component target at size 0; symlink at size 1 and at synthetic-1). Whole ./lib/protocol/ package suite passes after the fix, ~1-2 min total incremental rebuild at 1 CPU, first clone+module fetch at build time only.
